clause: Restricted Employees, Directors and their Associates are prohibited from engaging in Short Selling, Short-term Trading, margin lending, and from granting any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.
why_it_matters: The Key Principles restate the ban without even the word 'lenders', so on the policy's own summary a written call option granted over the shares to the bank is at risk of being read as a prohibited grant of rights, not merely the security interest.

clause: Security Trading covered by this Policy includes: ... creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to Securities;
why_it_matters: Every element of a funded collar, the put, the call, the charge and the loan, is separately a Trade requiring written pre-clearance and falling outside Blackout Periods, so there is no argument that only the share sale is regulated.

topic: restricted shares included in hedging ban
clause: prohibited from: hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights; and entering into a derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights granted under these plans.
why_it_matters: Only shares that are both vested and free of plan restrictions can be collared, so the collar pool must be carefully identified against the plan records.

clause: Any Trading that is the subject of pre-clearance must be executed within three business days of the receipt of the written pre-clearance (unless the pre-clearance is withdrawn).
why_it_matters: The whole structure would have to be priced, documented and executed inside three business days of clearance, and the clearance can be withdrawn in the meantime.

clause: Any pre-clearance to Trade can be given, withdrawn, refused or made subject to conditions by the applicable approver in their absolute discretion and without giving reasons. If pre-clearance is withdrawn or refused, the person seeking the pre-clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on obtaining or keeping clearance, and the executive may be barred from explaining to the bank why a trade cannot proceed.

clause: An application for pre-clearance to Trade in The Lottery Corporation Securities may be refused where the applicant is not, or as a result of the proposed Trading will not be, in compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy.
why_it_matters: Even the derivative legs can be refused if the collar would leave the director or executive short of the minimum shareholding, so the collared parcel should sit above that requirement.

clause: The Continuous Disclosure Committee may also, from time to time without prior notice, and conditionally or unconditionally, extend, reduce, or create an additional Blackout Period. ... The Board or Chairman may also, from time to time, at their absolute discretion, and without prior notice, impose ad hoc restrictions.
why_it_matters: Unannounced blackouts can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and the executive bears that timing risk.

clause: Short-term Trading (Trading within six months of the acquisition) of The Lottery Corporation Securities
why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any early unwind must sit beyond six months from the acquisition of the underlying shares, or fall within the narrow exceptional circumstances relief.

clause: Associates means any person or entity which might in the circumstances be reasonably associated with The Lottery Corporation or any of its Directors or Team Members (such as spouses, partners, dependent children, family trusts, family companies, joint venture partners).
why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a family trust, family company or self-managed superannuation fund does not escape the security interest ban or the pre-clearance regime.

clause: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement. You must ensure any portfolio of Covered Securities provided as collateral does not comprise ASX Group Securities.
why_it_matters: This defeats the secured loan leg of a funded collar outright, including the technique of pledging a diversified portfolio that happens to contain ASX shares.

topic: financing terms must not allow out-of-window sales
clause: You must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the terms of your margin loan or financing arrangement does not require, nor allow for, ASX Group Securities to be disposed of at such time that would breach this Policy, such as outside of a designated ASX Trading Window.
why_it_matters: Even a lawful financing arrangement must be documented so that the lender has no right to sell ASX shares outside a Trading Window, which rules out ordinary bank enforcement and margin-call mechanics.

topic: hedging vested shares is permitted but disclosable
clause: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. This may be publicly disclosed.
why_it_matters: The unfunded collar over vested, unlocked shares is permitted, but the executive must accept notification and possible public disclosure of the position.

topic: holding lock extends the hedging ban
clause: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: Vesting alone is not enough; any holding lock on the shares must have lifted before they can be included in the collared parcel.

topic: OTC instruments fall outside Covered Securities
clause: Securities: Any financial product quoted on a financial market. Covered Securities: Financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, including shares, options, derivatives, warrants, futures debentures, hybrids and single-entity ETPs.
why_it_matters: An over-the-counter put or call is not a Covered Security, so the pre-clearance and Trading Window machinery does not by its terms apply to the derivative legs, only the express hedging rule and the notification obligation do, but the 'letter and spirit' clause makes it prudent to pre-clear anyway.

clause: You may request a waiver from this Policy's dealing prohibitions in certain exceptional circumstances, including: severe financial hardship ... The proposed dealing is to be the only reasonable course of action available to you and any granted waiver may be subject to conditions.
why_it_matters: This is the only conceivable route to a secured facility, but it is limited to exceptional circumstances where the dealing is the only reasonable course available, so it cannot support an ordinary liquidity or diversification collar.

clause: The ASX Board may decline to open a Trading Window during the periods listed above. The ASX Board may also elect to shorten, change or close a ASX Trading Window at any time.
why_it_matters: There is no guaranteed window, so any collar entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement can be blocked at short notice.

clause: Pre-clearance to deal may be denied for any reason, including, but not limited, to: ... matters known to ASX, but not to you, and your ASX authorisation officer determines pre-clearance should not be granted.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on the executive being able to trade at any particular time, and no reason for a refusal need be given.

clause: This Policy contains a set of principles. You must comply with both the letter and spirit of this Policy.
why_it_matters: A structure engineered around the definition of Covered Securities to escape pre-clearance is exposed to challenge on spirit grounds even if the literal wording permits it.

topic: CS licensee directors cannot hold at all
clause: For NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees, the holding of ASX Group securities is prohibited.
why_it_matters: For that group there is no underlying shareholding at all, so no collar, funded or otherwise, is possible.

clause: Connected Persons are ASX peoples' spouse, de facto partner, children residing with the ASX person, and companies, trusts, Self-Managed Super Funds (SMSFs) or other entities controlled by an ASX person and/or their Connected Persons.
why_it_matters: Holding the shares in a family trust, company or SMSF does not avoid the collateral ban or the pre-clearance and window regime.

clause: You must deal within five business days once ASX pre-clearance approval has been granted.
why_it_matters: Any cleared leg must be executed within five business days, which is workable for a negotiated OTC trade but leaves no room for extended documentation.

clause: Employees must not Deal in Derivatives over Securities at any time.
why_it_matters: Both legs of the collar are prohibited for everyone the Policy covers, at every vesting state, with no consent route and no waiver, so the structure fails before the financing is even considered.

clause: Derivatives means any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities whether now or in the future.
why_it_matters: The definition turns on economic effect rather than instrument type, so a cash-settled, synthetic or forward-starting structure is caught just as squarely as a physically settled put and call.

clause: Employees must not enter into any margin lending arrangements or create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg is separately prohibited, and the words 'or other right to a lender or financier' are wide enough to catch even a negative pledge or a call option written in favour of the financing bank.

clause: Any Security Interest existing prior to the date this Policy is approved is excluded from the operation of this Policy.
why_it_matters: The only permitted encumbrances are those predating the Policy's approval in May 2025, so no new facility can be granted and the exclusion cannot be extended to a refinancing or an increase.

clause: Exceptional Circumstances means where: (a) the Director, Senior Executive or Employee is suffering severe financial hardship ... (c) there are other exceptional circumstances for which the sale of the Securities is the only reasonable course of action available.
why_it_matters: Every limb of the exceptional circumstances relief is framed around selling Securities, so there is no route to a hedged or financed position even in hardship; the only sanctioned answer to a liquidity need is an outright sale with consent.

topic: settlement must complete inside the window
clause: A Deal or Dealing in Securities will be within a Permitted Trading Window if the trade has been settled and completed before the closure of the Permitted Trading Window. ... If the transaction has not been completed or settled before the closure of the Permitted Trading Window at 4pm (AEST) on that day ... the Employee must cancel the trade.
why_it_matters: Unusually strict: settlement, not execution, must fall inside the window, so any physically settled leg would need to complete well before the window closes.

clause: These executives are prohibited from disposing of Securities acquired from awards under any Stockland equity-based plans granted on or after 1 July 2010, unless immediately after that disposal they would continue to hold a minimum number of Securities with a value being the equivalent of two times Fixed Pay for the Managing Director and one times Fixed Pay for all other Senior Executives.
why_it_matters: Even an outright sale, the only permitted form of monetisation, is floored at two times Fixed Pay for the Managing Director and one times for other Senior Executives.

clause: Consent will not be given under section 5.1 if there is any possibility that this Policy could be breached. No reason will be given for the grant or refusal of consent to Deal in Securities. The decision to refuse consent is final and binding on the person seeking consent.
why_it_matters: The 'any possibility' standard means a Consent Authority could not approve any transaction with a bank that touches the derivative or security interest prohibitions, and there is no appeal.

clause: The Chairperson may, at any time, through written notification to Employees impose an additional period for which Employees (or a specific group) are prohibited from Dealing in Securities while Stockland is considering matters subject to Listing Rule 3.1A. This additional period may be temporary or permanent.
why_it_matters: A blackout can be imposed indefinitely and must be kept confidential, so even a permitted sale can become impossible without the executive being able to explain why.

clause: Associate means persons and entities closely connected to a Director or Employee and includes a spouse, domestic partner, child or dependent ... company controlled by the Director or Employee and any other closely related party, as defined in the Corporations Act.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the loan through a spouse, family company or other closely related party does not avoid either prohibition.

clause: dealings under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy and where: the Director or Employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period; the trading plan does not permit the Director or Employee to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to undertake Dealings.
why_it_matters: The only sanctioned way to obtain scheduled liquidity outside a window is a cleared non-discretionary sale plan, which is the realistic alternative to offer in place of a collar.

topic: absolute hedging ban on Designated Personnel
clause: Personnel are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Sandfire securities provided the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Sandfire securities for the purposes of this Policy. This permission does not apply to Designated Personnel. Designated Personnel are prohibited from hedging activity in any circumstances.
why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: every Director, the Executive Leadership Team, restricted list members and their controlled entities and family are banned from the derivative legs outright, so no collar can be offered to them even though the financing side would be workable.

topic: security ban limited to unvested and locked shares
clause: Personnel may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Sandfire securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock to secure any obligation of that relevant Personnel or any third party.
why_it_matters: Unusually, the encumbrance ban stops at unvested and holding-locked securities, so a charge over vested unrestricted shares is not prohibited and the loan leg of a funded structure is available in principle.

clause: Notwithstanding the procedures set out in this Policy, Personnel may at any time: ... dispose of securities in the Company where the disposal is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
why_it_matters: Rare and valuable: lender enforcement is carved out of the Blackout Period and approval machinery altogether, subject only to notifying the Company Secretary within two business days, so a bank's security can be enforced without putting the borrower in breach.

clause: any dealing in Sandfire securities by Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is prohibited. This includes: entering a margin lending arrangement in respect of Sandfire's securities; transferring securities in Sandfire into an existing margin loan account; and selling Sandfire securities to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
why_it_matters: The facility must be a fixed term loan without margin call or top-up mechanics, and the shares must not be moved into a margin account, or the arrangement is caught notwithstanding the narrow security-granting ban.

clause: Short-term trading includes ... entering other short-term dealings (for example, transactions in derivative markets involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative) or otherwise enable Personnel to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
why_it_matters: A purchased put pays out as the price falls, so even for non-designated Personnel the collar should be structured and documented as protection of a held position over a tenor beyond three months, not as a speculative instrument.

topic: exceptional circumstances can lift any prohibition
clause: In exceptional circumstances, and only with prior approval, Personnel may deal in Sandfire securities during a Blackout Period, or in another way otherwise prohibited by this Policy.
why_it_matters: This is the only conceivable route for a Designated Person, since it purports to reach any prohibition, but it sits in tension with the statement that Designated Personnel are prohibited from hedging 'in any circumstances' and requires the Company Secretary, the Approver and sometimes the Remuneration Committee to agree.

clause: from the close of trading on the ASX on 31 March or 30 September each year until the commencement of trading on the ASX on the day following the day on which the relevant quarterly report for those financial quarters is released to the ASX
why_it_matters: Quarterly blackouts on top of the half and full year blackouts leave four closed periods a year, so entry, roll and unwind timing is materially constrained for a company on a quarterly reporting cycle.

clause: If approval to deal is granted, the Designated Personnel must undertake the intended dealing within two business days or such longer period that is advised by the approver (which may not be longer than five business days) following the day clearance is given.
why_it_matters: Any approved leg must be executed within two business days, extendable to five at the Approver's discretion, and the approval may be revoked at any time before then.

clause: An application for approval to deal in Sandfire securities may be refused where the relevant person is not, or as a result of the proposed dealing will not be, in compliance with the Guideline (including the Share Selling Principles).
why_it_matters: The Company Secretariat Function screens for Guideline compliance before the request even reaches the Approver, so a structure that reduces effective exposure may be refused on that ground.

clause: Where any approval is required for dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would be perceived that Personnel might be taking advantage of their position or could possibly be damaging to Sandfire's reputation.
why_it_matters: An open-textured veto sitting above the specific rules, which a hedging or financing structure involving a bank would have to survive.

topic: controlled entities and family are Designated Personnel
clause: as it relates to the persons referred to above: a company or trust controlled by any of the persons referred to above; and a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child (including a step-child or adopted child), a close relative, a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to above.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban follows the shares into family trusts, controlled companies and family members' hands, so the structure cannot be moved to an associate to escape it.

clause: Covered Persons are prohibited from: ... Using TechnologyOne's Securities as security for loans or margin lending.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for every director, officer, employee and contractor, with no approval or waiver route, so the funded structure cannot be offered.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested and locked stock
clause: Covered Persons are not permitted at any time to enter into a transaction that is designed or intended to hedge their exposure to TechnologyOne securities which have not vested or are subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction.
why_it_matters: Unlike the loan ban, the hedging prohibition stops at unvested and locked shares, so an unfunded collar over vested unrestricted shares is not itself prohibited.

clause: "Securities" include shares, options, derivatives, and any other financial products of TechnologyOne that can be traded on a financial market.
why_it_matters: The qualifier 'that can be traded on a financial market' leaves it arguable whether a bilateral OTC put and call are Securities at all, so the bank should assume they are and seek clearance rather than rely on the ambiguity.

clause: Short-term trading (buying and selling Securities within a 3-month period).
why_it_matters: Because Securities expressly include derivatives, buying a put and writing a call and then unwinding either leg inside three months risks being characterised as prohibited short-term trading, so the collar tenor and any roll should exceed three months.

clause: Additional blackout periods may be imposed by the Board or CEO as necessary.
why_it_matters: The Board or CEO can close the trading window without notice or stated criteria, so pricing, unwind or physical settlement of a collar can be blocked at short notice.

clause: This policy applies to all directors, officers, employees, and contractors of TechnologyOne and its subsidiaries (referred to as "Covered Persons").
why_it_matters: The policy never extends to spouses, dependants or controlled entities and trusts, so its literal reach over shares held through a family trust is untested rather than clearly prohibited; the bank should not treat that as a workaround.

clause: Details of Trading in TechnologyOne Securities undertaken by the Chair, Directors or KMP are to be provided to the Company Secretary as soon as possible and within two business days of the Trade at the latest so that notification can be made via the ASX Announcements Platform.
why_it_matters: Collar entry, roll and unwind by a Director or KMP will be disclosed publicly through Appendix 3Y-style notification within two business days, so the structure cannot be kept confidential.

clause: The Chair, Directors and KMP are required to be granted approval from the following before Trading.
why_it_matters: The policy states no validity period, response time, conditions power or revocation right for an approval, so the bank cannot rely on a defined execution window and should obtain the approval terms in writing before pricing.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans; - hedging; - short-term dealing, including buying and selling Securities on market within a three month period; and - short selling.
why_it_matters: 'Hedging' is undefined and unlimited by vesting state or venue, so a collar over fully vested unrestricted shares is prohibited for every Director and Executive Committee member, with no approval or hardship route.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans.
why_it_matters: The financing prohibition names only margin loans rather than secured financing generally, so the loan leg is not expressly banned; but with the hedge itself prohibited the point is academic, and a loan advanced against collared shares may still be characterised as a margin loan.

clause: Securities Includes, in relation to Orica Limited: ... any other financial product relating to securities whether or not the product is created by Orica or by a third party.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call are expressly Securities, so every leg of a collar and every roll or unwind is a dealing subject to the policy rather than sitting outside it.

topic: profit or loss arrangements are dealings
clause: Deal or dealing Includes: ... entering into a contract or arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations.
why_it_matters: This limb catches economically synthetic structures (collars, CFDs, prepaid forwards) even when no share changes hands, so no cash-settled variant escapes the policy.

clause: Do not deal in Securities if the Company has formally notified you that you are restricted from dealing.
why_it_matters: Even an employee outside the Restricted Persons tier can be individually blocked at any time without notice or criteria, so a counterparty cannot rely on a person's tier remaining unrestricted for the life of a collar.

clause: Any approval to deal may be withdrawn at any time if there is a change in circumstance, and any decision to refuse approval is final and binding and must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: Approval can be pulled after it is given and before execution, and the executive cannot explain a refusal to the bank, so there is execution risk between pricing and signing.

clause: A Restricted Person approved to deal must deal no later than two business days commencing on the day after approval is received, otherwise new approval must be sought.
why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be documented and executed inside a two business day window, which is tight for negotiating and signing OTC derivative and loan documentation.

clause: Associates of Directors, employees and contractors are subject to the same dealing restrictions that apply to that individual. ... a company or any other entity which you have an ability to control or significantly influence.
why_it_matters: Routing a collar through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the hedging prohibition, and the Restricted Person must obtain written approval for dealings on the associate's behalf.

topic: plan shares remain in scope after release
clause: Applying for or acquiring Securities under an employee incentive scheme; however, for clarity, any subsequent dealing of Securities which cease to be held under the terms of a scheme remains subject to the provisions of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Shares released from an incentive plan do not become policy-free, so vested shares held by a Restricted Person remain subject to the hedging prohibition.

topic: effects-based hedging ban over vested shares
clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.
why_it_matters: This is drafted by economic effect and expressly reaches vested shares, so the purchased put and written call of a collar are prohibited outright for every Director and CLT member with no approval or hardship route.

topic: secured financing wider than margin lending
clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently prohibited, so the funded element fails even before the hedging ban is considered.

clause: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) issued over or in respect of vested Caltex securities and unvested entitlements to Caltex securities.
why_it_matters: There is no argument that a bilateral OTC collar sits outside the policy; it is expressly captured, over both vested and unvested exposure.

clause: "Caltex securities" includes ordinary shares of Caltex and any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, option, warrant, or other derivative over an ordinary share of Caltex, whether issued by Caltex or a third party, and any other interest in an ordinary share of Caltex.
why_it_matters: The bank-written put and call are themselves Caltex securities, so the six month short-term trading ban and the closed period restrictions apply to the derivative legs and to any roll or unwind, not just to the underlying shares.

topic: six month short-term ban including derivatives
clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from engaging in short term or speculative trading in Caltex securities or derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.
why_it_matters: Even if hedging were permitted, any collar with a tenor, roll or early unwind inside six months would be separately prohibited as short-term or speculative trading.

clause: Clearance ... will lapse 14 calendar days after the date the clearance was granted ... Clearance to trade can be given or refused without giving any reasons and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. If clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: Any permitted transaction must be executed inside 14 calendar days, can be revoked between grant and execution, and the executive cannot tell the bank why a refusal occurred.

clause: Any clearance to trade may be withheld for perception reasons.
why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant transaction can be blocked on reputational grounds alone, which is precisely the ground on which a director's collar would be scrutinised.

topic: transfer to a third party holding is a trade
clause: Nature of proposed trade (i.e. on market purchase, on-market transfer or sale, transfer to super fund).
why_it_matters: The clearance form treats a transfer to another holding vehicle as a notifiable trade, so moving collared shares into a bank custody or security account would require clearance and post-trade notification, even though transfers with no change in beneficial interest are listed as Permitted Trading.

clause: Designated Caltex Personnel must notify the Caltex Secretariat of details of any trading in Caltex securities by submitting a contract note to secretariat@caltex.com.au no later than three days after the date of the trade.
why_it_matters: Any collar entry, roll or unwind by a Director or CLT member is reported to the Secretariat within three days and, for Directors, flows into ASX disclosure.

clause: "closely connected persons" of Caltex staff include immediate family members, companies and businesses in which Caltex staff hold a controlling interest and/or are a Director or Trustee where Caltex staff are beneficiaries.
why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a family company or trust does not escape the hedging and secured financing prohibitions.

clause: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.
why_it_matters: All of the collar-relevant prohibitions bind only Designated Caltex Personnel, but any employee can be notified into that tier at any time, so a counterparty cannot rely on a client remaining outside it for the life of the trade.

clause: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above; and Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.
why_it_matters: This is a permission rather than a prohibition, so the derivative legs of a collar over a Director's or Executive's shareholding are allowed provided each of entry, renewal, alteration and close-out is separately cleared and clean of price sensitive information.

clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, charges, pledges or encumbrances over Company securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is neither prohibited nor made subject to clearance or disclosure, so the funded element of the structure is not blocked by the policy, though the bank should still confirm the position with the Company Secretary.

clause: The policy is silent on sales of Company securities effected by a third party such as a secured lender, and there is no excluded dealing for them.
why_it_matters: A lender enforcement sale or physical settlement falling inside a black-out period has no safe harbour, and the only relief route is a discretionary Company Secretary approval for a disposal on exceptional circumstances grounds.

clause: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: Forward-style monetisation is expressly given as an example of a prohibited short-term dealing, so the collar tenor and any roll or unwind should comfortably exceed three months and the structure should be documented as a hedge rather than a forward sale.

clause: However, Executives are not permitted to hedge equity awards granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.
why_it_matters: The collar can only reference shares acquired on exercise that are free of any transfer restriction, so the eligible parcel must be verified against Plan records before pricing.

topic: close-out is a separate cleared event
clause: Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.
why_it_matters: Renewal, amendment and termination of the collar each require the person to be clean of price sensitive information and, under clause 6.1, to be cleared and outside a black-out period, so the documentation should avoid automatic or counterparty-triggered close-outs.

clause: Can be given or refused by Reece in its discretion, without giving any reasons; Can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances; Reece's discretion to refuse clearance is final and binding.
why_it_matters: Clearance can be revoked between grant and execution and a refusal cannot be explained to the bank, so there is execution risk in the five business day window.

clause: A clearance under this clause is not an endorsement of proposed trading and it is the Directors and Executives whom are ultimately responsible for ensuring their dealings in securities comply with the applicable laws and as applicable, the Policy.
why_it_matters: A clearance acknowledgement should not be treated by the bank as a company confirmation that the collar is compliant; the risk stays with the individual.

clause: For the purpose of this clause 6.1, a reference to 'Directors' and 'Executives' is also a reference to their Related Parties. ... A company, trust, partnership or another entity that the person or any of the persons referred to in the above bullet points controls or significantly influences.
why_it_matters: A collar entered through a family trust or controlled company still requires clearance, and the Director or Executive must communicate with the approver on that entity's behalf.

clause: If you possess price sensitive information in relation to an entity you cannot 'trade' or 'deal' in the following ways: Buy or sell securities in that entity or subscribe for new securities; or Enter into an agreement to subscribe for, buy or sell securities in that entity.
why_it_matters: The general dealing definition does not sweep in derivatives, encumbrances or stock lending; derivatives are regulated only through the separate section 6.2 hedging regime, which is a permission, so the policy's restrictive reach over an OTC collar is narrow.

clause: you may apply in writing to the Company Secretary for approval to dispose of (but not to acquire) Company securities during a black-out period.
why_it_matters: The exceptional circumstances relief is disposal-only, so a collar entry (which involves acquiring a put) cannot be cleared inside a black-out period on hardship grounds.

clause: A Restricted Person or Connected Person may not deal in Company securities or enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging) without the prior consent of the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director before commencing the transaction.
why_it_matters: Hedging is a consent-gated activity rather than a prohibition, so the derivative legs of a collar over ordinary vested shares can be approved; the consent is discretionary and the policy adds that Hedging is 'generally speaking discouraged'.

clause: The policy contains no provision on margin lending, secured financing, charges, mortgages or pledges over Company securities, and no related disclosure obligation.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited or made subject to consent, so the funded element turns on the general principles and on whatever conditions the approver imposes rather than on an express bar.

clause: do not utilise broker credit - relevant exchange settlement terms must apply on all occasions and all transactions must be settled according to industry standards.
why_it_matters: The only leverage-related principle in the policy bars trading on broker credit, so the bank should structure the facility as a third party loan secured on an existing holding rather than as credit used to acquire or settle Company securities.

clause: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons may never engage in short term trading of any Company securities. In general, the purchase of securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature.
why_it_matters: The tenor of the collar, and any roll, early termination or physical settlement, should exceed 12 months, since a written call that is exercised inside that period looks like a sale with a view to a repurchase or a short-dated disposal.

clause: in exceptional circumstances the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director, has discretion to approve dealings in Company securities during a Blackout Period, or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies, the waiver power extends beyond blackout relief to any dealing otherwise prohibited, so even the plan-securities hedging bar and the 12 month rule are in principle waivable on a case-by-case basis.

clause: Paragraphs 11(h) and 15 require consent from the Managing Director (or the Chairman for the Managing Director), while paragraph 16 requires the Company Secretary to seek consent from the Chairman of the Board as Authorising Officer (or the Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chairman of the Board).
why_it_matters: The policy names two different approval routes for the same dealing, so consent for a collar should be obtained from both the Managing Director and the Chairman of the Board through the Company Secretary to be safe.

clause: The Authorising Officer may refuse to consent to the proposed dealing or impose conditions on the dealing at their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any refusal or condition.
why_it_matters: The company can attach conditions to a collar approval, for example on size, tenor or disclosure, and those conditions must be reflected in the derivative and loan documentation before pricing.

clause: In all cases, the dealing consented to must occur within 5 business days following approval, otherwise the consent is no longer effective and fresh consent must be sought.
why_it_matters: The collar and loan documentation must be ready to sign before consent is sought, since the approval expires five business days after it is granted.

clause: "Company securities" includes any shares in the Company, debentures (including convertible notes) issued by the Company, units of shares in the Company and rights or options to acquire or subscribe for shares in the Company.
why_it_matters: Third party derivatives are not themselves Company securities, so a bank-written put and call are caught by the paragraph 15 Hedging test rather than by the dealing and Blackout provisions, and the analysis turns on economic effect rather than on instrument type.

clause: avoid personal trading that would not satisfy the Front Page Test, being: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as the individual taking advantage of his or her position in an inappropriate way? How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
why_it_matters: A director's funded collar is exactly the kind of transaction that attracts perception scrutiny, so the approver may refuse consent on this ground alone even though nothing in the policy prohibits it.

clause: A Restricted Person must also provide the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board ... with subsequent confirmation of the trading that has occurred (including trading by one of their Connected Persons). ... a director must notify the ASX within 5 days after any change in the director's relevant interest in securities of the Company.
why_it_matters: Hedging by a Restricted Person must be confirmed to the company after the event and a director's change in relevant interest reaches the ASX within five days, so the collar will not stay private.

clause: This policy also applies to Connected Persons of all Restricted Persons, being each of their respective associates (including a company or trust controlled by the Restricted Person, a spouse, dependent children, a close relative, a person acting in concert with the Restricted Person, etc).
why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through a controlled company or trust does not avoid the consent, short-term trading or confirmation requirements.

clause: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 of this Policy do not apply to the following: ... [excluded dealings]. Exceptional circumstances relief in section 4.2 is likewise expressed as relief to 'deal in securities during a blackout period'.
why_it_matters: Every relief mechanism in the policy operates only on the blackout and approval requirements, so the hedging, monetisation, publicly traded options and pledging bans that kill a funded collar cannot be waived by anyone, including the Board.

clause: You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The purchased put leg of a collar is the paradigm arrangement designed to offset a decrease in market price, and the word 'monetisation' independently captures the funded element, so the structure is prohibited on its face for all Employees and Connected Persons.

clause: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is separately and expressly prohibited, so even an unfunded collar could not be financed against the shares.

clause: Employees may not engage in transactions in publicly traded options in the Company's securities, such as puts, calls or derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market.
why_it_matters: Listed puts and calls are barred outright, and while a bilateral bank OTC option is not 'publicly traded', the substance over form statement means the Company will look through an OTC wrapper used to achieve the same result.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A structure engineered to sit outside the literal words (for example a bespoke OTC collar, a Connected Person entity, or a non-recourse loan documented as a sale) will still be assessed on its economic substance as hedging or monetisation.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a dealing that is technically permitted must survive a reputational test, and a bank-funded collar over executive shares is precisely the kind of transaction that would fail it.

clause: You may not place standing orders (e.g. open orders at set prices) involving Company securities.
why_it_matters: Price-triggered or knock-in/knock-out features and automatic delivery mechanics would need to be recast as a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, which cannot be entered into or amended during a blackout.

clause: Employees must ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities when the Employee to whom they are connected would be permitted to do so under this Policy. The same restrictions that apply to Employees apply equally to their Connected Persons.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a controlled trust, household member or influenced family member does not escape any of the prohibitions.

clause: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of 'short-swing profits' and restrictions on short sales of the Company's securities).
why_it_matters: For US-reporting insiders the put and call legs are themselves Section 16 derivative securities: entering, amending or settling them creates reportable transactions that can be matched against ordinary purchases within six months, generating disgorgement risk independent of the ASX policy.

clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: Any approved leg of a multi-step structure can be pulled without reasons before execution, and the five business day approval life means a cleared trade must be priced and closed quickly.

clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
why_it_matters: A breach can extinguish the very shares that collateralise the bank's loan, so the bank's security is exposed to a disciplinary outcome rather than only market risk.

clause: If you are aware of Inside Information when your employment or engagement ends, you must not trade until that information becomes public and one full trading day has elapsed, or it ceases to be material.
why_it_matters: Departure does not immediately free an executive to enter or unwind a structure, though the section 3 bans are framed as applying to Employees and so would fall away on cessation.

clause: The entering into of all types of 'protection arrangements' for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and otherwise, requires approval under Section 6.
why_it_matters: This is the pivotal clause: a collar is permissible in principle over vested, lock-free shares with clearance, but is absolutely barred over unvested awards and vested shares still under a holding lock, so the collateral pool must be carefully segregated.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in Section 6.
why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this does not ban secured financing, so the funded leg of the collar is available on approval, but the loan and the derivative legs each need clearance and both must be obtained before the structure is entered into.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights (for example, under a margin lending arrangement) [is excluded from the blackout restrictions] ... Unless otherwise stated, prior written clearance under Section 6 is not required for the above Dealings.
why_it_matters: The bank can enforce its security and sell the collared shares during a Blackout Period or Additional Period without putting the executive in breach and without a fresh clearance, which materially de-risks the lending leg.

clause: operate to limit the economic risk of any Restricted Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Restricted Person's behalf
why_it_matters: Shares sitting in an employee plan trust or a family trust count towards the hedging test, so a structure written over trust-held shares needs the same approval and, if those shares are still locked, is prohibited.

clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for a period of five business days ... Written clearance under this policy may be withdrawn by the Approving Officer in writing at any time during the clearance period ... should the Approving Officer consider that circumstances have changed.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documenting and executing both the derivative and the loan must fit inside a five business day window that the Company can revoke at will, so the bank should expect signing risk up to the moment of execution.

clause: The Approving Officer may as appropriate, seek input from relevant Key Management Personnel and Senior Employees about the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed Dealing ... Where any approval under this policy is required for a dealing, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the "front page" test.
why_it_matters: Clearance for an executive collar is a discretionary reputational judgment rather than a mechanical check, and the front page test is an express bar on approval.

topic: no acquisition relief in a blackout
clause: may be given prior written clearance to dispose of or transfer (but not to acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period
why_it_matters: Even in hardship, a collar cannot be entered, rolled or restructured during a Blackout or Additional Period; only outright disposals or transfers can be cleared, so timing must fall in an open window.

clause: Under no circumstances should Restricted Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities. This prohibition includes short term direct dealing ... involving exchange-trade options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.
why_it_matters: A short-dated collar, or one with early termination or knock-out features, risks being characterised as short-term derivative dealing prohibited 'under no circumstances', so tenor and structure should be plainly long-term and protective.

clause: A Restricted Person is: ... a Connected Person of any person referred to in the sub-paragraphs above.
why_it_matters: A spouse, controlled company or family trust entering the collar or the loan is itself a Restricted Person needing its own clearance, so nothing is gained by moving the structure off the executive's own name.

topic: OTC and cash-settled derivatives are securities
clause: Company Securities ... includes ... derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.
why_it_matters: A cash-settled OTC collar cannot be argued to fall outside the policy on the basis that no shares move; it is a dealing in Company Securities in its own right.

clause: The Company Secretary must maintain a register of notifications and clearances given in relation to trading in Company Securities ... and must report all notifications ... upon request by the Board.
why_it_matters: Any approval of a collar and secured loan will be recorded and reportable to the Board, and for directors the resulting change of interest is disclosed to ASX within five business days.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested and locked awards
clause: Designated Officers are also prohibited from entering into: transactions in products which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements or entitlements subject to a holding lock under any equity based remuneration schemes.
why_it_matters: This is the decisive limit: the hedging prohibition does not reach vested, unlocked shares, so a collar over those shares is not banned, but the collateral pool must exclude anything still unvested or under a holding lock.

clause: Directors of Sonic Healthcare Limited are also prohibited from entering into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Sonic securities without the prior approval of the Chair (and for the Chair, the Chair of the Remuneration and Nomination Committee) and disclosure of such arrangements to the Board.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is available to a director on Chair approval plus Board disclosure rather than being prohibited, and the clause binds directors only, so non-director Designated Officers face no secured financing restriction at all.

clause: Designated Officers are only permitted to trade in the period of eight weeks commencing on the business day after the public announcement of half year and year end results ... The Sonic Board of Directors must specifically consider and approve the opening of the "trading window" in each instance.
why_it_matters: This is a positive-permission regime: outside a Board-approved window a Designated Officer simply cannot trade, so entry, roll, restrike or unwind of a collar must be scheduled into a window that the Board has actually opened.

clause: Designated Officers are required to commit to this by signing the Securities Trading Policy and will forfeit their equity rewards should they be found to be in breach.
why_it_matters: A breach can extinguish the executive's unvested equity, which both removes future collateral and creates a strong incentive to structure conservatively; a bank should not lend against awards that a policy breach could forfeit.

clause: Designated Officers are also prohibited from entering into: ... short-term trading and short selling arrangements in Sonic securities.
why_it_matters: With no defined period, a short-dated or early-terminable collar risks being characterised as a short-term trading arrangement, so tenor should be clearly long and the structure should not contain features that look like a synthetic short.

clause: Sonic securities (including shares, options, derivatives, debt securities and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market) ... The prohibitions described above also apply to trading in financial products issued or created over Sonic's securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: The core definition is limited to products tradeable on a financial market, but the extension sentence sweeps in bilateral bank-created products over Sonic securities, so an OTC collar cannot be argued outside the policy.

clause: any clearance to trade can be given or refused by the appropriate person in their discretion, without giving any reasons; a clearance to trade can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances; ... a decision to refuse clearance is final and binding.
why_it_matters: Where approval is needed (Chair approval for secured financing, or for a sale by the Managing Director or Finance Director) it is unreviewable and revocable up to execution, so the bank carries signing risk on the funded leg.

clause: Sonic's Chair or Managing Director may impose other periods when Designated Officers are prohibited from trading because price sensitive, non-public information may exist.
why_it_matters: An open window can be shut at short notice without any stated disclosure obligation, which can strand a partially executed or maturing structure.

clause: All Sonic share dealings by Directors must be promptly notified to the ASX by the Company Secretary. Directors are therefore required to complete an Appendix 3Y and forward to the Company Secretary within two business days of executing (i.e. before settlement) any trade.
why_it_matters: Both derivative legs and any change in the nature of a director's interest arising from the collar and the security will become public via the Appendix 3Y within two business days.

clause: In relation to any person under (a) to (d) above: their spouse ... their nominee, including an investment manager managing funds on their behalf; a trust of which they, or any of their connected persons ... are the trustee or beneficiary; ... a company which they or any of their connected persons ... control.
why_it_matters: A collar booked in a family trust, controlled company or through a discretionary investment manager is treated as the Designated Officer's own trade and must sit in a window.

clause: Version Date: 4 November 2016.
why_it_matters: This is an old policy that predates the market convention of banning all hedging by KMP; the absence of a general hedging ban should be confirmed against the current remuneration report and any equity plan rules before a bank relies on it.

clause: KMPs and Employees are prohibited from ... obtaining margin loans using GPT Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or entering into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of GPT Securities.
why_it_matters: This is decisive: the loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared securities, is prohibited outright for every KMP, Employee and Associate with no vesting carve-out and no approval or hardship route.

topic: security interest over restricted vested securities
clause: entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested GPT Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition
why_it_matters: Even a financing that was not otherwise 'secured financing' cannot take a security interest over vested securities still under a holding lock or forfeiture condition, so no part of the restricted holding can be pledged.

clause: hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition
why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition is tied to restricted remuneration, so an unfunded collar over fully vested, unrestricted securities is not itself banned; only the funding and security elements are.

clause: Securities: Includes: shares or debentures in a company or unit or other interest in a scheme; an option over an unissued share, or debenture of, the company; ... Dealing: To: Sell (or otherwise dispose) or acquire GPT Securities or arrange someone else to do so whether on or off market; and Transfer legal ownership of Securities.
why_it_matters: Third-party derivatives over issued GPT Securities are not within the defined terms, so an OTC option is regulated only through the hedging and secured financing bullets, while any physical settlement is squarely a Dealing needing a Trading Window and notification.

clause: short-term dealing (i.e. if a person buys (or sells) GPT securities on a date and then sells (or buys) any GPT securities on a date that is less than 30 days after the first dealing)
why_it_matters: A mechanical matching rule with no intention element: any share purchase or sale within 30 days on either side of a physically settled leg breaches the policy, so settlement timing must be mapped against all other dealings.

clause: KMPs, Employees and Associates are prohibited from dealing in GPT Securities during all periods that are outside an available trading window.
why_it_matters: This is a positive-permission regime with five six-week windows a year, so entry, settlement or unwind of any structure must be scheduled inside a window that has not been suspended.

clause: The availability of any Trading Window may be varied, suspended or terminated by the GPT Group Board at any time, including being varied for all KMP and Employees or a subset of persons.
why_it_matters: The Board can close a window for one individual without notice to the market, which can strand a partially executed structure or block a scheduled settlement.

clause: Receipt of a notification of intention to deal and any clearance provided is intended as a compliance monitoring function only and is not endorsement or approval of the proposed dealing.
why_it_matters: A bank cannot treat a GPT clearance as company approval of the structure; the executive bears full responsibility and a clearance carries no comfort that the arrangement complies with 5.2.

clause: Any breach of this Policy or failure to act within the spirit of this Policy will be viewed seriously and will be subject to disciplinary action which may include termination of employment with GPT.
why_it_matters: Structuring around the literal words of the secured financing ban, for example through a non-recourse prepaid forward or a third-party funder, would still be judged against the spirit of the policy.

clause: extends to a KMP's and an Employee's family, related parties or associates, including related corporations, superannuation funds or investment vehicles where the KMP or Employee has influence over the related parties' judgement in relation to investment decisions
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a family trust, controlled company or self-managed fund does not avoid the secured financing prohibition or the window restriction.

clause: Any clearance provided under this section must be effected (even if not settled) within five business days of the date of the clearance.
why_it_matters: Any dealing leg must be executed within five business days of notification, and the approver may impose conditions in their discretion without giving reasons.

clause: In relation to vested Securities (held within a Group employee incentive scheme) or Securities held outside such a scheme: 1. you can only buy a derivative position during a trading window, and 2. you cannot sell a derivative position.
why_it_matters: This single clause defeats a collar: the written call is a sold derivative position and is prohibited outright, even over fully vested securities, while the purchased put on its own would be permissible in a window with consent.

topic: hedge must stay in your control
clause: The only hedging arrangements allowed is when they are in your control, rather than the control of any third party.
why_it_matters: A bank-documented OTC structure with dealer election rights, early termination triggers or enforcement over the shares places control with a third party, so even a put-only hedge must be structured so the executive retains control.

clause: You are not allowed to enter into, or seek to enter into, any type of margin loan arrangement in respect of Securities, whether on a stand-alone basis or as part of an investment portfolio.
why_it_matters: The funded leg is blocked: 'any type of margin loan arrangement' naturally covers a share-backed facility with loan-to-value maintenance, and the prohibition extends to merely seeking to enter one.

clause: Section 2.5 addresses margin loans only; the policy contains no prohibition on secured financing generally and no clause making the grant of a security interest a Dealing.
why_it_matters: A term loan secured on Charter Hall Securities without margining sits in a genuine gap in the drafting, but it would still fall foul of the control requirement in 2.4 and should be cleared with the Company Secretary rather than assumed permissible.

clause: You cannot enter, or seek to enter any type of transaction or arrangement that would hedge the exposure to movements in the price of unvested Securities or those which remain subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: Any collateral pool must exclude unvested awards and vested securities still under a holding lock; the prohibition bites on attempting the arrangement, not just completing it.

clause: Short-term trading of Securities (i.e., selling Securities within a four-week period from the date of acquisition) is not allowed.
why_it_matters: Securities delivered or acquired in connection with a structure cannot be sold for four weeks, which constrains delivery mechanics and any unwind that involves selling recently acquired securities.

clause: If a trade is set to trigger at a set price and has not been completed within the 5 business days a new consent will need to be obtained. If the trade has not happened and the window is closing, this trade must be cancelled by the end of business day of the close of a trading window.
why_it_matters: Contingent or price-triggered execution cannot survive a window close, so knock-in or barrier features that execute automatically are incompatible with the consent regime.

clause: Trading Windows to Deal in Securities are as follows: 1. for the period beginning the day after the announcement of the Charter Hall Group's half year results until and including 31 May; and 2. for the period beginning the day after the announcement of the Charter Hall Group's annual results until and including 30 November.
why_it_matters: Only two windows a year, each ending on a fixed calendar date, so any entry, roll or unwind must be scheduled well before 31 May or 30 November.

clause: Charter Hall may declare additional trading windows or trading blackouts in Securities at any time at its absolute discretion and without prior notice if considered necessary.
why_it_matters: A window can be closed without warning, and consent may be withheld without reasons whenever management accounts are available outside a window, so execution certainty is low.

clause: Consent will not be given if there is any possibility that this Policy could be breached by the Dealing. Consent may not be given when management accounts are available at a time other than during a Trading Window. Furthermore, no reason is required to be given for the grant or refusal of consent to Deal in Securities.
why_it_matters: The 'any possibility' standard is deliberately conservative, so an approver is likely to refuse a structure whose compliance is arguable, and there is no appeal or reasons.

clause: Securities: ... any interest created over those securities by third parties, structured financial products, swaps, future contracts, contracts for differences, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of those securities.
why_it_matters: A bank-created OTC option or swap over Charter Hall securities is itself a Security, so every leg is a Dealing subject to windows, consent and the notification regime.

clause: Charter Hall must disclose any purchase or sale of listed Securities by any one of its Directors to the ASX within 5 business days from the Dealing being settled/completed.
why_it_matters: Any permitted derivative purchase by a director becomes public within five business days of settlement, so the structure cannot be kept confidential.

topic: collars named in the derivative definition
clause: Derivative includes: derivatives within the meaning of section 761D of the Act, such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants and caps and/or collars.
why_it_matters: The policy expressly contemplates collars as a recognised instrument and, over vested unlocked shares, permits them, so the derivative legs are squarely within the permitted category rather than an unaddressed structure.

topic: collateral is a dealing, not a prohibition
clause: Deal or Dealing includes ... the use of Securities as collateral or security over Securities (including a Margin Lending Arrangement).
why_it_matters: The secured loan leg is permitted but must itself be timed inside a Trading Window and, for a Key Designated Person, covered by a notice of 'no objection'; the pledge and the option legs should be cleared together.

clause: An involuntary disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example under a Margin Lending Arrangement (provided that this Policy was complied with ... in relation to entry into the relevant secured lending arrangement), is an Exempt Dealing.
why_it_matters: The bank may enforce its security or close out the collar in a Prohibited Period without putting the executive in breach, provided the facility was properly cleared at inception - a materially better enforcement position than most ASX policies.

clause: any Cochlear Security (including where applicable any Plan Award) that is issued subject to a holding lock shall (notwithstanding any vesting) be subject to the same restrictions under this Section 4.5 as unvested Cochlear Securities, until the holding lock is released.
why_it_matters: Only vested shares free of any holding lock may be collared, so the bank must diligence the lock status of each parcel and not merely its vesting.

topic: no objection expires with the window
clause: Where a notice of "no objection" is given, the Key Designated Person must execute the proposed Dealing before the end of the Trading Window during which the notice of "no objection" was given.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and settlement of the collar and the loan must all complete inside a 30 day window that the Company Secretary can terminate early at any time.

clause: Cochlear may by notice in writing to a Designated Person withdraw a notice of "no objection" or waiver of this Policy if, subsequent to the grant, new information becomes available or there is a change in circumstances. Upon withdrawal ... the relevant Designated Person must not carry out any Dealings ... that remain unexecuted at the time.
why_it_matters: The bank should treat clearance as revocable up to execution and avoid staged or delayed closings that could be caught by a withdrawal.

clause: The Company Secretary may end a Trading Window immediately by notice in writing to Designated Persons.
why_it_matters: Unwinds, rolls, resets and top-ups of the collar can be blocked without warning, so the documentation should allow cash settlement or lender-side action that falls within the secured lender exemption.

topic: unvested hedging ban extends to associates
clause: A Designated Person must not enter (and must procure that none of his or her Associates enter) into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the Designated Person to risk relating to an element of the Designated Person's remuneration (including any Plan Award) that has not vested.
why_it_matters: The structure cannot be routed through a spouse, controlled company or family trust to hedge unvested awards, and the 'with anyone' wording captures OTC arrangements with a bank.

topic: disclosure of derivative and financing positions
clause: Directors of Cochlear must disclose to Cochlear any Derivatives position relating to Cochlear Securities. If requested by Cochlear, a Designated Person must disclose to Cochlear details of their current Derivatives positions [and] Margin Lending Arrangements relating to Cochlear Securities.
why_it_matters: Both the collar and the secured loan are disclosable to the company and potentially to the ASX, so confidentiality of the trade terms cannot be assured.

topic: short selling and stock lending bans
clause: Cochlear Personnel must not engage in short selling or stock lending activities in relation to Cochlear Securities.
why_it_matters: The executive must deliver or pledge shares they own outright and cannot lend stock to the bank to support its hedge, so the bank must hedge its own delta in the market.

clause: The Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by Perseus or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable.
why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: a funded collar is permitted only where the loan funds the exercise price of Perseus options or the hedge protects against a tax liability, so a collar used to raise general liquidity against a vested holding fails the closed list of permitted purposes.

clause: The Derivative has a maturity date that falls outside any Prohibited Period known at the time of entering into the transaction.
why_it_matters: The collar's expiry and any physical settlement date must be scheduled clear of the Closed Periods, which run from two weeks before to one Trading Day after each quarterly report and each half and full year result - roughly four blackouts a year - materially constraining tenor selection.

clause: Perseus is not a counterparty to the Derivative.
why_it_matters: A third party bank counterparty is expressly required, which suits the proposed structure.

clause: The Board's approval is required before Perseus's Key Management Personnel grant any encumbrances or enter into margin loans in respect of Perseus's Securities or make changes to any such arrangements.
why_it_matters: The security over the collared shares needs full Board approval, not merely Company Secretary clearance, and every amendment, roll or top-up of the facility requires the Board to approve again.

topic: forced sale protection conditional on Board approval
clause: The disposing of Securities ... as a result of a secured lender exercising its rights under a margin lending arrangement where prior written Board approval was received for entry into the arrangement under section 10.1(a) of the Policy [is excluded from the operation of this Policy].
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale is carved out of the Policy only if the Board approved the facility in writing at inception, so obtaining and documenting that approval is a condition precedent to any enforceable security.

topic: loan terms must not force prohibited dealing
clause: Key Management Personnel should ensure that the terms of any margin lending arrangements do not require Dealings in Perseus's Securities at a time when Key Management Personnel are prohibited from Dealing in Perseus's Securities.
why_it_matters: Margin call and close-out mechanics should be drafted so that the borrower is never obliged to trade during a Closed Period, for example by allowing cash cure, substitution of collateral or lender-side action.

clause: Short-term trading means the purchase and sale of the same type of Securities within a three month period. Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from Short-term Trading.
why_it_matters: Because Securities are defined to include Derivatives and products that limit economic risk, entering and unwinding a collar inside three months could itself be Short-term Trading, so tenor should exceed three months absent a Board exemption.

topic: securities definition sweeps in risk-limiting products
clause: Securities include shares, debentures, renounceable or unrenounceable rights ... Derivatives and other financial products that can be traded on a financial market including financial products issued or created over securities by third parties and products which operate to limit economic risk in securities holdings.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs are themselves Securities, so entry into and unwind of each leg is a Dealing requiring two Trading Days' prior clearance and post-trade notification within two Trading Days.

clause: Any clearance under this Policy may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. In such event the Company Secretary will notify the relevant Key Management Personnel who must withdraw any outstanding order for a Dealing in Perseus Securities promptly.
why_it_matters: Clearance is revocable up to execution, so pricing and signing should occur promptly within the five Trading Day window rather than in staged closings.

clause: In addition to the restrictions set out in section 10.2 of this Policy, any Applicable Person who has been issued with Securities under a Perseus incentive plan ... must not enter into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure ... to risk relating to an element of that Applicable Person's remuneration that has not vested ... or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: The bank must confirm that every share in the collared parcel is both vested and free of any holding lock, and that no incentive plan participant below KMP level is hedging plan securities.

topic: lender rights need CFO and Company Secretary approval
clause: prior approval must be obtained, via the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, before entering into an agreement which provides a lender with rights over a director's, officer's, executive's, senior manager's or closely-related party's interests in the Company's securities
why_it_matters: The security package for the loan leg is permitted but is gated by a specific approval from the CFO and Company Secretary that is separate from the ordinary section 11 dealing approval, and it is drafted broadly enough to catch any lender rights over the shares, not just a margin loan.

clause: where a disposal of securities of the Company occurs as a result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example under a margin lending arrangement [the trading is not subject to this Policy]
why_it_matters: Once the facility is approved, the bank can enforce its security or close out the collar even during a blackout period without the executive breaching the Policy.

clause: the guiding principle should be that at the time of purchase the person should not intend to resell the securities within 12 months with the aim of realising a capital gain.
why_it_matters: This is an unusually long horizon; a collar with a tenor under twelve months, or one with early unwind triggers, risks being characterised as short-term or speculative trading, which is banned outright with no approval route.

topic: hedging ban reaches restricted vested shares
clause: Codan employees and closely-related parties are prohibited from entering into transactions which would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an unvested option or performance rights, or to a vested security which remains subject to a trading restriction.
why_it_matters: Only fully vested shares free of any trading restriction can be collared, and the ban binds every employee and their closely-related parties with no approval or exceptional circumstances route.
