clause: "Dealing" means ... make or offer to make ... an agreement ... the purpose or purported purpose of which is to secure a profit or gain to a person who acquires, disposes of, subscribes for or underwrites the Securities or to any of the parties to the agreement in relation to the Securities.
why_it_matters: This second limb sweeps an OTC collar and any associated monetisation agreement into the definition of Dealing, so a designated officer must obtain written approval before signing and cannot sign during a blackout period.

clause: The fact that a blackout period is in place should be treated as confidential information.
why_it_matters: The executive may not be able to explain to the bank why signing, resetting or unwinding must be deferred, although the Company intranet reports daily whether a blackout is in place.

clause: Unless otherwise stated, an approval to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for five business days.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both the collar and the loan must be completed within five business days of approval unless a longer period is specified in the approval itself.

topic: senior managers are not designated officers
clause: For the purposes of this Policy, the following persons are considered to be designated officers: Directors, officers and executives of Codan Limited (and any family member or associate over whom they have influence).
why_it_matters: Senior managers face the blackout periods, the hedging ban and the lender-rights approval requirement but no general dealing pre-approval, so the clearance package differs by tier.

clause: the Company's directors must: notify the Company of any trading in the Company's securities; and notify the market of a substantial shareholding (more than five per cent) or any change(s) in that shareholding.
why_it_matters: A director's collar and the associated pledge will be reportable to the Company and, for substantial holders, may require market disclosure of the change in interest.

clause: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.
why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: the loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for every Non-Executive Director and Senior Executive with no approval route and no vesting carve-out.

topic: conflict from loans over other securities
clause: KMP must also use their best endeavours to ensure they are not put in a position of conflict with this policy by virtue of having margin or other loans over other securities.
why_it_matters: Even a facility secured on a different portfolio must not create a position that could force dealings in AFIC securities, so cross-collateralised or portfolio-wide lending is also constrained.

clause: The section 3 exclusions list contains no exclusion for a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, in contrast to most ASX trading policies.
why_it_matters: Consistent with the outright ban on pledging, there is no mechanism by which a lender's enforcement sale during a prohibited period would fall outside the policy.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested executive equity
clause: Senior Executives are prohibited from using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities they may receive as part of their performance-based remuneration (hedging). Breaches of the Company's policy in this regard will normally result in the termination of the Senior Executive's employment.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban is narrow, covering only unvested performance equity of Senior Executives, so unfunded put and call legs over vested shares are not themselves prohibited, but the penalty for getting the vesting analysis wrong is dismissal.

clause: The policy defines neither 'deal' nor 'securities' and contains no derivatives, encumbrance or agreement-to-deal limbs.
why_it_matters: Whether an OTC option over AFIC shares is a 'dealing' requiring prior notice is left open, so the bank should assume the notification requirements apply and seek confirmation from the Company Secretary.

clause: The Chairman (or in his absence the MD) and either the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) or Company Secretary must be given prior notice of proposed transactions by Directors (including the MD) in the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: Outside a prohibited period the regime is prior notification rather than approval, so if the secured financing ban did not apply the option legs would need only notice and immediate post-trade advice to the Company Secretary.

clause: A KMP ... may request and be given clearance to sell (but not purchase) the Company's securities when they would otherwise be prohibited by this policy from doing so if they are in severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances apply.
why_it_matters: The only relief available is for an outright sale in a prohibited period; it cannot be used to authorise a pledge, a derivative or a purchase leg such as buying a put.

clause: KMP must not deal in the Company's securities during ... the duration of the pricing period for any capital management event.
why_it_matters: For a listed investment company, capital management events such as placements, buy-backs and share purchase plans create unscheduled blackouts on top of the December and June periods, restricting when any structure could be entered, reset or unwound.

clause: KMP may be required annually and from time to time to verify in writing (including by email) that they have complied with this policy.
why_it_matters: A KMP with a secured facility over AFIC shares would have to disclose the breach on their annual certification, making the arrangement impossible to maintain quietly.

topic: express permission to hedge vested shares
clause: Relevant Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities on the following conditions: the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications are made on this basis; and the relevant requirements under paragraphs 4.1 and 4.2 of this Policy have been satisfied.
why_it_matters: This is an express, affirmative permission for the derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares, subject only to the ordinary approval and notification machinery - among the clearest hedging permissions on the ASX.

clause: the hedge transaction must not be entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Relevant Person is in possession of inside information
why_it_matters: Every roll, reset, amendment and unwind of the collar is separately gated, so the documentation must not require the executive to act at a fixed date that could coincide with possession of inside information.

topic: margin lending approval overrides trading windows
clause: Directors and senior executives (including the CEO and CEC) must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 4.1 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
why_it_matters: Approval for the financing leg is required at all times, but the phrase 'irrespective of any trading window' also signals that such approval can be sought and given outside an open window, which helps if the facility must be varied during a blackout.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with 4.3(b) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The Company can dictate the enforcement terms of the bank's facility, for example restricting when collateral may be sold on a margin call, so the credit terms must be agreed with the issuer as well as the borrower.

clause: subject to paragraph 4.3, a disposal of securities of the Company or the securities of Yanzhou that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from paragraphs 3.2 and 4.1 to 4.4].
why_it_matters: Lender enforcement, including during a blackout, is carved out of the blackout and approval rules provided the paragraph 4.3 approval regime was observed, so the bank's security can be enforced without putting the executive in breach.

topic: borrower-side margin call sales are dealings
clause: Such dealings will include: ... selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
why_it_matters: A sale by the executive to meet a margin call is a dealing needing prior approval, so the facility should rely on lender-exercised rights or cash cure rather than obliging the borrower to sell.

clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: Naming forward contracts means a short-dated collar or forward-settled leg risks characterisation as prohibited short-term trading, so tenor should comfortably exceed three months and the exclusions in paragraph 4.5 do not disapply this ban.

clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg in its annual report or to ASX).
why_it_matters: The existence and nature of the collar may be publicly disclosed, so the parties should assume no confidentiality over the structure.

clause: If a waiver is granted, the Relevant Person will be notified in writing (which may include notification via email) and in each circumstance the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 1 business day.
why_it_matters: Any blackout waiver gives only a single business day to price and execute, which is impractical for negotiating a collar, so the transaction must be planned for an open period.

topic: four blackouts a year plus Yanzhou securities
clause: Relevant Persons must not deal in the securities of the Company or Yanzhou Coal Mining Company Limited (Yanzhou) during any of the following blackout periods [31 December, 30 June, 31 March and 30 September, each until the day after the relevant results or quarterly report].
why_it_matters: Quarterly blackouts leave relatively short open periods for entry and unwind, and the same restrictions apply to dealings in the listed parent's securities, which matters if the hedge references Yanzhou rather than Yancoal.

clause: The Relevant Person must undertake the proposed dealing as soon as possible once the notification is provided or approval is granted or such other period specified in the approval. If the dealing is not undertaken within this time, the notification will no longer have effect and new notification or approval will be required.
why_it_matters: There is no fixed validity period, only an 'as soon as possible' standard, so the approval should specify an express window long enough to document and settle the collar and the loan.

topic: short selling defined by economic position
clause: Short selling of Company Securities (that is, entering into a transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities).
why_it_matters: The ban is drafted by economic effect and applies to every Greatland Personnel with no approval route, so the purchased put leg of a collar is arguably a prohibited 'position which would result in profiting from a decline', and the bank should get written confirmation that a covered protective put over shares actually held is not caught before proceeding.

clause: Securities means ... any other equity, debt or derivative instruments, or other linked financial instruments, including instruments to limit the economic risk of other securities held.
why_it_matters: Both collar legs are Securities in their own right with no venue limitation, so entering, amending or terminating the OTC options is itself a Dealing requiring a fresh Dealing Approval at inception, on any roll or reset, and on unwind.

clause: A Dealing Approval under (b) should not be expected to be given to a Restricted Person having regard to the risk of a forced trade in Company Securities as part of the arrangement during a Prohibited Period, and the consequential legal and market reputational risk.
why_it_matters: The loan leg is not banned outright but the Policy tells approvers to refuse it, so a funded collar depends on persuading the Chair that the bank's enforcement and physical-settlement rights are sufficiently constrained to avoid a forced trade in a Prohibited Period.

topic: assignment of rights attaching to shares
clause: any other contractual arrangement where: an entitlement to exercise a right attaching to Company Securities of a Restricted Person is assigned to or is exercisable by another party.
why_it_matters: Standard collar and security documentation that gives the bank voting, dividend or transfer rights over the collared shares is itself a Dealing needing approval, so the security package should leave those rights with the executive until enforcement.

clause: Closed Period means any time which is not a Trading Window or which is a MAR Closed Period. Trading Window means a period in which: in relation to a Director, Company Secretary or other PDMR, a Dealing Approval applies.
why_it_matters: For Directors and PDMRs there is no standing open window at all: the only permitted execution period is the two Business Days of a specific Dealing Approval, which can be shortened in writing at any time, so pricing and signing of every collar step must be compressed into that window.

clause: A Dealing Approval request by a PDMR during a MAR Closed Period or a Prohibited Period will only be granted in exceptional circumstances such as: severe financial hardship which requires the immediate Dealing.
why_it_matters: Between 1 July and the annual results and between 31 December and the half-year results, no collar step by a PDMR can be executed unless it meets the MAR exceptional-circumstances test, which a voluntary financing structure will not.

clause: (The Corporations Act also prohibits such hedging transactions for persons who have authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the entity (including Directors) and their closely related parties.)
why_it_matters: For KMP and their closely related parties the ban on hedging unvested or holding-locked remuneration is statutory as well as contractual, so no company approval could cure a collar over that portion of the holding.

clause: Greatland Personnel must not ... place themselves in a position where it may reasonably be perceived that they have Dealt in Company Securities, other than in compliance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: Reputational perception is an independent breach standard, and Section 5(a)(iii) makes 'adverse reputational imputations' a stated ground for refusing approval, which is a live risk for a publicly disclosable director collar.

clause: Restricted Persons means ... and persons associated with them (including close family; entities, trusts or investment vehicles over which they exercise control or material influence or of which they are a beneficiary; and business or other associates).
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust, SPV or investment vehicle does not avoid the Dealing Approval requirement or the disclosure obligations.

clause: The issue of a Dealing Approval is to be reported to the Board at the next Board meeting. The Company Secretary will maintain a written record of Dealing Approval requests and responses.
why_it_matters: Any approved collar becomes a matter of Board record as well as market disclosure, so the transaction cannot be kept confidential within the company.

clause: All Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.
why_it_matters: This is the only restriction on the loan leg of a funded collar: secured financing over Capricorn shares is permitted outright provided the pledged parcel stays below 3% of the Company's listed shares, so the structure must be sized against issued capital and monitored for buy-backs or capital reductions that could push it through the threshold.

clause: The Policy contains no reference to hedging, limiting economic risk, short selling, securities lending, margin calls or forced sales.
why_it_matters: Neither collar leg is prohibited by the trading policy itself, which is unusually permissive; the bank should instead diligence the equity plan rules and section 206J of the Corporations Act, which are not incorporated into this document.

clause: Key Management Personnel and Directors of the Company must seek approval from the Chairman or Company Secretary prior to any purchase or sale of securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: The approval requirement is not confined to Closed Periods, so entry, roll, reset and unwind of the collar each need the Chairman's or Company Secretary's prior approval, with no stated validity period, response time or revocation mechanism.

clause: from the end of each quarter until the commencement of trading on the second business day after the Company's Quarterly Report is released; from four weeks prior to the release of the Company's full year and half year financial results until the second business day after the financial results are released.
why_it_matters: As a quarterly-reporting miner the Company is closed for the whole gap between each quarter end and its quarterly report, on top of the four-week pre-results windows, leaving only short and irregular execution windows for pricing a collar.

topic: derivatives brought in by scope, not by rule
clause: This Policy applies to the following securities: ... derivatives and other financial products issued or created over or in respect of Capricorn securities.
why_it_matters: The OTC put and call are within the Policy's scope even though no clause addresses derivatives, so both legs are subject to the Closed Period and pre-approval regime but to no substantive prohibition.

clause: The Restricted Person must satisfy the Chairman that the circumstances are exceptional and that the proposed sale or disposal of the securities is the only reasonable course of action available to them.
why_it_matters: There is no route to execute any collar step inside a Closed Period for a voluntary financing transaction, since the waiver requires the disposal to be the only reasonable course of action.

clause: The Policy does not address margin calls, forced sales by a financier, or sales by a third party outside the executive's control.
why_it_matters: Enforcement or physical settlement by the bank during a Closed Period is not expressly a breach, but nor is it expressly excluded, so the position should be documented with the Chairman in advance rather than assumed.

clause: Reports of any breaches of the Policy will be forwarded to the Audit and Risk Management Committee. ... Strict compliance with the policy is a condition of employment.
why_it_matters: Any mis-step in approving or disclosing the collar is escalated to a board committee and can be treated as a termination event, so the paper trail of approvals should be complete before execution.

clause: Directors, Senior Executives, employees and consultants of TPG Telecom may take out margin loans over their vested holdings in TPG Telecom's Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is expressly permitted rather than banned, provided it is secured only over vested holdings; this is one of the few ASX policies that affirmatively allows a director to encumber shares.

clause: However, Directors, Senior Executives, employees and consultants must not allow a margin call to be met by the sale of TPG Telecom's Securities at a time when they would not be able to sell those Securities themselves under this Policy.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement and physical settlement rights must be drafted so that no sale of the collared shares can occur outside a Window Period or during an ad hoc closed period without the executive first obtaining written acknowledgement, otherwise the executive breaches the Policy through the lender's own action.

clause: The details of the Security Arrangements which must be provided must include the number of Securities of TPG Telecom involved, any trigger points, the right of the lender or security holder to sell the Securities unilaterally and any other material details.
why_it_matters: Commercial terms of the facility, including margin triggers and the bank's unilateral sale rights, must be handed to the Chairperson or CEO at inception and on every non-trivial amendment, and may be announced to the market under Listing Rule 3.1.

clause: Written acknowledgement is intended as a compliance monitoring function only and is not an endorsement of the proposed transaction. Individuals remain responsible for their compliance with the law.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot treat the designated officer's acknowledgement as company sign-off on the collar's legality, so it should obtain its own confirmation on insider information and plan-rule compliance.

clause: Directors and Senior Executives are only permitted to deal in TPG Telecom's Securities during a one month period following the release of TPG Telecom's half yearly and annual results ... and TPG Telecom's Annual General Meeting.
why_it_matters: This is a closed-by-default policy with only three one-month windows a year, so collar entry, roll and unwind must be scheduled into those windows or justified as Exceptional Circumstances.

clause: Outside the Window Period, Directors and Senior Executives may in certain circumstances (for example, Exceptional Circumstances) trade in TPG Telecom's Securities following written acknowledgement in accordance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: The annexed form requires details of the Exceptional Circumstances, so a voluntary financing transaction is unlikely to be executable outside a window.

clause: Securities include shares of any class, options, bonds, derivatives, managed investments and superannuation products and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.
why_it_matters: Derivatives are listed expressly, but the closing words 'able to be traded on a financial market' could be argued to confine the definition to exchange-traded products, leaving it unclear whether a bilateral OTC put and call are Securities for Policy purposes; confirm the company's view before relying on either reading.

clause: Directors and Senior Executives must not deal in TPG Telecom's Securities for short term gain. Short term means a period of three months or less.
why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any early unwind should exceed three months, and the structure should not be characterised as dealing for short term gain.

clause: The Policy contains no hedging prohibition, no restriction on hedging unvested or holding-locked equity, and no short-selling prohibition.
why_it_matters: Neither collar leg is prohibited by the trading policy itself; the constraints on hedging unvested incentive securities would have to come from the plan rules and section 206J of the Corporations Act, which are outside this document.

clause: it may lead to disciplinary action being taken against the person, including disposal of any TPG Telecom Securities acquired in breach of this Policy and/or dismissal in serious cases.
why_it_matters: A breach can trigger forced disposal of the underlying shares, which would cut across a collar and the bank's security position.

clause: Directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants) must also not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities.
why_it_matters: This is the only substantive obstacle to a collar: it bites only on unvested Securities, so a collar over fully vested shares is not prohibited, but the collared parcel must be strictly segregated from any unvested performance rights or options.

topic: notification is not approval but carries a veto
clause: Notification of any trade and completion of Part B of a Trade Notification Form does not constitute approval by or on behalf of Ramelius for the relevant trade. ... the Chairman ... must ... either complete Part B ... or direct the director/officer/employee that the trade should not be undertaken. A director/officer/employee must comply with the direction given.
why_it_matters: The bank gets no company approval it can rely on, but the Chairman holds an unqualified veto with no criteria, no response deadline and no stated validity period for a completed Part B, so timing risk on pricing the collar sits with the executive.

clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin loans, margin calls, security interests, encumbrances, forced sales, short selling, securities lending or short-term trading.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is unregulated by this policy, but that silence cuts both ways: there is no framework permitting or disclosing the financing and no protection against the bank's enforcement sale falling in a blackout period, so the position should be documented with the Chairman up front.

clause: The Company's Securities ... include any financial or associated product issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: A bank-issued OTC put and call over Ramelius shares are the Company's Securities for Policy purposes, so entering into, and later unwinding, each leg is a trade needing a Trade Notification Form and Chairman sign-off outside a blackout.

topic: frequent blackouts for a quarterly reporter
clause: during the period between the end of the Company's full financial year and the announcement of the Company's full year financial results ... during the period between the end of the Company's half year and the announcement of the Company's half year financial results ... during the one week period immediately prior to the lodgement of the Company's quarterly activity reports.
why_it_matters: The full-year and half-year blackouts run from period end to results announcement, which can be six to eight weeks each, and every quarterly report adds a further week, materially narrowing the dates on which a collar can be struck or rolled.

clause: the Board of Directors may determine that there are specific periods when directors, officers and employees are permitted to deal ... The Board of Directors may from time to time amend this trading policy or may extend or shorten a permitted period for dealing.
why_it_matters: Dealing windows are defined by Board determination rather than by fixed anchors and can be shortened at will, so a scheduled roll or unwind of the collar can be blocked at short notice.

clause: The discretion may only be exercised before a trade in the Company's Securities and not after the event.
why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security or the collar physically settles during a prohibited period, the breach cannot be cured retrospectively, so settlement mechanics must be conditioned on prior notification.

clause: Directors, officers, employees (including regular consultants) must take reasonable steps to prohibit dealing in the Company's Securities by immediate family and companies, trusts or other entities over which the director, officer, employee and regular consultant or immediate family member has control.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the Policy, and the obligation is framed as taking reasonable steps to prohibit their dealing altogether.

clause: No Director or Employee may enter into any ... derivative agreements in respect of any Relevant Mirvac Securities.
why_it_matters: This single limb defeats a collar on its own: it is not confined to unvested or plan securities, not confined to exchange-traded products, and carries no clearance route, so both the purchased put and the written call are prohibited even over fully vested shares.

topic: enter into or maintain secured financing
clause: No Director or Employee may enter into, or maintain, any loan or other financial arrangement under which security rights over Mirvac Relevant Securities are granted to a third party.
why_it_matters: The loan leg is separately and absolutely prohibited, and the word 'maintain' means an arrangement entered into before appointment or before the policy must be unwound rather than simply run off.

clause: Special Circumstances and the Approving Officers' consent operate only as exceptions to the Trading Window requirement in section 2; section 6 contains no equivalent discretion.
why_it_matters: There is no person or committee who can approve the structure, so a funded collar cannot be rescued by disclosure, board approval or hardship, only by a change to the policy itself.

clause: Dealing includes ... arranging, granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of Securities.
why_it_matters: Even setting aside 6.2(c), writing the call and later exercising or discharging either leg are each separate Dealings requiring their own approval inside a Trading Window.

topic: five business day approval and automatic lapse
clause: An approval must ... not be for a period of more than 5 business days ... An approval lapses immediately and without further notification if a Director or Employee to whom an approval has been given acquires Inside Information or if a Trading Window closes.
why_it_matters: Any permitted transaction must be instructed within five business days and dies instantly if the window closes or inside information arises, which is unworkable for a multi-leg structure requiring simultaneous pricing and documentation.

topic: settlement may fall outside the window
clause: once the instruction to trade has been placed, the Dealing may settle outside of the Trading Window or approval period.
why_it_matters: The only timing relief in the policy: settlement mechanics can run past a window provided the instruction was given inside it, which would matter for a physically settled structure if the substantive prohibitions did not already apply.

clause: In considering whether to approve, the Approving Officers may take into account future matters, plans and intentions of the Mirvac Group. ... No reason will be given for the grant or refusal of approval to Deal. A Director or Employee must keep confidential whether their request to Deal is approved or not approved.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot be told why an approval was refused or even that it was sought, so execution risk on any permitted dealing cannot be diligenced from the company side.

clause: Where this policy places a restriction on a Director or Employee in Dealing in Relevant Mirvac Securities, the Director or Employee must not knowingly allow a Dealing in Relevant Mirvac Securities by any of its Associates. ... An Associate of the Director or Employee must not Deal in Relevant Mirvac Securities without approval being obtained in accordance with this policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the loan through a family trust, controlled company, an entity where the executive is an officer, or an investment manager does not avoid any of the section 6 prohibitions.

clause: No Director or Employee may Deal in Relevant Mirvac Securities or options or derivatives over Relevant Mirvac Securities on considerations of a short-term nature (being a period of 6 months or less).
why_it_matters: The short-term test is six months rather than the usual three and expressly names options and derivatives, so even a permitted option strategy would need a tenor well beyond six months.

clause: The Mirvac Group may, at any time, declare additional trading windows or trading blackouts, or vary or cancel any existing trading windows or trading blackouts in Relevant Mirvac Securities at any time at its discretion and without prior notice if considered necessary.
why_it_matters: Windows can be cancelled without notice, voiding any outstanding Notice of Intention to Deal, so no execution date can be relied on in advance.

topic: collars named in the derivative definition
clause: Derivatives includes derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars) and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: A collar is expressly within scope, so both legs are Dealings and the substance test catches any economically equivalent structure, but nothing prohibits a collar over vested shares.

clause: Directors and Executives must obtain the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer ... before entering into any scheme, arrangement or agreement ... under which the relevant Director or Executive may alter the economic benefit or risk they derive in relation to any JB Hi-Fi Securities (whether received under an equity-based incentive award scheme or otherwise).
why_it_matters: The collar is available to Directors and Executives over vested and on-market shares but only on a wholly discretionary approval that may be refused without reasons and revoked before execution.

topic: voluntary public disclosure of hedges and loans
clause: JB Hi-Fi may publicly disclose this information irrespective of whether it is technically required by law or the ASX Listing Rules.
why_it_matters: Both the collar and the secured loan may be announced to the market even where no legal disclosure obligation exists, so the client cannot rely on confidentiality.

clause: Directors and Executives may not include their JB Hi-Fi Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement ... without first obtaining the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer.
why_it_matters: Unusually, the loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted subject to approval and disclosure rather than prohibited, so a funded structure is achievable.

clause: Any approval given under section 3.22 by the Relevant Company Officer will be valid for a period of 5 trading days, commencing on the date it is given.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both the collar and the loan must complete within 5 trading days of each approval or fresh approval is needed.

clause: Any approval given may be revoked in writing (including by email) by the Relevant Company Officer prior to Dealing taking place if new information comes to light, or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: The bank faces execution risk that a signed but unsettled collar or drawdown is withdrawn at short notice.

clause: Key Persons ... may not therefore Deal in the same JB Hi-Fi Securities within any 6 month period.
why_it_matters: Collar tenor, rolls, partial unwinds and any sale of the collared parcel should be spaced at least six months apart, since each is a Dealing in the same Securities.

clause: Any restriction on Dealing in JB Hi-Fi Securities during a Trading Window which is notified by the Company to all or particular Key Persons or other Employees is a confidential matter which must not be disclosed.
why_it_matters: The client may be unable to tell the bank why a scheduled entry, roll or physical settlement cannot proceed, so the documentation must tolerate silent postponement.

clause: No Key Person may enter into any scheme, arrangement or agreement ... under which the relevant Key Person may alter the economic benefit or risk derived by the Key Person, in relation to an unvested equity-based incentive award or grant.
why_it_matters: Only vested and exercisable holdings can be collared; the bank must verify vesting and exercisability before sizing the trade, as there is no approval route for unvested awards.

clause: Employees should ensure that any Securities trading which is prohibited by this Policy is not undertaken by: their spouse, partner or child; ... a company or trust over which the Employee has influence or control (regardless of who is the beneficiary) including any self managed superannuation fund.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or loan through a family trust, SMSF or controlled company does not avoid the approval and disclosure requirements.

topic: no relief for shares under option plans
clause: This may prevent, for example, Key Persons selling, and realising the value of, shares resulting from the exercise of options under a JB Hi-Fi Option Plan at a particular time, even though the Plan rules would otherwise allow this.
why_it_matters: Physical settlement of the collar out of plan shares can be blocked by a Prohibited Period notwithstanding the plan rules, so cash settlement or a delivery grace period should be provided for.

clause: Sections 15, 19 and 25 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares is expressly outside the blackout, prior approval and short-term trading rules, so lender remedies survive even in a closed period.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 32 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The Company can dictate LVR or sale-trigger terms as a condition of approving the loan, so the facility terms must be agreed with the Company before the bank commits.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A collar cannot be structured around the unvested hedging ban or the margin lending approval by relabelling the instrument or using a Connected Person.

clause: Where any approval is required for trading under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the trade would not satisfy the test set out in section 9 above.
why_it_matters: Approval of the collar can be refused purely on perception grounds, independently of inside information or blackouts, and the approver need not give reasons.

clause: During any period that is not a blackout period under section 15, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed trade, obtain written approval for the proposed trade of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: There is no free trading window at all: entry, roll, partial unwind and physical settlement of the collar each need fresh written approval, valid for only 7 days.

clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time.
why_it_matters: Approval can be withdrawn after the term sheet is agreed but before execution, creating settlement risk for the bank.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade Company securities during ... the period from 4.00pm (Sydney time) on 31 March each year until the day following the release to the ASX of the March Quarterly Report.
why_it_matters: Quarterly as well as half and full year blackouts leave short and irregular open periods, so collar entry and any scheduled roll must be timed around four blackouts plus any Board-imposed period.

clause: Restricted Persons must take reasonable steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only trade securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to trade under this Policy.
why_it_matters: A collar booked through a spouse, family trust or controlled company must itself be cleared, so the counterparty entity does not avoid the approval requirement.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into hedging arrangements over any unvested Company securities (including equity incentives issued under the Company's Equity Incentive Plan) to which they may be entitled.
why_it_matters: Sizing must be limited to vested holdings, and the wording 'to which they may be entitled' extends the ban to unvested rights and future entitlements, not just issued shares.

clause: the Company has notified the Restricted Persons that they must not trade securities (either for a specified period, or until the Company gives further notice).
why_it_matters: An open-ended trading ban can be imposed at any time and may block delivery or unwind indefinitely, so the collar documentation needs a settlement deferral mechanism.

clause: If a Designated Person wishes to enter an arrangement where Argo securities are held as collateral for a loan facility, they must notify by email the approval group comprising the Chairman, Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, Managing Director and Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar needs only notification, not consent, which is materially easier than the approval regimes in most ASX policies.

clause: in order that the Board can ascertain whether the arrangement is material, and if required, the Company will disclose the key terms of the arrangement to the market pursuant to the ASX continuous disclosure requirements.
why_it_matters: The key commercial terms of the facility, potentially including LVR and trigger levels, may be published to the market, so confidentiality cannot be assured to the borrower or the bank.

clause: This Policy does not apply to Designated Persons in the following circumstances: ... Disposal of securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by Argo securities or by the securities of other companies
why_it_matters: An enforcement or margin call sale by the bank is outside the Policy entirely, so it can occur in a prohibited period without breach and needs no clearance.

clause: Designated Persons seeking to enter a transaction or arrangement to limit the economic risk of their Argo security holding must obtain approval in the same way as if they traded in the underlying securities directly.
why_it_matters: The derivative legs need email approval from the Chairman, Managing Director and Company Secretary group and must be executed within five trading days and outside prohibited periods.

clause: The Company prohibits hedging of unvested Argo securities, such as performance rights awarded under an executive incentive share scheme.
why_it_matters: Only vested holdings may be collared, and unvested performance rights cannot be counted towards the collared parcel.

clause: All approval requests are to be emailed to the entire approval group, with any one of the group able to grant approval.
why_it_matters: Clearance is administratively quick, but approval can also be withdrawn within the five trading day window, creating execution risk before pricing.

clause: The Company may from time to time impose additional periods when trading is prohibited, such as ... If it has orders in the market for its own securities due to the activation of an on-market share buy-back or pursuant to any of the Company's employee incentive schemes.
why_it_matters: As an LIC that regularly buys back its own shares, Argo can impose additional prohibited periods at short notice, so collar entry, roll and physical settlement dates need flexibility.

clause: Designated Persons must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Closely Connected Persons also comply with this Policy.
why_it_matters: A collar or facility booked through a family trust or controlled company is subject to the same approval and notification obligations.

topic: exceptional circumstances relief is sale only
clause: may request and be given clearance to sell (but not purchase) Argo securities in circumstances otherwise prohibited by this Policy
why_it_matters: During a prohibited period the executive can be cleared to sell but not to buy, so a collar unwind requiring a repurchase leg or a cash-settled buy-back of the put cannot rely on hardship relief.

topic: hedging of vested options is notification only
clause: Where a director or senior executive enters into arrangements for the hedging of vested options granted under the Company's employee equity scheme, details of the hedging arrangements must be immediately notified to the Chairman or Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: Hedging vested holdings is expressly contemplated and requires only immediate disclosure of details, not consent, so the derivative legs are achievable.

clause: The Policy contains no margin lending, secured financing or encumbrance provision; the only reference is the exclusion of 'a disposal of securities that is a result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example, under a margin loan arrangement'.
why_it_matters: The loan secured on the collared shares is neither prohibited nor subject to approval or notification, and lender enforcement is expressly outside the Policy even in a closed period.

clause: have been advised by the Chairman that there is no reason to preclude them from trading in the Company's securities as notified
why_it_matters: Clearance is a discretionary Chairman confirmation with no stated validity period, response time or revocation rule, so the bank should fix its own execution deadline in the term sheet.

clause: have complied with any conditions on trading imposed by the Chairman (including, for example, any time limits applicable to the clearance).
why_it_matters: The Chairman can attach conditions, including volume or timing limits, that may cut across the hedge ratio or execution schedule agreed with the bank.

clause: in the two weeks prior to the release of the Company's quarterly reports and for 1 business day after the release of the report
why_it_matters: With two week quarterly and four week half and full year blackouts, open windows are short and irregular for a quarterly reporting miner, so entry and roll dates must be planned around them.

clause: the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their respective associated parties trading in Company securities at any time.
why_it_matters: An unqualified embargo can be imposed at any time and extends to family trusts and companies, so it can block collar entry, roll or physical settlement without notice.

clause: Short-term trading is a purchase and sale of the same securities within a period between one to six months.
why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any unwind or re-hedge involving the same securities should exceed six months, and there is no carve-out for plan share sales as there is in many policies.

topic: closed period relief is sale only
clause: In exceptional circumstances clearance may be given for a Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities when they would otherwise be prohibited from doing so
why_it_matters: A closed period unwind requiring a purchase, such as buying back a written call, cannot be cleared even for hardship.

clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her associated parties (being immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust) complies with the same respective restrictions.
why_it_matters: A collar or facility booked through a family company or trust attracts the same clearance and notification obligations as one in the executive's own name.

clause: arrangements for the hedging of vested options granted under the Company's employee equity scheme
why_it_matters: The notification clause is drafted around vested plan options rather than ordinary shares, so the treatment of a collar over shares held outright rests on the general trading clearance rather than an express permission.

clause: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg is the problem: if the facility secured on the collared shares is characterised as a margin lending arrangement it is flatly prohibited for Directors, Senior Executives and Nominated Employees, with no approval route.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A facility documented as a term loan rather than a margin loan will still be assessed on its substance, so LVR tests, top-up rights and enforcement over the shares make the section 5.2 ban likely to bite.

clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: A short-dated collar or forward leg can itself be a prohibited short-term dealing, so tenor should comfortably exceed 90 days and early termination rights should be limited.

clause: Company securities held by a Restricted Person must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan.
why_it_matters: Vesting alone is not enough: shares still under a plan holding lock cannot be collared, so the bank must diligence lock status as well as vesting.

clause: Sections 4.3, 4.4 and 5.1 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
why_it_matters: If a compliant secured facility could be put in place, enforcement sales sit outside the blackout and approval rules, though this carve-out cannot cure the margin lending prohibition itself.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even an otherwise compliant collar over vested shares can be refused on perception grounds alone, and the approver need not give reasons.

clause: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.4, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: There is no free trading window: entry, roll, partial unwind and physical settlement each need fresh written approval, valid only 5 business days.

clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: Approval can be withdrawn after pricing is agreed and the client cannot explain why, so the documentation must tolerate silent withdrawal before settlement.

clause: Employees must not deal in Company securities: from the close of trading on the ASX on 30 September each year until the day after the announcement to ASX of the full year results ... from the close of trading on the ASX on 31 March each year until the day after the announcement to ASX of the half-year results.
why_it_matters: The blackouts follow a 30 September financial year end, and approval is described as more likely only in the 4 weeks after each results release, so execution should be scheduled into those windows.

clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Booking the structure through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not escape the margin lending ban or the clearance requirement.

clause: The windows trading policy means that trading in both securities and derivatives of Atlas Arteria can only occur at the discretion of the ATLAX and ATLIX Boards during the four week window commencing after: the release of annual and half yearly results; the Annual General Meeting; and lodgement with ASIC or ASX of a disclosure document or a cleansing statement for a capital raising.
why_it_matters: There is no default open period: every leg of a collar (entry, roll, unwind, physical settlement) must be executed inside a Board-opened four week window that may be withheld or shut without notice.

clause: ATLAX and ATLIX directors along with the CEO and direct reports to the CEO, must not enter into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements over their Atlas Arteria Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is expressly prohibited for directors, the CEO and CEO direct reports, but the ban does not reach Staff below that level.

clause: Directors and Staff must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Atlas Arteria securities, or in derivative or other financial products issued over or in respect of Atlas Arteria securities. Short term means a term of less than a six month period.
why_it_matters: A collar must have a term of at least six months and must not be structured with early unwind or knock-out features that make it short term or speculative in substance.

clause: In the case of ATLAX and ATLIX directors, the CEO and direct reports to the CEO, they are expected to not actively trade in Atlas Arteria securities and if they wish to sell must also pre-clear these trades through the ATLAX or ATLIX Chair (as relevant).
why_it_matters: Even where a structure is technically permitted, the senior group is expected to be inactive, so a bank should assume any derivative programme for them attracts Chair-level scrutiny.

clause: If pre-clearance is given for a specific transaction, then the order must be placed and executed within three trading days following the granting of the pre-clearance. Any part of the order that is not actioned within this time must be pre-cleared again or cancelled.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both collar legs must complete inside three trading days of clearance or the clearance must be sought again.

clause: A pre-clearance can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. Any pre-clearance to trade can be given or refused by the clearer in their discretion, without giving any reasons. A decision to refuse pre-clearance is final and binding.
why_it_matters: A bank cannot rely on a granted clearance surviving to settlement, and there is no appeal if clearance for an unwind or settlement is refused.

clause: Staff who hold unvested or restricted Atlas Arteria securities must ... not enter into any transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested or restricted securities. This includes not entering any transaction to manage the risk of the timing, likelihood or manner of vesting, or unrestricted vesting.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban is limited to unvested or restricted securities, so a collar over vested unrestricted shares is not caught by it; but the collar must not be sized so that it economically covers unvested awards as well.

clause: Trades in Atlas Arteria ... are prohibited for Atlas Arteria Staff and their Associates, as defined above, outside of the designated trading windows.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust, SMSF, controlled company or spouse does not escape the windows, pre-clearance or (for directors and the CEO group) the secured financing ban.

clause: ATLAX and ATLIX directors are required to acquire and maintain a minimum holding of Atlas Arteria Securities which equates to one year of the base non-executive director fee.
why_it_matters: Directors must keep an unencumbered-equivalent holding, and the policy is silent on whether collared or pledged shares count towards it, so the bank should assume shares delivered under the collar reduce compliance.

clause: The policy contains no provision dealing with sales by a third party (such as a lender) outside the holder's control, and no exemption other than exceptional circumstances.
why_it_matters: If a financier ever sold collared shares outside a window there is no excluded-dealing safe harbour, and the holder would need a written exceptional-circumstances exemption from the Company Secretary and CEO (and Chairs).

clause: Designated Persons and their Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Steadfast's Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is expressly prohibited for every director, KMP and designated person and their Associates, with no clearance route.

clause: Designated Persons and their Associates are not permitted to engage in short selling or stock lending of Steadfast's Securities.
why_it_matters: Structures in which the executive lends the collared shares to the bank to support its hedge, or the bank borrows them back, are separately prohibited.

clause: A Designated Person may request, and the Notification Officer may give, prior confirmation for the Designated Person or their Associate to: a) deal in Steadfast's Securities outside a trading window; or b) dispose of Steadfast's Securities even if otherwise prohibited under part 6.
why_it_matters: The only relief from part 6 is to dispose of shares, so it cannot be used to authorise entering into a secured loan, a hedge, stock lending or a short-dated collar.

clause: The Board may, in its discretion, adjust or exclude a specific requirement of this policy from time to time, either generally or on a case by case basis.
why_it_matters: This is the only realistic route to a funded collar: the Board would have to disapply the margin lending and stock lending prohibitions for the specific transaction.

clause: (lender disposals) disposals of Steadfast's Securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposals under any margin lending agreement where such agreements are prohibited by this policy.
why_it_matters: A secured lender's enforcement sale is a permitted dealing in principle, but the carve-back withdraws that protection for any facility the policy itself prohibits, so a bank enforcing against a Designated Person's collared shares gets no safe harbour.

topic: OTC derivatives arguably outside the clearance regime
clause: shares, options, derivatives and any other financial products of Steadfast that are able to be traded on a financial market ("Steadfast's Securities") ... financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Steadfast's Securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: The window and clearance machinery bites on 'Steadfast's Securities', which is qualified by tradability on a financial market, while the wider 'financial products' definition that plainly captures an OTC collar is used only in the short term trading ban; the gap is arguable rather than reliable, so a bank should still require clearance.

clause: (off market) off-market transfers of Steadfast Securities, other than those by the Board Directors and their Associates, where there is no change in beneficial ownership.
why_it_matters: For directors, moving collateral shares into a lender's nominee or custodian account is not an excluded dealing even if beneficial ownership is unchanged, so it needs an open window and clearance.

clause: Designated Persons and their Associates must not engage in short term trading in Steadfast's Securities or in financial products associated with Steadfast's Securities. Buying and selling Steadfast's Securities within a 3 month period is considered short term trading.
why_it_matters: The tenor of any collar must exceed three months and it must not be unwound early, because the ban expressly reaches associated financial products.

clause: must not enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: a) has not vested; or b) has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: The 'with anyone' and 'could have the effect' wording is broad but the ban is limited to unvested or holding-locked remuneration, leaving vested unrestricted shares hedgeable.

clause: Designated Persons will be notified of trading windows by email prior to the opening of a trading window. Designated Persons must not assume that a trading window is open in the absence of notification, as the Board may vary, suspend or terminate (conditionally or unconditionally) trading window arrangements at any time.
why_it_matters: Execution certainty is low: a window can be suspended between pricing and signing, and there is no default open period.

clause: Designated Persons must keep for 12 months and make available to the Company Secretary on request, a record of all dealings in Steadfast's Securities by themselves and their Associates, in the form of a record of every trade, including any supporting materials.
why_it_matters: Collar documentation and confirmations would be discoverable by the Company Secretary for at least 12 months.

topic: hedging over vested securities expressly permitted
clause: once Challenger Securities have vested, derivatives or hedging may be used in relation to those vested Securities in the following circumstances: to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by Challenger; to protect the value of the security where the staff member had paid or is required to pay a tax liability in relation to the vested Securities; on a case by case basis with approval from the Committee.
why_it_matters: This is one of the few ASX policies that positively contemplates hedging vested shares, and the first limb even contemplates a hedge protecting an asset that supports a loan; a collar over vested shares can therefore be approved on a case by case basis by the Committee.

clause: neither Challenger nor any member of the Challenger Group can be a counter party to the derivative.
why_it_matters: The bank writing the collar must not be a Challenger Group entity, which is straightforward for a third party bank but excludes any Challenger-issued structured product.

clause: the derivative or hedge must not have a maturity date that falls within a closed prohibited period.
why_it_matters: The collar's expiry must be scheduled outside the 30 June to results and 31 December to results closed periods, and rolling or early termination must be planned around dates that can shift when the Boards vary closed period timing.

clause: Challenger prohibits margin lending over Challenger Securities other than as approved by the Challenger Board.
why_it_matters: The loan leg is not an absolute bar as it is in most ASX policies: the Challenger Board can approve margin lending over CGF securities, so a funded collar turns on obtaining that Board approval alongside Committee approval of the hedge.

clause: As a general principle, staff are prohibited from holding net short positions in Challenger Securities through derivative instruments or otherwise.
why_it_matters: The collar must be sized no larger than the shares actually held, since an over-hedged position or a written call in excess of the holding would create a net short position.

clause: Shares, securities, interests in a managed investment scheme including mFund units, options, stock specific derivatives, derivatives (both over the counter (OTC) and exchange traded), warrants, contracts for difference (CFDs) ... It also includes security specific derivatives, options, Contracts for Difference (CFDs) and warrants that may be issued by third parties where the underlying or referenced security is Securities issued by Challenger.
why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so both collar legs written by a bank are Challenger Securities requiring pre-trade approval and subject to the Prohibited Periods.

topic: prohibited periods framed around quoted securities
clause: There are periods throughout the year during which Challenger staff are not permitted to trade in Challenger Securities which are quoted on a relevant stock exchange irrespective of whether or not they are in possession of inside information.
why_it_matters: The Prohibited Period wording is expressed by reference to quoted securities, but 7.6.2 assumes derivatives are subject to closed periods, so a bank should not rely on an argument that OTC legs escape the blackout.

clause: Approved trades must be placed within 1 business day and complete within 7 days, unless otherwise informed by the Company Secretary. Once the approval lapses, re-approval to trade will be required.
why_it_matters: The collar must be placed within one business day of approval and completed within seven days, though the Company Secretary can vary this, which is likely necessary for a negotiated OTC structure.

clause: Any approval to trade can be granted or refused in the Company's absolute discretion, without providing any reasons. An approval to trade may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. Any refusal to trade is final and binding on you, and you must keep that information confidential.
why_it_matters: Approval to enter, roll or unwind the collar can be withdrawn between pricing and execution, with no appeal and no reasons given.

clause: You must not do indirectly what you are prohibited from doing directly.
why_it_matters: A term loan secured on CGF shares that is economically a margin loan, or a synthetic short achieved through combined legs, will be treated as caught even if the label differs.

topic: forced sale carve-out sits in the third party rules
clause: Forced sales or acquisitions as a result of margin lending calls or corporate actions ... which do not accommodate personal discretion are not subject to pre-trade approval for Designated Staff.
why_it_matters: The only forced-sale relief appears in section 8 (Third Party Securities) and is expressed for Designated Staff, so it is unclear whether a lender's enforcement sale of CGF shares in a Prohibited Period is protected.

clause: A staff member's ownership or power in Securities may be acquired through closely connected persons and entities including a related party or controlled entity such as an immediate family member or companies and trusts including self-managed superannuation funds.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust, SMSF or controlled company is treated as the staff member's own personal trading and needs the same approvals.

clause: Version 10, Date of Version November 2018, Review of Policy Due by November 2019.
why_it_matters: The lodged policy is dated November 2018 and was due for review in November 2019, so the bank should confirm no more recent version has superseded these unusually permissive hedging provisions.

clause: All Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in IGO securities where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.
why_it_matters: The only hard limit on the loan leg is a size test measured against IGO's whole issued capital rather than the individual's holding, so a normal executive funded collar sits comfortably below it, but the bank must size the security package against 3% of listed shares.

topic: secured financing permitted with prior approval
clause: Without prior approval, directors and senior management should not enter into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in IGO securities (such as the disposal of some or all of those IGO securities) if a secured lender exercises their rights (for example, under a margin lending or secured financing arrangement).
why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this permits margin lending and secured financing outright subject to prior approval, so the loan leg of a funded collar is achievable for directors and senior management.

clause: a disposal that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, where the director or senior manager has already received prior written clearance for the original financing arrangement in accordance with this Standard.
why_it_matters: Enforcement or physical settlement by the bank is an excluded dealing even in a blackout period, provided the facility itself was pre-cleared in writing, which gives the bank certainty it lacks under most other policies.

clause: or entering into forward contracts, or short selling at any time, except in circumstances of special hardship, with the Chair's prior written approval (email suffices).
why_it_matters: A prepaid variable forward or any forward-sale leg is prohibited outright, so the structure must be built from a purchased put and a written call rather than a forward.

clause: All Personnel are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of holding unvested entitlements, or entitlements that are subject to a holding lock or similar deal restriction under the terms of any employee, executive or director equity plan.
why_it_matters: The collar may only cover shares that have vested and are free of any plan holding lock; nothing in the Standard restricts hedging vested unrestricted shares.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could I be perceived to be taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? How would it look if it was reported on the front page of the newspaper? ... Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Standard, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: A reputational overlay sits above every approval, so a large executive collar can be refused purely on how it would read publicly even if technically compliant.

clause: any other period imposed by the Board from time to time (Additional Period). Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: The executive cannot tell the bank why a trade date must move, so documentation should allow the client to defer without explanation.

clause: Any written clearance granted under this Standard will be valid for five business days from the time which it is given or such other period as may be determined ... A clearance to deal can be withdrawn at any time. The decision to refuse the clearance is final and binding.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar must complete within five business days of clearance, and the clearance can be pulled at any point before dealing.

clause: NATURE OF TRANSACTION (Specify precisely, e.g.: sale of shares) ... Permission given on the basis that the transaction is completed by no later than close of business on ...
why_it_matters: Each leg and the financing must be described precisely on the Appendix 1 form and completed by the stated deadline, so a multi-leg collar needs a carefully drafted single application.

clause: a company or any other entity which the Personnel has an ability to control, including a family trust or superannuation fund, including pursuant to standing orders to trade. Where this Standard requires Personnel to do an act or thing (for example, obtaining written clearance), the relevant Personnel must do that act or thing in respect of the associate.
why_it_matters: A collar booked in a family trust or SMSF needs the same clearance obtained by the executive on the entity's behalf.

clause: Group Governance Standard 7 Dealing in Securities, date 24/06/2019, to be reviewed annually by the IGO Board of Directors.
why_it_matters: The lodged Standard dates from 2019 under the company's former name Independence Group NL, so the bank should confirm the current version before relying on the permissive financing provisions.

clause: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.
why_it_matters: This is the only financing control in the policy: a funded collar is permissible for directors and KMP provided the security package stays below 3% of Regis's listed shares, with no approval, disclosure or condition otherwise imposed.

clause: The policy contains no hedging clause, no derivatives clause, no short selling clause and no definition of dealing, trading or securities.
why_it_matters: Neither collar leg is expressly restricted, but the absence of drafting also means there is no clearance mechanism through which a bank can obtain company comfort that the structure is compliant.

topic: restrictions framed as buying or selling
clause: All Restricted Persons are prohibited from buying or selling Company securities: in the 14 day period prior to the release of the half yearly results announcement to ASX ...
why_it_matters: The closed periods are expressed as a bar on buying or selling Company securities, so on a literal reading entering an OTC option with a bank is not caught, though physical settlement or a collateral transfer plainly would be.

clause: The Company Secretary will endeavour to notify all Directors, employees and any other Restricted Persons of the times when they are permitted to buy or sell the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: There is no pre-clearance requirement for ordinary dealing, only notification of permitted times, so a bank cannot rely on a company approval as evidence the structure was sanctioned.

clause: The notification must also specify whether the trading took place during a closed period, where prior written clearance was required, and if so, when that was provided.
why_it_matters: The ASX notification clause assumes a prior written clearance process that the policy never establishes outside the exceptional circumstances route, so the practical process should be confirmed with the Company Secretary.

clause: All directors and Key Management Personnel must complete a Trading Notification form and provide it to the Company Secretary within 2 days after that person buys or sells securities in the Company. The Trading Notification form must be completed in full, including details of the number of securities traded, the date the trading took place and whether the trading occurred inside a closed period.
why_it_matters: Any physical delivery or on-market leg of the collar triggers a two day notification and, for directors, a Company ASX filing within five business days if relevant interests change.

clause: there exists information regarding definition drilling, resource or reserve upgrades or new discoveries or the awarding of any major contract or relating to other activities such as those set out in clause 3.5 of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Exploration and resource news flow creates frequent open-ended trading bars for Restricted Persons that are not tied to a calendar, so execution dates cannot be planned reliably.

topic: spouses and related parties are Restricted Persons
clause: Restricted Persons means: all directors and their spouses and related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act 2001);
why_it_matters: Booking a collar through a director's spouse, family trust or related party does not escape the closed periods.

clause: Directors and employees should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.
why_it_matters: There is no stated period, so the tenor risk is unquantifiable and a bank should assume a conservative minimum such as twelve months and avoid early unwind features.

clause: Securities Trading Policy (applicable from 31 December 2010). Last updated: 23 December 2010.
why_it_matters: This policy is from 2010, pre-dates the hedging and margin lending provisions now standard in ASX policies, and no review cycle is stated, so the bank must verify whether a current version exists before relying on the silences.

clause: trading in Dexus securities by any Employee is permitted during the following periods ... 28 days commencing the day after half yearly and yearly results are announced to the market; 14 days commencing the day after the AGM. Trading outside these periods is prohibited.
why_it_matters: Dexus runs an open-window model with only about 70 trading days a year available, so collar entry, any roll and any physical settlement or unwind must each be scheduled inside a narrow window and separately approved.

clause: Trading windows can be cancelled at any time, as notified by the CEO. Such closure will become effective immediately on notification.
why_it_matters: A window can close between pricing and execution of the collar, so trade documentation should not commit the executive to deal on a fixed future date.

clause: A clearance to trade may be withdrawn if circumstances change. The Employee will be contacted directly in this situation and must keep this fact confidential.
why_it_matters: Approval for the collar is revocable up to execution and the executive cannot tell the bank why, so the bank must accept unexplained withdrawal of the trade within the 5-business-day validity period.

clause: Employees must not undertake the following types of personal trading activity: ... trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on Dexus securities is at serious risk of being characterised as margin lending activity, which is prohibited outright with no approval or hardship route.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Media Test.
why_it_matters: Even where the black-letter prohibitions do not bite, approvers have an express reputational veto over a director hedging or borrowing against Dexus securities, and no reasons need be given.

clause: Employees must not undertake ... trading that may cause a conflict (or appearance of conflict) of interest with Dexus or its clients.
why_it_matters: A written call over Dexus securities held by a Dexus funds-management executive could be treated as an appearance of conflict independently of the hedging and margin lending limbs.

clause: reference to Dexus Securities includes reference to Dexus (ASX:DXS), Dexus Industria REIT (ASX:ADI) and Dexus Convenience Retail REIT (ASX:DXC).
why_it_matters: The Policy reaches the two managed REITs as well as DXS, so a collar over any of the three is caught by the same windows, approvals and margin lending ban.

clause: All trades by Employees in listed and unlisted financial products managed by Dexus require prior approval in accordance with the Business Approval Table.
why_it_matters: The approval trigger is drafted around products managed by Dexus rather than derivatives referencing them, leaving it unclear whether an OTC put and call with a bank needs approval at all; a bank should require the executive to seek approval anyway and obtain written confirmation.
