clause: The Compliance team must be provided with a copy of contract notes or transaction advices of approved trades once they have been executed.
why_it_matters: Confirmations for the collar legs would have to be handed to Dexus Compliance, so the structure cannot be kept confidential from the issuer.

clause: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: in compliance with section 5.1 above; and providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.
why_it_matters: Unusually for an ASX policy, the collar's derivative legs over vested unrestricted shares are affirmatively permitted rather than banned, subject only to clearance and the inside information test.

clause: not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information
why_it_matters: Every roll, restrike, partial unwind and termination of the collar is a separate compliance event, so the bank cannot rely on unilateral adjustment rights and must build in the executive's ability to stand still while in possession of price sensitive information.

clause: hedging includes the entry into any transaction, arrangement or financial product which operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding in the Company and includes financial instruments such as equity swaps and contracts for differences.
why_it_matters: The definition is drafted by economic effect rather than instrument or venue, so an OTC put and call package with a bank is plainly within it and cannot be structured around.

clause: Directors and Executives must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The funding leg is the only real obstacle: 'margin lending arrangement' is not defined, so a loan secured on the collared shares should be documented as a fixed-term facility without margin calls or collateral top-up, and written confirmation obtained from the Company Secretary that it is not caught.

clause: Executives are not permitted to hedge performance rights granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.
why_it_matters: The collateral pool must be limited to shares that have been exercised and released from any transfer restriction; the bank should require evidence of that status at trade date.

clause: A clearance under this clause is not an endorsement of proposed trading and it is the Directors and Executives whom are ultimately responsible for ensuring their dealings in securities comply with the applicable laws and as applicable, the Policy.
why_it_matters: Clearance for the collar gives the bank no comfort that the Company has assessed the structure against the margin lending or short-term dealing prohibitions.

clause: or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts)
why_it_matters: Naming forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealing means the collar and any associated funding should have a tenor comfortably beyond three months and no early-termination triggers within it.

clause: This policy applies to all executive and non-executive directors (Directors) and all employees (Employees) of the Company and its subsidiaries (the Group).
why_it_matters: The Policy has no associates or connected persons clause, so on its face a collar entered by a family trust or controlled entity is not directly caught, although the executive's own conduct in procuring the dealing remains subject to the insider trading provisions.

clause: for any other period designated as a black-out period by the Board and advised to the Employees.
why_it_matters: Ad hoc black-outs are communicated by Company-wide email and intranet rather than kept confidential, so the executive can at least tell the bank that a dealing window is unavailable.

clause: Designated Persons may not, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company Securities, to secure any obligation of that Designated Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities, except with prior written consent under section 5.3.
why_it_matters: Unusually, the loan leg of a funded collar is expressly contemplated and available over vested unlocked shares with prior written consent, rather than banned outright.

clause: Designated Persons may not, at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The margin lending limb of the first paragraph of section 6.3 is not on its face confined to unvested securities and appears to contradict the consent route in the second paragraph, so the facility should be documented as a secured term loan rather than a margin loan and the Company's written position on the inconsistency obtained.

clause: Designated Persons may, at any time: ... a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
why_it_matters: Lender enforcement is an express exemption available at any time, including during a Blackout Period, which removes the usual objection that a bank cannot realise its collateral without putting the executive in breach; the Designated Person must still advise the Authorising Officer.

clause: Company Securities means all securities issued by the Company and includes shares, share rights, performance rights, options and derivatives of any of the above (including, equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.
why_it_matters: Both legs of an OTC collar are Company Securities in their own right, so entering, amending or unwinding them are Dealings requiring authorisation and are barred in Blackout Periods absent exceptional circumstances.

clause: including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf
why_it_matters: Shares held through an employee share trust cannot be collared while unvested or locked, so the collateral pool must be limited to fully vested, released holdings.

clause: from close of trading on the ASX on 31 March and 30 September, until commencement of trading on the ASX trading day immediately following the announcement of Westgold's quarterly reports
why_it_matters: Quarterly as well as half and full year blackouts leave narrow open windows, so entry, roll and unwind of the collar must be tightly scheduled or brought within the section 5.4 exceptional circumstances discretion.

clause: The Board may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on Dealing ... Any restriction communicated by the Board ... must be kept strictly confidential as the restriction itself may be considered Inside Information.
why_it_matters: The executive may be unable to tell the bank why a scheduled roll or unwind cannot proceed, so the trade documentation must tolerate unexplained delay.

clause: Written authorisation under this Policy may be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer in writing at any time during the clearance period ... having regard to the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed Dealing.
why_it_matters: Authorisation for the collar is revocable on reputational grounds at any point in the five business day window, so pricing should not be locked before execution.

clause: Reporting insiders must also file an insider trading report within five (5) days if the reporting insider enters into, materially amends, or terminates an agreement, arrangement or understanding that (i) has the effect of altering, directly or indirectly, the reporting insider's economic exposure to the Company
why_it_matters: The collar and any material amendment or termination must be publicly disclosed on SEDI within five days, so the structure cannot be kept confidential and the parties should agree disclosure wording in advance.

clause: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The prohibition is undefined and absolute, so a short-dated or highly geared collar risks being characterised as speculative even where consent for the protection arrangement is available.

clause: Any authorisation to trade by the Authorising Officer under this section 5.4 is not an endorsement to trade.
why_it_matters: Consent to the collar carries no representation by Westgold that the structure complies with the Policy or the law, so the bank should not treat the Form FM201 as a compliance opinion.

clause: Enter into hedging transactions to limit the economic risk of their holdings in BEN securities. This applies to both unvested and vested entitlements.
why_it_matters: The derivative legs of a collar are prohibited outright for every Designated Officer over fully vested shares, with no clearance or exemption route, which defeats the structure at the first step.

clause: Use BEN securities as security for entering into margin loans or similar financing arrangements.
why_it_matters: The words 'or similar financing arrangements' extend past classic margin lending to any loan secured on BEN securities, so the funding leg is prohibited independently of the hedging ban.

clause: Designated Officers and close connections may apply to trade during blackout periods only in exceptional circumstances
why_it_matters: The only discretionary relief in the Policy is permission to trade during a blackout period; nothing empowers the Board Chair, CEO or Company Secretary to waive the hedging or secured financing prohibitions.

clause: The following close connections of Designated Officers are also subject to restrictions: Family members - Parents, spouse/partner and dependent children. Entities controlled by the Designated Officer or their family. Trusts where the Designated Officer or family are beneficiaries.
why_it_matters: A collar written on shares held by a family trust or controlled entity is caught, and the Designated Officer is obliged to take reasonable steps to ensure the entity complies.

clause: Trading: Any action taken to buy, sell, transfer, or otherwise deal in securities. Transfer: Administrative transfers of securities between own accounts or to personal superannuation funds.
why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for dealings with no change in beneficial interest, so even moving the collateral parcel into a custody or security trustee account is Trading requiring prior written clearance inside a Trading Window.

clause: Hold BEN securities for less than 30 days.
why_it_matters: Any physically settled leg of a collar must not result in shares being acquired and disposed of within 30 days, which constrains cash-settled substitution and early unwind mechanics.

clause: BEN Securities: Includes shares, options, rights, debentures or any derivatives relating to BEN Group securities.
why_it_matters: Every leg of an OTC collar is itself a BEN Security, so entering, amending or closing it is Trading and is caught by the clearance regime as well as the hedging ban.

clause: Share Registry Provider (MUFG): Monitor controls and provide alerts placed on Designated Officers in the share registry. ... Flagged Holdings Reports when Designated Officers trade.
why_it_matters: Registry alerts are placed on Designated Officer holdings, so any transfer of the collateral parcel to a bank nominee would be detected and reported to the Company Secretary.

clause: The decision to grant or refuse clearance is at the Approving Officer's absolute discretion. If clearance is refused, that decision must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: Even for permitted trades the executive cannot explain a refusal to the bank, so no timetable dependent on clearance can be contractually guaranteed.

clause: For clarity, our People and their Associates are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted HUB24 Securities outside of designated restricted periods provided that the hedge transaction is treated as trading in HUB24 Securities for the purpose of this policy and the relevant approvals have been obtained.
why_it_matters: The derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares are affirmatively permitted, including for Associates such as a family trust, subject only to timing and approval.

clause: Our People and their Associates are permitted to have margin loans that have interests in HUB24 Securities under their margin lending arrangement, this includes meeting a 'margin call'.
why_it_matters: Unusually, borrowing against HUB24 Securities is expressly allowed rather than banned, so the funding leg of a collar is available in principle.

clause: Our People and their Associates must maintain sufficient liquidity or alternative securities in the margin lending arrangement to ensure that HUB24 Securities are not dealt with under a 'margin call' until prior written approval is obtained to deal in HUB24 Securities. ... regardless of the urgency of a margin call, a margin call that includes a request to trade HUB24 Securities, will only be considered in accordance with this policy and no special consideration is likely to be provided nor approval given.
why_it_matters: This is the central obstacle: the bank cannot realise the collared shares on short notice, because any sale under the facility needs prior written HUB24 approval that will most likely be refused during a Restricted Period, so the facility must be sized and documented so that enforcement over HUB24 shares is never needed.

topic: margin dealings are a restricted period item
clause: Our People and their Associates may not deal in HUB24 Securities during the following Restricted Periods: ... Dealings in HUB24 Securities under margin lending arrangements - refer to Section 6.
why_it_matters: Dealings under a financing arrangement are drafted into the Restricted Period list itself, so they are treated as permanently restricted and always require an approval decision.

clause: Failure by our People or their Associates to obtain prior written approval to deal in HUB24 Securities under a margin lending arrangement is considered a breach of this policy.
why_it_matters: A lender's unilateral sale exposes the executive to disciplinary action up to dismissal, so the security documents should require notice and a standstill while approval is sought.

clause: Enter into, renew, alter or close out a hedge transaction when they are in possession of Inside Information.
why_it_matters: Rolls, restrikes, partial unwinds and terminations are each separately regulated, so the bank cannot rely on unilateral adjustment or early termination rights.

clause: Hedge prior to vesting of any unvested HUB24 Securities acquired under the employee share plan operated by HUB24; Hedge HUB24 Securities subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of the employee share plan
why_it_matters: The collateral pool must be limited to shares that have vested and are free of any holding lock or plan dealing restriction.

clause: from the balance date (i.e. 30 June or 31 December) until 24 hours after the release of HUB24's annual or half-yearly results to ASX
why_it_matters: Roughly four months of each year are closed, plus a month before any prospectus and each Market Sensitive announcement day, so entry, roll and unwind must be scheduled into the open periods.

clause: Any approval expires: within five (5) business days of the date of the approval; or such other period as is agreed by the Company Secretary ... any approved but incomplete trades will lapse at the expiry and new approval to must be sought.
why_it_matters: The five business day window can be extended by agreement, which is useful for a negotiated OTC trade that cannot be executed as quickly as an on-market order.

clause: Approvals can be withheld where it's reasonable to believe that the person seeking approval is in possession of Inside Information or for reasons of good corporate governance or for other reasons taking into account matters such HUB24's trading activities and proposed transactions.
why_it_matters: Approval for a collar can be refused on general corporate governance grounds without reasons, and any refusal must be kept confidential from the bank.

clause: Approval requests will generally be answered within one business day after their receipt, provided those requests are received prior to 3pm on a business day and all relevant information is provided.
why_it_matters: A one business day service standard makes it practical to obtain approval close to pricing, reducing market risk between approval and execution.

clause: Designated Person includes any of our People who by virtue of their position and or duties are identified by management and Risk and Compliance as requiring additional securities trading requirements to be applied to them.
why_it_matters: Additional, unpublished trading restrictions may be imposed in writing on a particular executive, so the bank should ask for confirmation of whether the client is a Designated Person and what extra requirements apply.

clause: Margin Loan means any loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected from falls in the value of the Securities by a call right over those Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is secured against APE Securities and the bank takes a call right over them, so it should be treated as a Margin Loan requiring prior Board approval, immediate notice to the Chair and consent to public disclosure, even though it is not a margin loan in the conventional sense.

clause: Section 8 restricts only Margin Loans, and only for Directors and Senior Executives; there is no general prohibition on secured financing, encumbrance or hedging of vested shares anywhere in the policy.
why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this one leaves a funded collar over vested unrestricted shares available, subject to Board approval of the loan and the ordinary notice or Closed Period approval for the derivative legs.

clause: Any Employee who participates in an employee equity or incentive plan must not hedge ... Securities that have not vested or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan, without the Chair's approval.
why_it_matters: Even unvested and holding-locked plan shares can in principle be collared with the Chair's approval, which is unusual; without approval the sanction is forfeiture or lapsing of the unvested Securities.

topic: notice not approval outside closed periods
clause: Restricted Persons must not Deal in APE Securities outside Closed Periods without prior notice to the Chair or Company Secretary (or in their absence, to a non-executive Director).
why_it_matters: Entering, rolling or unwinding the collar outside a Closed Period needs only prior notice, with no stated approval, validity period or response deadline, so execution timing is far more flexible than under a preclearance regime.

clause: The approval may include conditions include the period in which the Dealing may occur.
why_it_matters: A Closed Period approval for collar entry or settlement can be time-boxed or otherwise conditioned, so the bank should treat the approval terms as execution constraints.

clause: The prohibitions on Dealing in Securities under clauses 3.1 and 3.2 will not apply to any Dealing ... in respect of which the Restricted Person has no control or influence over the Dealing decision.
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale or a bank's physical settlement of the collar during a Closed Period is arguably outside the executive's control and so within this exception, but the policy nowhere addresses forced sales expressly and the point is untested.

clause: Each Director and/or KMP member must hold a relevant interest in APE shares to a value of at least equal to the Company's annual base fee for non-executive Directors, subject to a transitional period to acquire the initial holding of 3 years.
why_it_matters: Shares pledged under the collar still give a relevant interest, but the policy is silent on whether hedged shares count towards the MSR, so the size of the collar relative to the required holding should be raised with the Chair.

clause: irrevocably consents to any public disclosure in relation to the Margin Loan which the Board may deem necessary or appropriate from time to time.
why_it_matters: The existence and terms of the collar loan may be publicly disclosed at the Board's discretion, which the executive cannot withdraw consent to, so confidentiality cannot be assured to the bank.

clause: Closed Period means any period from: (i) 30th June (ie. the end of APE's half year) until either results for that half year are announced ... or (ii) 31st December (ie. the end of APE's full year) until ...
why_it_matters: The half year and full year labels are transposed relative to APE's actual reporting calendar, but the operative dates are clear: 30 June and 31 December to results or guidance, and all collar entry, roll and unwind should be scheduled outside those two periods.

clause: any Employee who is nominated from time to time by the Chair or CEO to be a Restricted Person for the purpose of any provision of this policy ... or any other Employee whatsoever.
why_it_matters: A counterparty cannot rely on an executive's current status; the Chair or CEO can bring any employee into the Restricted Person or Senior Executive regime at any time, changing the approvals needed to unwind an existing collar.

clause: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).
why_it_matters: The hedging ban is defined by plan custody rather than by vesting, so a collar becomes available over exactly the shares that have been withdrawn from the Share Plan and are held as ordinary AMP shares; the bank should evidence withdrawal or conversion before pricing.

clause: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.
why_it_matters: For the two most likely client groups the loan leg of a funded collar, secured over AMP shares, is very likely a margin lending arrangement 'in respect of AMP Securities' and is banned outright, with no clearance or exceptional circumstances route.

clause: prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: A person who becomes an AMP Limited director or ExCo member while a funded collar loan is outstanding must unwind it, so promotion or board appointment is an unwind trigger the facility documents must anticipate.

clause: subject to section 2.7, a disposal of AMP Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excepted from the black-out prohibition]
why_it_matters: For a Designated Person who is not a Director or ExCo member, lender enforcement or physical settlement during a black-out period is an excepted Trade and does not breach the policy, which is unusually accommodating of secured lending mechanics.

topic: no clearance for margin call sales
clause: Clearance would not likely be granted under section 3 of this policy to sell AMP Securities during a black-out period to allow a Designated Person to comply with the terms of a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The executive cannot rely on being allowed to sell into a black-out period to top up collateral, so any funded collar should be sized and margined so no discretionary top-up sale is ever required.

clause: The Head of Corporate Governance (or their delegate) may direct the Designated Person who is proposing to Trade not to do so, or to impose conditions on the Trade in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any direction or condition.
why_it_matters: Although 2.4 is framed as notification rather than approval, AMP retains an unreasoned veto, so collar entry, roll and unwind carry execution risk right up to the trade date.

clause: a proposed Trade may only be effected on the second, third, fourth or fifth business day after notification.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar legs must be scheduled inside a four business day window opening two business days after notification, which constrains fixing dates and roll mechanics.

clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term trading (ie 30 days or less) in AMP Securities. The 30 days applies from the last time an AMP Security is bought until an AMP Security of that class or type is sold (or vice versa).
why_it_matters: Because AMP Securities include derivatives over AMP shares, entering and unwinding or rolling collar legs within 30 days risks breaching 2.8; tenor and roll dates should exceed 30 days.

clause: Designated Persons must also take appropriate steps to ensure that their Close Associates only Trade in Securities in circumstances where the Designated Person themselves would be permitted to Trade under this policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar through a controlled trust, company or investment account does not avoid the black-out, notification, short selling or hedging restrictions.

clause: This policy may also be specifically extended in writing by the CEO by specifying that Designated Persons are restricted from Trading in the Securities of other specified entities with which an AMP Group Company may have a relationship.
why_it_matters: The restricted universe is not fixed to AMP Securities and can be broadened by CEO direction, which matters where the collar references a basket or a related listed entity.

clause: Directors and Employees should ask themselves not only 'can we?', but 'should we?' ... How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
why_it_matters: A funded collar by a senior executive is precisely the kind of transaction this test targets, so expect scrutiny and possible informal discouragement even where each leg is technically compliant.

clause: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements (and other secured financing arrangements) to fund the acquisition of AGL Securities or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is a secured financing arrangement in relation to which AGL Securities would be used as security against repayment, so it is prohibited outright for every AGL Employee with no approval route.

clause: or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan
why_it_matters: The trigger is the possibility of the shares being used as security, not actual granting of the charge, so even a negative pledge structure or a facility with an optional security mechanic over AGL shares is caught.

topic: derivatives over vested shares expressly allowed
clause: For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement includes any proposed dealing in Derivatives in respect of fully vested AGL Shares.
why_it_matters: The unfunded legs of a collar over fully vested, unlocked shares are contemplated and approvable, so the structure fails only on the financing leg; a cash-settled or unfunded collar could still be presented for approval.

clause: Derivatives ... includes options, forward contracts, swaps, futures contracts and warrants and any combination of one or more of these things or any other arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in AGL Securities.
why_it_matters: A synthetic or combination structure over unvested entitlements cannot be engineered around the 3.6 ban, since the definition is drafted by economic effect rather than instrument type.

clause: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided ... the AGL Securities are not subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: The bank must verify not only vesting but the absence of any holding lock on the specific parcel before the collar legs may be written.

clause: AGL Employees who acquire AGL Securities must not dispose of those Securities, or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those Securities being disposed of, within 3 months of acquisition.
why_it_matters: Independently of 3.7, a collar with physical settlement or lender enforcement rights over recently acquired shares is an arrangement that could result in disposal within 3 months, so tenor and share selection matter.

clause: Where the Board imposes additional blackout periods from time to time, to protect confidentiality there may not be any internal notification by AGL that a prohibition on dealing is in place.
why_it_matters: Undisclosed blackouts can block entry, roll or unwind at any time, and the executive may only learn of one when an approval request is refused without explanation.

clause: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused by the applicable approver in his or her absolute discretion without giving reason. ... Any approval to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for one week unless it is withdrawn.
why_it_matters: Approval for the derivative legs is revocable up to execution and lapses after one week, so pricing must be completed inside a short window and the bank carries the risk of late withdrawal.

clause: There are certain times during the year when approval under this Policy is more likely to be granted. These are the four-week periods immediately following each blackout period.
why_it_matters: Practical execution should be scheduled in the four weeks after each results announcement, which effectively narrows the collar entry and roll calendar to two short windows a year.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: An express substantive ground for refusal: a senior executive hedging a large stake is exactly the transaction likely to fail a reputational perception test, independently of technical compliance.

clause: This Policy extends to Connected Persons of Designated Persons in relation to dealing in AGL Securities ... (which will be read as if references to 'Designated Person' throughout the Policy was a reference to Connected Persons).
why_it_matters: Holding the shares or the borrowing through a family trust, controlled company or SMSF does not escape the secured financing ban or the approval requirement.

topic: margin loan and similar funding ban
clause: No Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is a funding arrangement in respect of Ansell Securities and so within clause 4.8, which is the principal obstacle; note the hortatory 'should' rather than 'must not'.

clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officers listed in clause 4.3(d) have discretion to approve Dealings by the respective Designated Person in Ansell Securities outside a Trading Window, or to approve Dealings in Ansell Securities that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
why_it_matters: Unusually, an Authorising Officer can approve dealings that the policy otherwise prohibits, so the funded collar is not structurally impossible; the whole structure would need Board Chair or CEO level sign-off as an exceptional circumstance.

topic: lender enforcement is an excluded dealing
clause: Designated Persons may at any time, without seeking Clearance ... dispose of Ansell Securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
why_it_matters: The policy expressly contemplates secured lending over Ansell shares and protects the executive if the bank enforces or takes delivery outside a Trading Window, requiring only after-the-event notice to the Authorising Officer.

clause: All participants in an approved share or equity plan of the Company are prohibited from engaging in any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value ... while the Securities remain unvested.
why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition is bounded by vesting rather than by any holding lock, so vested plan shares are available for a collar, subject to the Trading Window and Clearance regime.

clause: Designated Persons and their Closely Related Parties may, unless the Company advises otherwise, Deal in Ansell Securities during the 30-day period beginning ... on the second trading day after [half-yearly results / annual results / the AGM]. ... Designated Persons may not Deal in Ansell Securities outside the Trading Windows.
why_it_matters: This is a positive-window policy: entry, roll and unwind of the collar must each fall inside one of only three 30-day windows a year, which constrains tenor selection and expiry dates.

clause: the clearance will be confirmed in writing and will be valid for a period of five trading days (inclusive of the approval date) unless otherwise stated. No Dealing ... may be executed beyond the five day period ... without having sought and received further Clearance.
why_it_matters: Pricing and signing of the derivative legs must complete within five trading days of Clearance, and a staged or averaged execution beyond that needs fresh Clearance.

clause: The Company, in its sole and absolute discretion, may impose additional restrictions on Dealing ... even where the proposed Dealing would otherwise take place when a Trading Window is open. Any restriction ... must be kept strictly confidential.
why_it_matters: An open window is never a guarantee; a confidential ad-hoc restriction can block collar entry or unwind without the bank being told why.

topic: front page test as a refusal ground
clause: Where any approval under this Policy is required for a Dealing, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the 'front page' test.
why_it_matters: An express mandatory ground for refusing Clearance, and a senior executive hedging a stake with bank funding is squarely the kind of transaction it targets.

clause: Designated Persons must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Closely Related Parties are aware of, and comply with, this Policy. Where this Policy requires a Closely Related Party to do an act ... you must do that act on behalf of your Closely Related Party.
why_it_matters: Holding the shares or the borrowing through a controlled trust or company does not avoid clause 4.8 or the Clearance requirement, and the Designated Person must obtain Clearance on the entity's behalf.

clause: No Designated Person should Deal in Ansell Securities on a short-term trading basis, including trading in Ansell Securities within a 3 month period of receiving the Securities.
why_it_matters: Collaring shares within three months of vesting or acquisition risks breaching clause 4.6 unless the Company Secretary approves, so the parcel selection should favour older holdings.

clause: Any sale of Ansell shares acquired by a Designated Person under any Ansell share or equity plan (at the end of applicable vesting or restriction periods or upon exercise of options) must only occur during a Trading Window ... and with Clearance.
why_it_matters: Physical settlement of the call leg over plan-sourced shares is a sale that must itself fall inside a Trading Window with fresh Clearance, so expiry dates should be aligned to the windows or the collar cash settled.

topic: collars named in the derivative definition
clause: derivative: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.
why_it_matters: The policy names collars specifically and defines derivatives by economic function, so there is no argument that a put plus call structure falls outside the hedging prohibition.

topic: flat hedging ban for Designated Persons
clause: Designated Persons and their Associates must not ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities, including those specified in paragraph 9 (no hedging).
why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to plan securities or to unvested holdings, so a Designated Person cannot collar even shares bought on market with their own money, and paragraph 16 offers no exemption route for it.

clause: A Designated Person or their Associate may request to ... seek an approval for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 11b ... you must provide written details of the securitisation arrangement and any other information requested by Endeavour. The request should be submitted concurrently to the CLO and Company Secretary (Endorsers) and the Chair and the Board Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee (Approvers).
why_it_matters: Endeavour is one of the few ASX policies with an express pathway to approve pledging shares as loan collateral, so the financing leg of a funded structure is negotiable at Board Chair level even though the hedging leg is not.

clause: use Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including any margin lending arrangements (no security or margin lending), unless otherwise permitted under this policy
why_it_matters: The prohibition is drafted at the level of collateral in any financial transaction, so it catches any bank facility secured on the shares regardless of how the loan is documented, and approval must be obtained before the security is granted.

clause: deal in the same Endeavour Securities, or in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities, within a six month period (no short term gain).
why_it_matters: Even a permitted derivative programme could not be entered, rolled or unwound within six months, so short-dated or frequently rolled collars are unavailable to Designated Persons.

clause: The opening of Trading Windows will be notified to Designated Persons by email. Designated Persons must not assume that a Trading Window is open in the absence of such notification.
why_it_matters: Windows are not self-executing from the results calendar; the bank should require evidence of the notification email before scheduling execution.

clause: the Designated Person or Associate must undertake the dealing within three business days of obtaining the clearance ... A dealing must be placed within a Trading Window (not prior) and executed by 4.00pm on the last day of the relevant Trading Window. A dealing may settle after the close of the Trading Window.
why_it_matters: Any approved leg must be placed and executed inside the window and within three business days of clearance, though settlement may fall outside, which is helpful for a structure with a delayed settlement date.

clause: Deal includes to: ... margin lend, stock lend or make other financing arrangements for securities; ... transfer ownership between accounts, brokers or sponsors.
why_it_matters: Moving the collared shares into a custody or collateral account, and the financing arrangement itself, are each dealings needing a Trading Window and clearance, not just administrative steps.

clause: Associates ... includes ... a company, trust, partnership or other entity that the Relevant Person, or any of the persons mentioned above, control or significantly influence; or the trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangements of which the Relevant Person ... is a beneficiary.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar through a family trust, controlled company or the trustee of a fund in which the executive is a beneficiary does not escape the hedging ban or the collateral clearance requirement.

clause: You must not deal in Endeavour Securities (or securities of another company) if the proposed dealing could be perceived by the market as you taking advantage of your position in an inappropriate way.
why_it_matters: An independent, self-executing obligation that applies to every team member at all times and cannot be waived by any exemption, so even an approved collateral arrangement remains vulnerable to a perception challenge.

clause: A liability to pay tax does not normally constitute severe financial difficulty.
why_it_matters: Funding a tax bill on vesting is expressly not an exceptional circumstance, closing off the most common justification for an out-of-window monetisation.

clause: Directors and Employees must not trade in CWY derivatives. This applies to all CWY securities including performance rights issued under CWYs incentive schemes.
why_it_matters: Both legs of a collar are CWY derivatives, so the structure is prohibited outright for every Director and Employee with no clearance or hardship route available.

clause: you cannot enter into any hedging arrangements or acquire financial products (such as equity swaps, caps and collars or other hedging products) over unvested performance rights which have the effect of reducing or limiting exposure to risks associated with the market value of CWY securities
why_it_matters: Collars are named in terms, removing any argument that the ban was not intended to reach this product, although the explanatory sentence is drafted by reference to unvested performance rights only.

clause: Section 3.4 first bans trading in CWY derivatives over 'all CWY securities', then explains the ban only by reference to hedging 'over unvested performance rights'.
why_it_matters: The only conceivable opening for a collar over vested shares is to read the operative ban down to the explanatory sentence, which would require the Board to confirm the narrow reading in writing before a bank could rely on it.

clause: Unless the prior written consent of the Chairman of the CWY Board has been obtained, all Directors, Executives, Employees (to the extent that their margin loans are considered material) and Related parties of the above persons are prohibited directly or indirectly from entering into any margin loan facility against CWY securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg is not banned outright, unlike the derivative legs, but a facility secured on CWY shares would need the Chairman's prior written consent, and 'directly or indirectly' catches structures routed through related entities.

clause: Each Director and Executive must also take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Related Parties do not deal in CWY securities without the Director or Executive obtaining approval ... Related party ... An immediate family member ... A company, trust or other entity that is controlled by the relevant Director or Executive; or The trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangement of which the relevant Director or Executive is a beneficiary.
why_it_matters: Placing the collar or the borrowing in a family trust or controlled company does not escape the derivatives ban, the approval requirement or the margin loan consent gateway.

clause: Directors and Employees must not deal in the same CWY securities within any three month period.
why_it_matters: Even if a hedge were permitted, entry, roll, partial unwind and physical settlement over the same parcel inside three months would breach the policy, so any structure must be long dated with settlement outside the window.

clause: If an approval to trade is granted, it may be revoked by the Company at any time at its absolute discretion. If an approved share trade is conducted, it must occur within 3 business days from the date that the approval is provided and must not exceed the number of shares that were the subject of the request.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of any approved transaction must complete within three business days and remain revocable until done, which is difficult for a negotiated OTC structure.

clause: Directors and Executives will not be given approval to deal in CWY securities under sections 3.2 or 3.3 of this policy where price sensitive, non-public information exists in relation to a matter, even though they may not be aware of it.
why_it_matters: Approval can be withheld for information the executive does not hold, so a bank cannot treat a clean insider-trading representation as sufficient for the transaction to proceed.

clause: Where a request for approval is refused, that refusal must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: The executive may be unable to tell the bank why an agreed collar or unwind cannot proceed, so documentation needs a no-reasons termination right.

clause: For the purpose of this policy, securities can be more than just shares. They also include options, rights and warrants or any instrument which has the feature of converting into an equity interest in the Company. They can include bonds and other financial products.
why_it_matters: OTC options over CWY shares are securities under the policy, with no venue limitation, so an off-market bank trade is treated the same as an on-market one.

clause: The exceptional circumstances relief in section 3.2 is expressed only as approval to 'dispose of securities outside these Trading Windows'.
why_it_matters: The hardship route can unlock a sale but cannot authorise a derivative or hedging transaction, so it offers no path to a collar.

clause: you must obtain the Board's approval to enter into a margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin's securities, providing the Board with the material terms of the proposed arrangements, including the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and trigger events
why_it_matters: This is an affirmative approval pathway for both the hedge and the secured loan of a funded collar, but the bank must expect its unilateral sale rights, LVR triggers and termination events to be disclosed to and scrutinised by the full Board before signing.

topic: incentive securities hedging ban survives vesting
clause: You are prohibited from hedging securities granted as incentives under any Paladin employee incentive scheme. This relates to both vested and unvested securities. Prohibited hedging practices include put/call arrangements over 'in-the-money' rights to hedge against a future drop in share price.
why_it_matters: Shares that originated from an LTI or STI grant can never be collared even long after vesting, so the collateral pool must be limited to securities acquired outside the incentive schemes and the bank needs provenance evidence for every share pledged.

clause: Prohibited hedging practices include put/call arrangements over 'in-the-money' rights to hedge against a future drop in share price.
why_it_matters: The exact structure of a collar is named as a prohibited practice for incentive securities, so there is no scope to argue the ban was not aimed at this product.

clause: you must not enter into margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement ... that would have the effect of limiting your exposure to risk in relation to part or all of your remuneration that has not vested, or has vested but remains subject to a restriction arrangement (e.g. a holding lock).
why_it_matters: Board approval cannot cure a hedge over unvested or holding-locked remuneration, so the collateral must be free of any restriction arrangement at the time the collar is struck.

clause: For the purposes of this Policy, this prohibition applies to any contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Paladin's securities.
why_it_matters: A cash-settled collar is a contract intended to avoid a loss based on price fluctuations, so any cash-settled variant risks being caught by this catch-all even where the underlying shares are freely held.

topic: creating a hedge or security interest is a Trade
clause: Trade or Trading includes: ... creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to securities; transferring legal ownership of securities, even where beneficial ownership does not change; ... and agreeing or applying to do any of the above.
why_it_matters: Signing the collar, granting the security and transferring the shares to a custodian or the bank's nominee are each separate Trades needing permission and falling outside blackout periods, and even the agreement to do so is caught.

clause: securities Includes ... any derivatives of those securities (including equity swaps, contracts for difference, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise).
why_it_matters: There is no venue or settlement-method gap: an OTC, cash-settled bank option is a Paladin security for every purpose of the Policy.

clause: If permission to Trade is given, such permission is valid for five business days, unless the written permission to Trade specifies another period; can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution must complete within five business days unless a longer bespoke period is negotiated in the written permission, and the permission remains withdrawable until the transaction is done.

clause: Any permission to Trade can be given or refused, without giving any reasons. ... The decision to refuse permission is final and binding ... If permission to Trade is refused, the Restricted Person seeking the permission must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: The executive cannot tell the bank why a collar entry, roll or unwind is blocked, so the documentation needs an unexplained termination or extension right.

clause: Permission to Trade will generally not be granted if ... there is a risk the market will suspect the person seeking permission to trade had Inside Information, or there is a risk of reputational damage to Paladin.
why_it_matters: Even a fully compliant collar can be refused on optics alone, which makes any committed bank facility contingent on a discretionary judgement.

clause: the periods commencing from the end of: a financial quarter up to the day after the release date of the quarter's results; a half-year ...; and a financial year ...
why_it_matters: As a quarterly reporter Paladin closes the window four times a year, so execution and any unwind must be timed to the narrow post-release periods.

clause: if you have entered into any margin lending arrangement, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement with the Board's approval, you must keep the Company Secretary informed of any change in circumstances that may be relevant to Paladin's continuous disclosure obligations
why_it_matters: Amendments, LVR breaches or enforcement steps under the facility must be reported to the Company Secretary on an ongoing basis and may become publicly disclosed.

clause: A Restricted Person must not, and must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Closely Connected Persons do not, Trade in securities without the Restricted Person obtaining permission to do so under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a spouse's name or a family trust does not avoid the approval, blackout or hedging restrictions.

topic: no closed-period relief for anything but a sale
clause: In exceptional circumstances, permission may be given by an Authorising Officer for a Restricted Person or their Closely Connected Person to Trade securities in Paladin (where such Trade only involves a proposed sale of securities) during a 'blackout' period.
why_it_matters: Blackout relief is available only for outright sales, so a collar cannot be struck, rolled or hedged during a blackout even in hardship.

clause: "Secured Financing Arrangement" means any financing arrangement pursuant to which Shares are provided as security, and includes (without limitation) a margin loan facility and a capital protected loan with put and call options.
why_it_matters: The funded collar is described almost exactly and is treated as permissible with consent rather than prohibited, which makes this one of the few ASX policies that expressly contemplates the product.

clause: A Key Management Member must obtain the written consent of the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer prior to entering into a Secured Financing Arrangement.
why_it_matters: A single executive consent, not a full Board resolution, unlocks the loan and security leg, and it may be given by email.

clause: A forced sale of Shares under a margin loan to satisfy an unmet margin call or default, or otherwise pursuant to a Secured Financing Arrangement will be a breach of this Policy unless the Key Management Member has first obtained approval to the Secured Financing Arrangement in accordance with this clause. ... a disposal of Shares that is the result of a secured lender exercising rights under a Secured Financing Arrangment where approval of the arrangement was obtained pursuant to clause 5.6 [is excluded trading].
why_it_matters: With prior consent, the bank's enforcement or close-out sale is excluded trading and can occur even in a Prohibited Period; without consent the same sale puts the executive in breach, so obtaining consent before signing is critical to the bank's enforcement rights.

topic: hedging plan shares permitted on notice
clause: Each Key Management Member must notify the Chairman if that person hedges any Shares acquired as a result of the exercise of any Performance Rights.
why_it_matters: Hedging vested plan shares is treated as a notifiable event rather than a prohibited one, which is the opposite of the standard ASX approach and leaves the option legs available over vested stock.

clause: Each Key Management Member must not hedge any Performance Rights.
why_it_matters: Because Performance Rights are defined to include Shares granted under a shareholder-approved plan, unexercised rights and plan-granted shares that have not been acquired 'as a result of the exercise' of a right sit on the wrong side of the line and cannot form part of the collared parcel.

clause: Each Key Management Member must not deal or trade in any Shares received upon exercise or vesting of any Performance Rights while those Shares are subject to any transfer restriction.
why_it_matters: Shares still inside a holding lock or disposal restriction cannot be pledged or hedged at all, so the collateral pool is limited to plan shares whose restriction period has ended plus shares acquired on market.

clause: The Company may be obliged to disclose the existence and terms of any Secured Financing Arrangement to the market pursuant to the ASX Listing Rules and the Key Management Member must provide the Company sufficient details of any existing or proposed Secured Financing Arrangement so as to allow the Company to fulfil its obligations.
why_it_matters: The bank must expect the terms of the collar and loan, including LVR and trigger events, to be given to the Company and potentially announced, so confidentiality provisions in the facility need to accommodate that.

clause: If a Key Management Member, acting reasonably, would believe that there will be an unmet margin call, event of default or other circumstance in relation to any Secured Financing Arrangement which may result in a financier exercising its rights to force an acquisition or disposal of Shares, the Key Management Member must immediately disclose to the Chairman, Company Secretary or Chief Executive Officer, full and complete details.
why_it_matters: Approaching an LVR trigger creates an immediate internal reporting obligation before the bank acts, so margin call notices should be structured to give the executive time to comply.

clause: A Restricted Person may buy, sell, otherwise acquire, or deal in Shares during any Prohibited Period within twenty eight (28) days after the grant of written consent ... Any consent granted pursuant to clause 7.1 is automatically revoked if the Restricted Person receives Price Sensitive Information, without the need for ... written notice of the revocation.
why_it_matters: Twenty eight days is generous by ASX standards and comfortably accommodates negotiation and pricing of an OTC structure, but the consent evaporates automatically and silently if the executive receives price sensitive information before execution.

topic: derivatives only blocked in Prohibited Periods
clause: Each Key Management Member is prohibited from trading during any Prohibited Period in financial products issued or created over or in respect of any Shares.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs are restricted by timing rather than by subject matter, so they can be struck inside a thirty day Trading Window without any express derivatives ban applying.

clause: The Policy contains no definition of associates, closely connected persons or related parties, and no clause extending the restrictions to spouses, dependants or controlled entities.
why_it_matters: There is no express look-through to family trusts or controlled companies, though the insider trading law and clause 3.2(f) on procuring family members or trusts still apply.

clause: Each Key Management Member must not engage in short term trading in Shares except where ... the request relates to exercised or vested Performance Rights ... and the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer gives prior written approval.
why_it_matters: With no defined period, a short-dated or early-terminated collar carries characterisation risk, so a longer tenor and consent that expressly covers the unwind are prudent.

clause: Employees and Partners must not engage in hedging of Telix Securities. Hedging is a form of dealing and includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Telix Securities.
why_it_matters: The test is economic effect rather than instrument type or venue, so an OTC put and call with a bank over vested shares is squarely prohibited and cannot be re-engineered around.

clause: Employees and Partners must not obtain margin loans using Telix Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Telix Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is separately and independently prohibited, so even if the hedge could be justified there is no route to the borrowing.

topic: no exemption authority for the bans
clause: The exemptions in section 5 are limited to plan participation, disposals in exceptional circumstances, and a closed list of excluded dealings; sections 4.5, 4.6 and 4.7 have no approval or exceptional-circumstances carve-out.
why_it_matters: There is no person or committee that can waive the hedging or secured financing prohibitions, so a bank cannot cure the problem with a company consent letter.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy under section 6.1, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test. ... How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
why_it_matters: An optics-based veto sits over every approval, so even an otherwise compliant transaction can be blocked on perception grounds alone.

clause: Any other special blackout period that the Board specifies from time to time. ... Some examples which may constitute Inside Information include ... (l) the existence of a special blackout period.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed Board-imposed blackout can block execution or unwind at any time and the executive may not be able to explain the delay to the bank.

clause: If approval to deal in Telix Securities is granted, the dealing must be conducted within three business days of the approval. ... it may be withdrawn at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised.
why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be documented, priced and executed inside three business days and remains revocable until lodged, which is unworkable for a negotiated bilateral structure.

topic: directors need approval even in a window
clause: Prior approval to deal in Telix Securities: (a) by Directors (including the CEO) and their Connected Persons during a Trading Window ... must be sought.
why_it_matters: Directors have no self-executing dealing right at all, so every step of any structure, including a permitted outright sale, needs the Chair's sign-off.

clause: Connected Person is a person or entity that is connected to another person or entity in a way that allows for influence over dealings, including ... individuals with close family ties, business partners, and associated companies or trusts; a company or any other entity which the Employee or Partner has an ability to control, including its directors and officers.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust, controlled company or business partner does not escape the hedging and secured financing bans.

clause: Subsequent dealings with Telix Securities issued on exercise or conversion of any Telix Share Plan Derivative are always subject to this Policy, including section 4.1.
why_it_matters: Vesting confers no freedom: shares issued out of the plans remain fully subject to the hedging and financing prohibitions.

clause: Prompt notification to the Group Company Secretary is essential to assist Telix in complying with its disclosure obligations under the Corporations Act, the U.S. Securities Exchange Act, the Listing Rules, the U.S. federal securities laws and related compliance policies.
why_it_matters: Any transaction would also engage Nasdaq and SEC insider reporting and, for a pledge or hedge by an officer or director, US disclosure regimes on top of the ASX rules.

clause: Employees or Partners who fail to adhere to the requirements of this policy may face disciplinary action, including suspension or termination of employment, forfeiture of securities issued under any equity incentive plan of the Group, and/or exclusion from participating in any equity incentive plan of the Group.
why_it_matters: Breach can extinguish the very shares a bank is relying on as collateral, which is a direct credit risk to a secured lender.

topic: OTC derivatives not named in the securities definition
clause: Telix Securities means shares, American Depositary Shares representing shares, and other instruments considered to be a security for the purposes of the Corporations Act or Listing Rules ... as well as exchange traded options and warrants.
why_it_matters: The securities definition names only exchange traded options, but the hedging prohibition is drafted by economic effect rather than by reference to Telix Securities, so the venue gap gives no opening for an OTC structure.

clause: Restricted Personnel and their Associates are prohibited from entering into: (a) transactions in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of Securities or entitlements to acquire Securities (such as options or share rights) including hedging or similar arrangements;
why_it_matters: The test is economic effect and expressly includes 'similar arrangements', so a put and call collar over vested New Hope shares is prohibited regardless of venue, structure or vesting status.

topic: stock lending and margin lending banned
clause: stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities;
why_it_matters: The financing leg is also blocked, and the express ban on stock lending forecloses the rehypothecation and borrow arrangements a bank would ordinarily rely on for the collateral.

clause: The following circumstances ... are therefore excluded from the operation of paragraphs 5.1, 6.1, 9.1(b) and 9.1(c) and section 7 of this Policy
why_it_matters: The excluded dealings list is drafted to relieve the Trading Window, approval, short-term and short selling rules but deliberately not the hedging and margin lending prohibitions in 9.2, which therefore admit of no exception at all.

clause: Restricted personnel for the purposes of this policy are ... (g) a family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Restricted Personnel ... and any companies or any other entity which the Restricted Personnel has an ability to control (Associates).
why_it_matters: Associates are not merely subject to a look-through duty, they are themselves Restricted Personnel, so a spouse's trust or a controlled company cannot enter the collar or the loan either.

clause: Restricted Personnel and their Associates must not at any time: (a) deal in Securities when directed not to do so by the Chair of the Board, the Chief Executive Officer or the Company Secretary (even if in a Trading Window);
why_it_matters: Three individuals can each block any dealing at any moment without reasons, so no execution or unwind date can be treated as certain.

topic: windows can be closed without reason
clause: The Company Secretary, in consultation with the Chair of the Board or Chief Executive Officer of the Company, may also prohibit certain or all Restricted Personnel from dealing in Company Securities during a Trading Window or an ad hoc Trading Window. Where Restricted Personnel are prohibited, the Company Secretary will notify them and does not need to provide a reason.
why_it_matters: Even a scheduled window is not a reliable execution period, and the executive cannot explain a cancellation to a counterparty.

clause: If approval to deal is granted ... in each circumstance the duration of the approval will be two business days. ... The approver ... may revoke their approval at any time.
why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be priced and executed within two business days and remains revocable throughout, which no negotiated bilateral structure could reliably meet.

clause: If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: The executive is barred from telling the bank why the transaction cannot proceed, so documentation needs a no-reasons termination right.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: An optics veto sits over every approval, and a director monetising a stake through a bank structure is exactly the kind of transaction that would fail it.

clause: Restricted Personnel who are aware of information that they suspect might increase or decrease the market price for the Company's Securities if it were announced must explain this when seeking approval to trade.
why_it_matters: The applicant carries an affirmative disclosure burden beyond a clean insider trading representation, which increases the chance of refusal for a large structured trade.

clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action, including compulsory divestment of the securities, forfeiture of securities and/or summary dismissal.
why_it_matters: A breach can lead to compulsory divestment or forfeiture of the very shares pledged, which is a direct credit risk for a secured lender.

topic: plan shares fall back under the policy
clause: where securities in the Company granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy
why_it_matters: Vested plan shares are fully subject to the hedging and margin lending prohibitions, so there is no free pool of collateral once shares leave the plan.

clause: Paragraph 9.2(b) prohibits 'stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities' but contains no express catch-all for 'any other secured financing arrangement'.
why_it_matters: The only conceivable argument for a collar loan is that it is not 'similar' to margin lending, but that argument fails in any event because 9.2(a) independently prohibits the option legs.

clause: Directors and members of the ELT must not enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of SEEK Securities except with prior written clearance from the Chairman, or in the case of an arrangement proposed to be entered into by the Chairman, the ARMC Chairman.
why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this is a consent regime rather than a ban, so the secured loan leg of a funded collar is available to Directors and ELT if the Chairman approves, and is entirely unrestricted for Designated Persons below ELT.

clause: The following types of dealings are excluded from the operation of section 3 of this Policy and may be undertaken by Designated Persons at any time without prior notification or approval ... (lender disposal) a disposal of SEEK Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement or close-out sale of the collared shares is expressly outside the blackout and clearance regime, so lender enforcement during a Blackout Period is not a breach.

clause: Where it is determined that the relevant margin loan or other security arrangement is material, SEEK will make a disclosure to the market ... Such disclosure will address the existence of the margin loan and set out relevant terms such as the trigger points or the right of the financier to sell unilaterally.
why_it_matters: A material funded collar loan for a Director or ELT member will be publicly disclosed including its trigger levels and the bank's unilateral sale rights, so confidentiality cannot be assumed.

clause: arrangements which have the effect of limiting the economic risk related to an unvested share, option or other Security granted or awarded under a SEEK employee incentive scheme (or a vested share, option or other Security granted, awarded or acquired under a SEEK employee incentive scheme that is still subject to disposal restrictions).
why_it_matters: The collar must be sized only to shares that have vested and are free of disposal restrictions; unvested and still-restricted plan shares cannot be included in the collar pool at all.

clause: SEEK may grant or refuse clearance to trade in its absolute discretion. A clearance to trade can also be withdrawn by SEEK if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: Clearance for the collar can be revoked between approval and execution, so the bank should not treat clearance as a firm condition precedent until the trade is actually struck.

clause: Any dealing in SEEK Securities by a Designated Person in respect of which clearance is given under this section 3 must occur within 5 Trading Days of receipt of the clearance.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both derivative legs and the loan drawdown must all be completed inside five trading days of clearance, or clearance must be sought again.

clause: A Designated Person must not: (a) buy and sell SEEK Securities on a short term basis (that is, within a three month period) except with prior written clearance obtained in accordance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: A collar unwound or rolled within three months is not banned outright but requires separate express clearance, so short-tenor or frequently rolled structures carry extra approval risk.

clause: Associate includes ... a trustee where the beneficiaries of the relevant trust include the Designated Person or his or her spouse, partner, child or step-child; and any other persons over whom a Designated Person ... has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the blackout and clearance regime, and the Designated Person must procure the associate's compliance.

clause: additional restrictions on dealing in SEEK Securities apply to Designated Persons who are specified in the Annexure to this Policy (and their Associates).
why_it_matters: All equity plan participants are Designated Persons under the Annexure, so any executive holding vested plan shares will be inside the restricted population.

clause: Employees and their Connected Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities provided that the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications required under section 4 are made on that basis.
why_it_matters: This is an express positive permission for the derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares, rather than the more common outright hedging ban, so the structure has a clear policy pathway.

clause: any Employee or their Connected Persons must not enter into, renew, alter or close out a hedge transaction when they are in possession of Inside Information;
why_it_matters: Rolls, amendments, resets and unwinds of the collar are each separately regulated events, so the bank must build in approval and inside-information checkpoints at every lifecycle step, not just at inception.

topic: margin lending is an approval regime
clause: Employees and their Connected Persons must obtain approval ... for any proposed dealing in the Netwealth's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement. Examples of such dealings include: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Netwealth's securities; transferring securities in Netwealth into an existing margin loan account; and selling securities in Netwealth to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
why_it_matters: The secured loan leg is permitted with approval rather than banned, but each of inception, the transfer of the collared shares into the lender's account, and any self-help sale to meet a call is a separate dealing needing its own approval.

topic: conditional approval on margin call sales
clause: The relevant approver may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with this Policy conditional upon such terms and conditions as Netwealth sees fit (for example, regarding the circumstances in which Netwealth's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: Netwealth can impose conditions that constrain the bank's enforcement rights, so the facility documentation should anticipate company-imposed limits on when collateral may be sold.

clause: Sections 4.1, 4.3 and 5.2 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of Netwealth that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Lender enforcement is outside the blackout, prior-approval and short-term trading rules, so the bank can realise the collateral even in a blackout period without putting the executive in breach.

clause: Short-term trading includes the buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: A prepaid forward or a short-dated collar risks being characterised as a prohibited short-term dealing, so tenor should comfortably exceed three months or NWL Board authorisation should be obtained.

topic: 14 day cooling off in the annual declaration
clause: Appendix A, question 8: 'I have not traded or transferred NWL securities within 14 days of purchasing or selling one or more NWL securities.'
why_it_matters: The annual declaration asserts a 14-day gap between trades that has no counterpart in the body of the Policy, so paired legs or a same-window loan drawdown and share transfer may need to be spaced or explained.

clause: We will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A collar or loan structured to sit outside the literal wording of the margin lending and hedging sections will still be assessed on its economic substance.

clause: Where any approval is required for a trading under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the trading would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Approval for the collar can be refused on pure reputational grounds regardless of technical compliance, and the approver need give no reasons.

topic: no reasons for direction or condition
clause: The Company Secretary (or their delegate) may direct the person who is proposing to trade in the Company's securities not to trade, or impose conditions on the trading in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any direction or condition.
why_it_matters: Execution of the collar can be blocked or conditioned at short notice without explanation, so the bank should treat approval as revocable until the trade is struck.

clause: All Employees must keep an up to date register containing information relating to all trading of Financial Products (Trading Register). ... I confirm I do not have a margin loan associated with my NWL securities and / or have not hedged my NWL Securities.
why_it_matters: The existence of the collar and any associated loan must be recorded and annually declared, so it cannot be kept confidential from the company.

clause: The entering by a Designated Person or their Affected Parties into all types of "protection arrangements" for any of the Company's securities (or Company products in the derivatives markets): (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and (b) otherwise, requires approval under section 4.3(a).
why_it_matters: This is a two-tier regime rather than a blanket hedging ban: the collar is available over vested unrestricted shares with Authorising Officer approval, but can never touch unvested or holding-locked stock.

clause: operate to limit the economic risk of the relevant person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including the Company's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that person's behalf
why_it_matters: Shares sitting in an employee share trust are within the protection arrangement definition, so the collar cannot be run over trust-held plan shares while they remain unvested or locked.

clause: Designated Persons may not at any time, and must procure that their Affected Parties do not at any time, directly or indirectly, enter into any margin lending arrangement involving the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The word 'indirectly' means a loan documented as something other than a margin loan but carrying LVR, margin call or top-up mechanics over the collared shares would be prohibited, so the funding leg must be a genuinely non-margin term facility.

clause: dispose of Company securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement;
why_it_matters: The exemption confirms that non-margin secured lending against Company securities is contemplated and is not caught by section 5.3, and that the bank's enforcement sale may occur at any time, including outside a Trading Window.

clause: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons or their Affected Parties engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's securities.
