This prohibition includes short-term direct dealing ... (within a period of less than three months) as well as transactions in the derivative markets ... which are short-term or speculative.
why_it_matters: There is no approval route around this, so the collar must be long-dated and defensively characterised as risk management of an existing holding rather than a speculative derivative position.

clause: Designated Persons and their Affected Parties are only permitted to buy or sell, or otherwise deal in, Company securities: during a Trading Window; and if they have received clearance in accordance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: This is a positive-permission regime with only four four-week windows a year, so entry, any roll and any unwind of the collar must each be timed into a window or need exceptional-circumstances clearance from the chair.

clause: order or otherwise authorise the dealing in Company securities within five clear trading days of receiving approval from the Authorising Officer ... if the approval is given during or after trading on one day, the order for the dealing must be lodged or otherwise authorised ... before the close of trading on the fifth trading day after the approval is given.
why_it_matters: Both derivative legs and the associated share transfer must be authorised inside a tightly defined five trading day window from approval, which constrains documentation and pricing timetables.

clause: the Company may impose such restrictions notwithstanding that the dealing in the Company's securities may otherwise be permitted under section 4.1. Any restriction communicated by the Company to any or all Designated Persons under this section 4.2 must be kept confidential
why_it_matters: An undisclosed company-imposed restriction can block entry, roll or unwind of the collar even inside a Trading Window, and the executive cannot tell the bank why.

clause: clearance can be given or refused at the discretion of the Authorising Officer, without giving reasons; clearance can be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised
why_it_matters: Approval is not a bankable condition precedent: it can be revoked at any point before the trade is authorised and no reason need be given.

clause: in relation to directors of the Company only, any other person or entity where dealing in securities of the Company by that person or entity would require disclosure to the ASX by the director. This includes where the director ... is entitled to benefit from a contract to call for or deliver securities in the Company;
why_it_matters: A director's rights under the collar are themselves a contract to call for or deliver Company securities, which points to the arrangement being a notifiable interest change requiring ASX disclosure within five business days.

clause: The Company Secretary (or a delegate) will maintain a copy of: all requests for an approval to deal in the Company's securities submitted by a Designated Person; and details of all dealings in the Company's securities by a Designated Person and their Affected Parties.
why_it_matters: The full collar and its lifecycle will sit on the company's register, so the structure cannot be kept off the company's books.

clause: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts, or contribute our securities to exchange funds in a manner that could be interpreted as hedging in our stock or otherwise limiting economic risk relating to the securities.
why_it_matters: The precise structure a funded collar uses is named as a prohibited activity for every Insider, with no vesting carve-out and no clearance route, so the transaction cannot be done without a Board waiver.

clause: Other than the exercise of equity awards issued by us, engage in transactions involving options or other derivative securities on our stock, such as puts and calls, whether on an exchange or in any other market.
why_it_matters: Documenting the put and call bilaterally with a bank rather than on an exchange does not avoid the prohibition, which expressly reaches any other market.

clause: Engage in short sales of our securities, meaning a sale of securities that you do not own, including short sales "against the box."
why_it_matters: Even a fully covered downside position against shares the executive already owns is caught, removing the usual argument that a collar over an existing holding is not a short sale.

topic: pledging is the one permitted financing route
clause: Use or pledge our securities as collateral in a margin account or as collateral for a loan (e.g. margin lending or similar funding arrangements) unless the pledge has been approved by our General Counsel and in accordance with any applicable policy or guidelines of the Company regarding pledging.
why_it_matters: The loan leg alone is achievable with General Counsel approval, so a plain share-secured loan without any hedge is the only part of the funded collar that survives, subject to unseen pledging guidelines.

clause: Our Board reserves the right in its sole discretion to modify or grant waivers to this Policy. Any amendments or waiver may be publicly disclosed if required by applicable laws, rules and regulations.
why_it_matters: The only route to a collar is an express Board waiver, which may have to be publicly disclosed under US rules, making it a high-visibility ask.

clause: Our General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer may designate special trading Blackout Periods that apply to specific individuals or groups of people ... no one may tell anyone that a special Blackout Period has been designated or that one previously was in place because that also is confidential information that cannot be disclosed internally or externally.
why_it_matters: An executive could be blocked from any permitted step, such as pledging or unwinding, without being able to explain the reason to the bank.

clause: short-term trading includes acquiring securities ... with a view to selling the securities within a 6 month period as well as selling securities with a view to repurchase within a 6 month period.
why_it_matters: The look-forward period is six months rather than the usual three, so even the share transfers and repurchases around a financing would need a longer horizon.

topic: Regulation S hedging restriction on CDIs
clause: From the ASX announcement cover page: 'the CDIs are restricted securities under Rule 144 of the Securities Act ... In addition, hedging transactions with regard to the CDIs may only be conducted in accordance with the Securities Act.'
why_it_matters: Even if the Policy were waived, US securities law independently constrains hedging of the CDIs, so the bank would need a Regulation S and Rule 144 analysis on top of the trading policy.

clause: Any approval to trade can be withdrawn or refused by the General Counsel, the Chief Financial Officer, the CEO or the Company in its discretion (and will be automatically deemed to have been withdrawn where the person seeking approval becomes aware of MNPI).
why_it_matters: Approval is not a bankable condition precedent; it lapses automatically on the executive becoming aware of material nonpublic information before execution.

topic: gifts and transfers in closed periods
clause: Unless approved in advance by our General Counsel, make a gift, charitable contribution or other transfer of our securities during a period when the Insider cannot otherwise trade.
why_it_matters: Delivering or transferring the collateral shares to a lender or custodian during a Blackout Period would itself require prior General Counsel approval.

topic: hedging ban keyed to the holding, not the instrument
clause: this policy prohibits personnel from: ... hedging performance rights, bonus entitlements or shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements;
why_it_matters: The ban is defined by which shares are hedged rather than by transaction type, so a collar is available over vested shares that are free of dealing restrictions and surplus to the minimum holding, but nothing else.

clause: selling shares held to fulfil any minimum holding requirements (unless consent is granted);
why_it_matters: The collar and the security package must be sized only to the surplus above the executive's minimum holding, because physical settlement or lender enforcement over those shares would be a prohibited sale absent consent.

topic: lender may sell at any time
clause: A lender (who is not a personnel's associate) may deal in Worley shares that they have provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan, provided that the lender complies with the law when doing so.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement rights over pledged shares are expressly preserved, including during a closed period, provided the lender is not an associate and acts in accordance with the loan terms.

topic: residual inside information risk on enforcement
clause: If the lender does so when the personnel has inside information, they may still be in breach of insider trading laws or this policy. It is personnel's responsibility to consider carefully the circumstances, if any, in which they provide Worley shares as security for a margin loan to ensure that this does not occur.
why_it_matters: The executive, not the bank, bears the risk that an enforcement sale coincides with their possession of inside information, which argues for a facility structured to avoid discretionary sales or with long cure periods.

clause: The insider trading laws, Front Page Test and notice requirements still apply in these circumstances, even if personnel are not involved in the decision to deal in Worley shares.
why_it_matters: A director or senior executive must still give Worley two business days advance notice and post-trade notice of a lender's sale, which is impractical for an unannounced enforcement and should be addressed in the facility's notification mechanics.

clause: Designated personnel are required to notify Worley of any dealing in Worley shares two business days in advance of the dealing and within two business days after the dealing. They must receive confirmation that there are no restrictions on trading in the particular circumstances before they trade.
why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and settlement of the collar each need two business days lead time and a positive no-restrictions confirmation, which sits awkwardly with market-priced derivative execution.

clause: Where consent to deal in Worley shares is required under this policy, consent will only be granted to personnel in exceptional circumstances.
why_it_matters: Any step needing consent, such as a closed period unwind or a sale of minimum-holding shares, is very unlikely to be approved, so the structure must be timed entirely outside closed periods.

clause: Worley personnel must also follow the procedures set out in the Securities Dealings Standard.
why_it_matters: The operative definitions, including what counts as short term dealing and how derivatives are treated, are in a document that is not lodged with ASX and must be obtained before the structure can be confirmed as compliant.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could I be perceived to be taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
why_it_matters: A funded collar by a senior executive is exactly the kind of arrangement this reputational test targets, and the approver may refuse or the individual may be criticised even where the technical rules are met.

clause: This policy applies to Worley personnel ... and any "associates", which are family members and controlled entities of those persons, wherever they are located. Personnel are responsible for ensuring their associates comply.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the policy, and the lender must not be an associate for the enforcement carve-out to apply.

clause: A Restricted Person must not, without prior written approval by the relevant person specified in rule 7, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example ... put and call options ...
why_it_matters: The put and call legs of a collar are expressly contemplated and are permissible with prior written approval, so the derivative side of the structure has a clear approval route rather than a prohibition.

clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with unvested securities issued pursuant to any employee option or share plan.
why_it_matters: Unusually, unvested plan securities are brought within the same approval gate rather than an absolute ban, so a collar is not automatically confined to vested shares, although approval over unvested holdings would be difficult to obtain in practice.

clause: Restricted Persons must notify the Company in advance before engaging in any margin or securities lending arrangements or granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities. ... The proposed arrangement must not be entered into or grant made until written clearance has been given by the person nominated in rule 7.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted subject to notification and written clearance, so both legs of a funded collar can be approved by the same approver.

clause: Clearance to deal in Company Securities can be revoked at any time but will otherwise be valid (unless another period is otherwise specified in the clearance) for a period of ten trading days commencing on the date following the clearance being obtained.
why_it_matters: A ten trading day window is long enough to document and price a collar, but the unrestricted revocation right means the bank should not rely on clearance surviving to settlement and should build a termination right for revoked clearance.

clause: In determining whether to clear the proposed dealing, the relevant person nominated in rule 7 will consider whether the proposed dealing is appropriate having regard to all relevant circumstances.
why_it_matters: There is no SLA, no criteria and no appeal, so approval of a collar turns entirely on the Chair's or Board's view of appropriateness and cannot be assumed.

clause: Rule 6.10 requires clearance for margin and securities lending and encumbrances but says nothing about margin calls, forced sales, price triggers or what happens if the lender sells during a blackout period.
why_it_matters: The policy gives the executive no protection if the bank enforces during a blackout, so enforcement and physical settlement mechanics must be negotiated into the loan and collar documents rather than relied on from the policy.

clause: any other period that the Company specifies from time to time
why_it_matters: Ad hoc blackouts with no stated notice or duration can block entry, roll, unwind or settlement of the collar at any time.

clause: If a Restricted Person needs to deal in the Company Securities due to exceptional circumstances ... the Restricted Person must apply to the person specified in rule 7 for a waiver ... in each circumstance the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 2 business days.
why_it_matters: A blackout-period unwind or settlement is theoretically possible on a severe financial hardship or court order waiver, but only for 2 business days and only on evidence that dealing is the most reasonable course available.

clause: their associates (as defined in the Takeovers Code)
why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the clearance and notification gates, since associates are themselves Restricted Persons.

clause: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain or short sell any Company Securities.
why_it_matters: No fixed period is set, so a short-dated collar or one with knock-out features could be characterised as short term or speculative; a longer tenor and physical settlement reduce that risk.

topic: collar named in the derivative definition
clause: Derivative includes a derivative within the meaning of section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as an option, forward contract, swap, future, warrant, cap and collar) and any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities.
why_it_matters: The policy names a collar as a Derivative product, so the derivative legs of a funded collar fall squarely within the section 5.1 prohibition and cannot be argued outside it.

topic: hedging ban reaches all shares and all staff
clause: No Employee may enter into any agreement, arrangement or scheme ... whereby the Employee changes the economic benefit or risk derived by the Employee in relation to any holding of Breville shares or an equity-based incentive award or grant ...
why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to plan or unvested securities and applies to every director, employee, contractor and consultant, so there is no class of shares or class of person over whom a collar could be written.

topic: no waiver of the hedging ban
clause: Section 4.4 permits approval to deal during a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances; it relieves only the Closed Period restriction and no provision permits a waiver of section 5.1.
why_it_matters: Even severe financial hardship or a court order gives no route to a permitted collar; the only relief available goes to timing, not to the prohibited structure.

clause: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties may not include their Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement without first seeking the approval of the Chair using the approval procedures described in section 4.3 above.
why_it_matters: A loan secured on Breville shares is permitted with the Chair's approval, so the funding leg is available in isolation even though the protective legs of a collar are not.

topic: approved lender enforcement is an excluded dealing
clause: an involuntary disposal of Breville Securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending arrangement (provided the arrangement was previously approved in accordance with this policy).
why_it_matters: Unusually protective: a bank enforcing over collateral, including during a Closed Period, does not breach the policy so long as the facility was approved up front, which makes a plain secured loan workable.

topic: no rehypothecation or lending of collateral
clause: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties are also prohibited from “lending” their Breville Securities to any other party for the purposes of short selling, Securities lending or for any other purpose.
why_it_matters: Any structure in which the bank borrows or rehypothecates the pledged shares to hedge its own position is prohibited, so collateral must be held on a no-reuse basis.

topic: forward contracts caught by the short-term rule
clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period or entering into other short-term dealings such as forward contracts.
why_it_matters: A forward or short-dated derivative is independently prohibited as short-term dealing, so tenor cannot be used to cure the section 5.1 problem.

clause: The approver may refuse a request, impose conditions on a proposed dealing or revoke a previously granted request, and in each case is not obliged to provide reasons for their action. Any refusal to approve a request will be final and binding, and the person seeking approval must keep that decision confidential.
why_it_matters: Approval for the financing leg can be revoked or conditioned without reasons and lapses after 5 business days, so the bank should not treat an approval as a durable condition precedent.

clause: Closely Connected Parties includes: certain family members of a Restricted Person, such as their spouse and dependent children; and any entity which the Restricted Person or a person referred to in (a) above controls or has an ability to control.
why_it_matters: Routing a collar through a spouse or a controlled trust or company does not avoid the prohibitions, and section 5.1 in any event binds the Employee personally.

clause: Restricted Employees must not ... enter into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Sims’ securities;
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for every director, officer, KMP and executive, with no approval or hardship route.

topic: derivatives ban with no venue limit
clause: trade in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims’ securities;
why_it_matters: The purchased put and written call are derivative products in respect of Sims' securities, so the protective legs are prohibited regardless of whether they are exchange-traded or written OTC by a bank.

clause: enter into any hedging arrangements that limit exposure to Sims’ securities.
why_it_matters: The prohibition is not confined to unvested or plan securities, so even a collar over long-held, freely tradeable shares is caught.

clause: Dealing includes any transaction or change affecting title to, or an interest in securities, such as buying, selling or transferring shares, using Sims’ shares as security for a loan and entering into an agreement (or exercising an option) to buy or sell securities.
why_it_matters: Granting the bank security over the shares is itself a dealing, so it is caught by black-out periods and the approval process even before the secured financing ban is reached.

clause: The exceptional circumstances mechanism permits an Employee 'who need[s] to sell (but not buy) Sims’ securities during a black-out period' to seek approval; nothing in the policy permits approval of a restricted dealing.
why_it_matters: Even severe financial hardship gives access only to a sale during a black-out period, never to a collar or a secured loan, so there is no route to the structure at all.

topic: restrictions follow the tier, not the person
clause: there are certain Employees that will be notified by the Company Secretary that they are restricted employees ... Restricted Employees include: Directors and Officers ... Key Management Personnel ... Executives
why_it_matters: The bans bite on exactly the population a bank would target for a funded collar, while ordinary employees, who face no such bans, are not a commercially relevant client group.

clause: Persons closely associated with Employees (including Restricted Employees) are subject to the same dealing restrictions that apply to that Employee ... companies, trusts, partnerships or entities ... the economic interests of which are substantially equivalent to the Employee or a family member.
why_it_matters: The economic equivalence limb defeats any attempt to place the collar or the loan in a family trust, controlled company or other vehicle.

clause: How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
why_it_matters: Even for a dealing that is not prohibited, the Company Secretary applies a reputational perception test, and a director hedging their exposure would rarely survive it.

clause: Upon receipt of approval, complete the dealing within two business days (commencing the day after approval is provided) otherwise approval must be sought again. ... Approval to deal can be withdrawn if circumstances change.
why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be documented and executed inside two business days and approval can be withdrawn, which would be impractical for a negotiated derivative even if one were permitted.

clause: Margin lending refers to any arrangement which is in the nature of, or parties intend it to be in the nature of, loaned monies which are secured or are otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities (regardless of the form the security or transfer takes).
why_it_matters: The definition is drafted to defeat form-based structuring, so a bespoke bank loan, a limited recourse facility or a title transfer collateral arrangement supporting the collar is all margin lending and prohibited for Directors and KMP.

topic: prohibition bites on the dealing, not just the loan
clause: Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into any dealing in EMR securities where such margin lending arrangements apply.
why_it_matters: It is the dealing itself that is banned once a margin lending arrangement applies, so the collar legs and the pledge fall together with the loan rather than being severable from it.

clause: EMR Staff are not permitted to enter into 'hedge contracts' or other forms of arrangements which may have the effect of fixing the value of, or return on, securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package (whether the securities are fully vested or not).
why_it_matters: Any share traceable to an LTI grant or to incentive remuneration can never be collared, however long ago it vested, so only shares bought or subscribed for independently are candidates.

clause: The policy contains no general hedging, derivatives or short selling prohibition; section 11 is confined to incentive securities and section 9 to margin lending.
why_it_matters: An unfunded collar over shares that a Director bought on market is not prohibited, and would need only the Chairman's written approval outside a blackout period; the funding leg is what makes the structure impossible.

clause: In all cases, approval is to be given by the Chairman or Managing Director acting in accordance with this policy.
why_it_matters: There is no stated validity period, response time, revocation right or condition-imposing power, so the parties must agree contractually how long an approval is treated as good for.

clause: there may be occasions when the EMR board imposes a suspension on the ability of Staff to trade at a time when trading might otherwise have been allowed ... If a suspension occurs, Staff must not trade while the suspension is in force.
why_it_matters: An ad hoc suspension can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and only financial hardship approval by the Chairman relieves a blackout, not a suspension.

clause: the blackout period starts 10 business days before the planned date for release of the relevant quarterly report ... and ends on the business day after the day of release
why_it_matters: As a quarterly reporting explorer EMR has four blackout periods a year rather than two, materially narrowing the windows in which a collar could be entered or unwound.

clause: Staff shall not engage in speculative trading whereby EMR securities are purchased with a view to selling or otherwise dealing (including by way of a sale and subsequent purchase) in those securities within a 6 month period.
why_it_matters: Tenor should exceed six months, and shares recently acquired should not be collared, since the arrangement could be read as purchase with a view to otherwise dealing.

clause: This Policy applies equally to any dealings in EMR securities by a Staff's spouse, partner or by or on behalf of any dependent child, family company or family trust.
why_it_matters: Placing the shares, the pledge or the derivative in a family company or trust does not avoid the margin lending or hedge contract prohibitions.

clause: Every Company Insider is prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities such as put, call, or short sale.
why_it_matters: Both legs of a collar, the purchased put and the written call, are named prohibited positions, so the derivative side of the structure is impossible for any Insider with no approval route.

clause: Company Insiders include: commissioners, directors, or employees of the Company; Major shareholders of the Company; Individuals who, due to their position or profession or to their business relation with the Company, are allowed to gain Insider Information; or Any parties which, within the past 6 (six) months, no longer become any Party referred to above. 'Business relation' ... includes customer relation, supplier, contractor, client, and creditor.
why_it_matters: A bank that becomes a creditor of the Company could itself fall within the Insider definition, and a departing executive remains an Insider for six months, so the prohibition follows the client past resignation.

clause: Every Company Insider is prohibited to give or cause anyone to transfer Company Securities during a period where they are not allowed to conduct trading.
why_it_matters: Delivery of collateral, physical settlement or a financier's enforcement sale occurring inside a blackout would be an Insider causing a transfer when not permitted to trade, and there is no lender enforcement carve-out.

clause: Company Insiders are not allowed to disclose to any outside party that a certain blackout period has been determined.
why_it_matters: A client cannot tell a bank why an execution, roll or unwind is being delayed, so a facility must tolerate unexplained inability to act.

topic: quarterly closed periods with open-ended end
clause: Blackout period commences on 30 March, 29 June, 29 September, and 30 December every year and ends when the company disseminates information which previously is non-public information.
why_it_matters: Four blackouts a year, each of indeterminate length because it ends only on results dissemination, leaves narrow and unpredictable windows for any transaction in the shares.

clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, pledges, charges or securities lending.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the shares is neither prohibited nor regulated, so it is governed only by Indonesian law and the Company's other rules, and a bank would need separate confirmation from the Corporate Secretary rather than reliance on this Policy.

clause: every trading of Company Securities by Company Insiders must be reported in advance to the Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer. ... Company Insiders are required to report/confirm to the Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer after a Company Securities trading transaction has been done.
why_it_matters: The regime is notification rather than approval, with no validity period or response time, so any permitted share transaction supporting a financing must be pre-notified with reasons and confirmed afterwards.

clause: The parties included in the scope of this Policy are also responsible for ensuring the compliance of their families, including all their close relatives with this Policy.
why_it_matters: The prohibitions cannot be avoided by placing the position with a family member, although the Policy does not extend expressly to trusts or controlled companies.

clause: The Policy is a 2008 board decision translated from Indonesian, with no review date, no derivatives or financing framework and no cross-reference to ASX Listing Rule 12.12 content requirements.
why_it_matters: Its silences should be treated as gaps to be checked with the Corporate Secretary rather than as permissions, and a bank should confirm no later Indonesian or ASX-facing policy supersedes it.

clause: No Director or member of the ELT may enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company securities.
why_it_matters: The only funding prohibition bites on borrowing used to acquire Company shares, so a loan secured on shares the executive already owns, drawn to fund something else, is outside the ban on its literal terms, though a bank should expect the substance over form clause to be raised if the facility is characterised as a share-funding arrangement.

clause: Sections 4.3, 5.1 and 5.2 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Enforcement by the bank over the collared shares, including in a blackout period, is an excluded dealing needing no approval, which removes the enforcement risk that defeats a funded collar under most other ASX policies.

clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: Forwards are singled out as the example of a prohibited short term dealing, so a collar should have a tenor comfortably beyond three months and avoid a forward-sale characterisation or early termination triggers.

clause: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or Director equity plan operated by the Company.
why_it_matters: The collarable pool is defined by plan documents outside the policy, so the bank must confirm from the plan rules and the register that the specific parcel is vested and lock-free.

topic: substance over form and Front Page Test
clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it. ... Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Approval for a collar can be refused purely on perception grounds even where no rule is broken, and a structure that looks like a disguised sale or a disguised margin loan can be treated as one.

clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. ... the approved dealing must occur as soon as possible, and no later than 3 business days following approval.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both collar legs must complete inside three business days of approval, and the approval can be withdrawn up to signing without reasons.

clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a controlled company or family trust does not avoid the approval requirement or the hedging bans.

clause: TWE People must not deal in the Company's securities if ... the Company has notified TWE People that they must not deal in securities (either for a specified period, or until the Company gives further notice).
why_it_matters: An open-ended company notice can block entry, roll or unwind of a collar at any time, and it binds all employees, not just Restricted Persons.

clause: Certain parts of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons.
why_it_matters: Blackout periods and prior approval do not apply to employees outside the Restricted Persons list, so for them a collar over vested unrestricted shares needs no company consent at all.

clause: Approval must be obtained in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Securities; and transferring Securities in Ventia into an existing margin loan account.
why_it_matters: Ventia regulates rather than prohibits borrowing against its shares, so the loan leg of a funded collar has an approval pathway instead of an outright bar, and the same approval route covers moving existing shares into a lender's account.

clause: Ventia may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 4.4 conditional upon such terms and conditions as Ventia sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The company can dictate the enforcement mechanics of the facility as a condition of approval, so a bank should expect its close-out and top-up rights to be negotiated with Ventia before the facility is signed.

clause: Sections 3.3, 4.1 and 4.3 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Enforcement by the bank over the collared shares, including during a Blackout Period, is an Excluded Dealing needing no clearance, which materially de-risks the security package.

clause: Securities means ... any rights to subscribe for, acquire or dispose of securities (including future contracts, options, performance rights, share rights or other interests); derivatives and other financial products covered by section 1042A ... whose price or value is linked to the price or value of any of the securities referred to in (i) to (v) above.
why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call written with a bank are themselves Securities and dealing in them is squarely within the clearance requirement and the Blackout Periods.

clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling Securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: Forwards are the named example of prohibited short term dealing, so a collar should run well beyond three months and avoid a prepaid-forward characterisation or short-dated roll structure.

clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision and may revoke their approval at any time prior to the Dealing. ... the approved Dealing ... must occur within 2 business days following approval.
why_it_matters: Both legs and the facility drawdown must be executed inside two business days of clearance, and clearance can be pulled without reasons at any point before signing.

clause: Approval will not be granted to Ventia Personnel to Deal in Ventia Securities where the Dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: A collar can be refused purely on perception grounds even where no substantive rule is breached, and there is no appeal or reasons requirement.

clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only Deal in Securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to Deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Holding the collared parcel through a controlled trust or company does not escape the clearance requirement, the hedging bans or the margin lending approval.

clause: The policy contains a Front Page Test but no substance over form or anti-avoidance provision.
why_it_matters: Unlike several peer policies, Ventia has no express anti-avoidance hook to recharacterise a collar-plus-loan, so the analysis turns on the literal wording of sections 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6.

clause: the Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by WAF or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable
why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: a collar is permitted only where it protects collateral for a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of WAF options, or protects against a tax liability, so a funded collar raised for liquidity, diversification or general purposes is prohibited outright, while an option-exercise-funding facility with a protective collar fits the wording precisely.

clause: the Derivative has a maturity date that falls outside a Prohibited Period
why_it_matters: Because Prohibited Periods run for one week before to one business day after every quarterly, half year and annual report, the expiry date of both collar legs must be diarised around a dense quarterly reporting calendar, and any roll or extension must land on a clear date.

clause: WAF is not a counterparty to the Derivative
why_it_matters: A bank counterparty is expressly contemplated and permitted; only the company itself is excluded.

clause: the relevant securities are fully vested
why_it_matters: Performance options and performance rights cannot be collared until vesting, and there is no Board waiver of this criterion.

clause: Key Management Personnel should ensure that when arranging finance either for themselves or through their Related Persons, where WAF securities are provided as collateral, such obligations do not conflict with their obligations under this policy. In particular, Key Management Personnel should ensure that the terms of any margin lending arrangements do not require dealings in WAF securities at a time when Key Management Personnel are prohibited from dealing.
why_it_matters: The facility must be drafted so that no mandatory sale, top-up or delivery obligation can be triggered during a Prohibited Period, which constrains margin call mechanics even though section 6(b)(ii) excludes an actual enforcement sale from the policy.

clause: The following dealings ... are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... The disposing of securities ... as a result of a secured lender exercising its right under a margin lending arrangement;
why_it_matters: An enforcement sale by the lender sits outside the policy entirely, including during a Prohibited Period, which protects the executive if the bank has to realise the collateral.

clause: The Board may seek information from Key Management Personnel about their level of ownership of WAF's securities and about any encumbrances granted or margin loans taken out in respect of those securities. The Board may also require them to keep the Company Secretary informed of changes to such information.
why_it_matters: The security package over the collared shares is disclosable to the Board on demand and, through the continuous disclosure hook, potentially to the market.

clause: Key Management Personnel are required to notify WAF of all intended dealings in WAF's securities ... two business days before such intended dealings.
why_it_matters: Outside Prohibited Periods there is no approval gate at all, only a two business day advance notice and a post-trade price confirmation, so execution timing is within the executive's control, but the notice period must be built into pricing.

clause: The Board may on application exempt Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons from this prohibition in exceptional circumstances.
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies the three month holding period ban can be waived by the Board, which gives a route to unwind or restructure a collar inside three months.

clause: Subject to the law, Designated Persons and their closely related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act) must not ... deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.
why_it_matters: This is the clause that defeats the collar: unlike the remuneration hedging ban in 31(a), it is not limited to unvested or locked shares, covers derivatives created by third parties including OTC options, swaps and forwards, and extends to closely related parties, and nothing in Appendix 1 permits a hedge.

clause: except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy
why_it_matters: Read literally, 'permitted by law' could swallow the prohibition, since a collar over vested shares held without inside information is lawful; the drafting is ambiguous and would need a written ruling from the General Counsel & Company Secretary before a bank could rely on it.

clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Company Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult the General Counsel & Company Secretary or Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on BOQ shares is expressly outside the margin lending ban and needs no approval or disclosure, so the obstacle to a funded collar is the derivative legs, not the financing.

clause: Examples of prohibited arrangements: a. a put option on variable remuneration;
why_it_matters: The purchased put over plan-sourced shares is the exact structure the policy names as prohibited, so there is no room to argue the ban was not aimed at collars.

topic: forced sale carve-out with a margin lending exception
clause: (lender disposal) a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement if the agreement is prohibited by this policy;
why_it_matters: Enforcement over the shares by a bank under a permitted, non-margin facility can proceed at any time including in a Prohibited Period, but if the facility were later characterised as a margin loan the executive loses that protection and the enforcement sale becomes a policy breach.

topic: 30 day short term test covering derivatives
clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Company Securities or in derivatives or other financial products issued over or in respect of Company Securities. Short term means in less than a 30 day period.
why_it_matters: Even if the derivatives ban were relaxed, any collar or roll with a tenor under 30 days would independently breach the policy, and 'speculative' is undefined.

clause: A confirmation confirms that the proposed dealing by the Designated Person is within the terms of the Securities Trading Policy but does not otherwise constitute approval or endorsement by the Company or the Notification Officer for the proposed dealing.
why_it_matters: The clearance is a compliance check with a 3 business day life, not an endorsement, and a Notification Officer cannot confirm a dealing that paragraph 31 prohibits.

clause: Associates of a Designated Person include ... any trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which a Designated Person has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence, companies in which a Designated Person may control directly or indirectly, nominees ...
why_it_matters: Holding the collared parcel through a trust, nominee or controlled company does not avoid paragraph 31, which binds closely related parties directly.

clause: any extension to a closed period, and any additional period (conditionally or unconditionally), as specified by the Chairman, MD & CEO or CFO of the Company.
why_it_matters: Three officers can extend or add Prohibited Periods conditionally at short notice, so any structure requiring a dealing on a fixed future date carries timing risk.

clause: apply to participate in any of the Company's executive share plans and request the transfer of unrestricted Securities from the trustee to an executive
why_it_matters: The policy is silent on unvested or restricted plan securities generally; it treats a funded collar over already-vested, unrestricted shares the same as any other Dealing, with no vesting-based carve-out or restriction beyond the general prohibitions.

clause: Each Restricted Person must take reasonable steps to prevent any of their connected persons from dealing with Securities in any way that is prohibited under this Securities Trading Policy.
why_it_matters: A collar or loan routed through a spouse, family trust, or a company in which the executive holds 20%+ is not exempt from the bans; the Restricted Person must proactively prevent it, so structuring through an associate does not avoid the prohibitions.

clause: In exceptional circumstances only, the Chairman has the discretion to grant an exemption to the prohibition on dealing in the Company's securities during the Closed Periods... No exemption will be granted if the Chairman... considers that a Restricted Person possesses (or may reasonably be presumed to possess) Price Sensitive Information that has not been disclosed to the ASX or NZX.
why_it_matters: Collar execution inside a Closed Period is not automatically fatal since a narrow Chairman-level exemption exists, but it cannot be relied upon, is barred whenever price-sensitive information is held, and offers no relief from the separate hedging or margin-lending bans.

topic: margin-call forced sale as short-term trading
clause: this prohibition applies to any: ... trades undertaken by margin lenders to close out margin calls
why_it_matters: A lender's forced close-out sale within six months of the underlying shares' acquisition is deemed prohibited speculative trading in its own right, so any funded structure needs the underlying shares to have been held for more than six months and a tenor that avoids triggering a forced sale within that window.

topic: no venue limitation on hedging/derivatives ban
clause: must not engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which limit the economic risk related to the Company's Securities
why_it_matters: There is no OTC/exchange distinction, so an OTC purchased put and written call with a bank falls squarely within the absolute hedging and derivatives ban applying to every Director, employee and contractor, independent of the loan leg or approval status.

clause: the Chairman will seek to determine if he believes that the Company is in possession of inside information or that such proposed trade is, for any other reason, not in the best interests of the Company.
why_it_matters: Clearance for the collar legs, and for any later unwind, roll or physical settlement, rests on an unbounded discretion that can be exercised against a hedging or financing structure purely on optics, so no leg of the trade can be assumed to be approvable.

clause: it is prohibited ... that [a Person] trade in the Company's securities or in any derivatives created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: Entering, unwinding or settling the put and call is barred from 2 business days before each quarterly, half-year and full-year results announcement, which given quarterly reporting closes the window four times a year.

clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, charges, pledges, hedging or short selling.
why_it_matters: The loan secured on the collared shares is not prohibited by the policy, so the bank's constraints come from the Corporations Act, ASX disclosure and any plan rules or employment terms rather than from this document; the absence of any forced-sale clause also means the policy is silent on a lender selling into a closed period.

clause: The policy makes no reference to employee equity plans, unvested securities, performance rights or options issued as remuneration.
why_it_matters: Nothing in the policy limits a collar to vested shares, but nothing exempts plan securities from the clearance or short-term rules either, so any plan documents must be checked separately for hedging or disposal restrictions.

clause: Short-term trading means buying and selling the same security within 30 days.
why_it_matters: A collar established and unwound inside 30 days, or one whose legs are opened and closed against each other in that period, risks being characterised as short-term trading, so tenor should comfortably exceed 30 days.

clause: Such approval would not constitute a representation that such person would not be in breach of the law in so trading, as it is such person's obligation to make such determination.
why_it_matters: Chairman clearance gives the bank no comfort that the director is free of inside information, so the bank must obtain its own representations at each of entry, roll and settlement.

clause: each Director shall promptly (within one business day) report to the Company officer maintaining that register the details of any change in such holdings of such Director.
why_it_matters: A change in a Director's holdings caused by physical settlement, share transfer to a security trustee or lender enforcement must be reported within one business day, on top of the Appendix 3Y/3Z regime.

clause: not engage in "short-term" trading in securities in the Company or in any close business associate (such as a joint venture partner, major supplier, major buyer etc) of the Company.
why_it_matters: The short-term ban reaches beyond the Company's own securities, so a basket or index hedge containing joint venture partner securities could be caught.

clause: The policy is expressed to apply to 'employees, consultants and Directors' and to 'Persons'; it does not define associates, spouses, dependants or controlled entities.
why_it_matters: There is no express extension to family trusts or controlled companies, so the policy's own reach over a collar held through such a vehicle is untested, though the insider trading law and the procuring provisions still apply.

topic: secured lending is clearance-gated, not banned
clause: Liontown Personnel must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 8.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is expressly permitted subject to prior written clearance rather than prohibited, which is the single most important difference from policies that ban secured financing outright.

topic: hedging is clearance-gated for vested holdings
clause: Liontown Personnel must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs are permissible with clearance over vested unrestricted shares, and the clearance form has a dedicated field for section 12 details, so the structure must be disclosed to the Approving Officer in full.

clause: Liontown Personnel are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
why_it_matters: The collar must be sized strictly to vested shares; no Approving Officer discretion can cure a hedge that reaches unvested performance rights or options, and over-hedging vested holdings risks being characterised as hedging the unvested tail.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 6].
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the Blackout Period restrictions, so lender enforcement during a closed period does not itself breach the policy, though section 8's blanket clearance requirement for Restricted Persons is not in terms disapplied and the carve-out does not displace the insider trading law.

clause: Written clearance can be withdrawn by the Approving Officer at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised, if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: Pricing risk sits with the client: a cleared collar can be pulled before execution, so the bank should not commit hedge or funding until the trade is actually lodged.

clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of 3 business days from the time which it is given or such other period as may be determined by the Approving Officer. The expiry time of the clearance will be stated in the clearance granted.
why_it_matters: The default execution window is only 3 business days, but the form lets the Approving Officer specify a longer bespoke period, which can be requested up front to accommodate documentation and settlement of a collar and loan.

clause: Any request for written clearance can be given or refused by the Approving Officer in their absolute discretion. ... Where a waiver is refused, it is final and binding on the Restricted Person and the Restricted Person must keep all information relating to the waiver confidential.
why_it_matters: There is no appeal and no reasons requirement, so the bank cannot assume approval of a collar and the client may be unable to explain a refusal to the bank.

clause: Liontown Personnel must not trade in Company Securities within any period imposed by the Board (or its delegate) from time to time ... Liontown Personnel must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: Undisclosed Additional Periods can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and the client is barred from telling the bank why.

clause: Any Liontown Personnel who holds Company Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) ... will be unable to trade in those securities during that time.
why_it_matters: Escrowed shares cannot be delivered to a security trustee or sold on enforcement, so only unrestricted vested shares can serve as collateral for the loan.

clause: Liontown Personnel must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The prohibition is undefined and qualitative, so a short-dated collar, an early unwind or a cash-settled structure could be characterised as speculative trading in Company Securities, and tenor and settlement mechanics should be raised with the Approving Officer at clearance.

clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through a family trust, controlled company or spouse does not avoid the clearance requirements for hedging or secured lending.

clause: If before carrying out the trade, the Restricted Person comes into possession of Inside Information or a Prohibited Period commences, that person must not carry out the trade, notwithstanding that it has been approved.
why_it_matters: Approval lapses automatically on the onset of inside information or a blackout, so the bank needs a fresh representation at signing and at each subsequent settlement or roll.

clause: written clearance granted under this policy is never an endorsement of the proposed trade or a confirmation regarding the absence of Inside Information.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on the Approving Officer's clearance as diligence and must take its own representations from the client.

topic: exceptional circumstances gate on hedging and security
clause: If you are a Restricted Person ... who wishes to engage in speculative trading or grant security over your Megaport Securities, but cannot do so because of this Policy, you may apply for permission to trade if exceptional circumstances exist. ... Written Clearance can only be given if ... the proposed trade is not for speculative gain ... and exceptional circumstances exist justifying the issue of the Written Clearance.
why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause for a funded collar: both the derivative legs and the security over the shares are routed to a clearance that on its face is only available in exceptional circumstances such as financial hardship or a court order, so an ordinary portfolio-diversification collar is very unlikely to be approvable.

topic: security arrangements are gated, not banned
clause: you must not, unless you have Written Clearance, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (such as a charge, mortgage or pledge) over any of your Megaport Securities (including those Megaport Securities which are unvested or the subject of a holding lock) to secure your obligations to any third party, including a margin lender.
why_it_matters: The loan leg is not prohibited outright and can even in principle cover unvested or holding-locked shares, but it needs Written Clearance and reaches indirect security, so a security trustee or back-to-back arrangement does not avoid it.

clause: This Policy does not apply to: ... disposal of Megaport Securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the Megaport Securities.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale is entirely outside the Policy, so lender enforcement during a Closed Period or Board-imposed Restricted Period does not breach it, although the Corporations Act insider trading prohibition still applies to the disposal.

clause: The Authorisation requirement table (Chair to Chair of the Audit Committee; CEO or a director other than the Chairperson to the Chair; all other Executive Management to the CEO) differs from the Authorised Trading table (Chair to two non-executive directors or a non-executive director and the CEO or CFO; CEO or a director other than the Chair to two directors; any other Restricted Person to the CEO).
why_it_matters: A hedging or security arrangement is an Authorised Trading matter, so a director needs sign-off from two directors rather than the Chair alone, which raises the approval bar and lengthens the timetable for documenting a collar.

clause: Unless otherwise specified in the Written Clearance and provided the Written Clearance has not been withdrawn, trades and other dealings in Megaport Securities that have received Written Clearance must be made within 7 days of the date of that Written Clearance.
why_it_matters: The collar legs and the security must be executed within 7 days of clearance unless a longer period is written into the clearance, so documentation should be fully negotiated before clearance is sought.

clause: Authorised Officers have absolute discretion to give or refuse Written Clearance and to withdraw Written Clearance if new information comes to light. The Authorised Officer's decisions are final and if you are refused Written Clearance you must keep that refusal confidential.
why_it_matters: Clearance can be pulled before execution and a refusal cannot be explained to the bank, so the bank should not commit funding or hedge until the trade is done.

clause: the proposed trade is not for speculative gain, to take advantage of Inside information or likely to be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair.
why_it_matters: An optics test sits alongside the legal tests, and a director monetising a large stake through a bank collar is exactly the kind of transaction that could be judged likely to be seen as unfair.

clause: A Restricted Person who would be prohibited from trading under this Policy must not trade through any member of their family, or through a trust or company over which they have influence or control.
why_it_matters: Controlled Entities are themselves Restricted Persons, so holding the collared shares through a family trust or company gains nothing and the same Written Clearance is needed.

clause: All requests to buy or sell Megaport Securities must include: ... the intended volume of securities to be purchased or sold; an estimated time frame for the sale or purchase; and a statement that the person is not in possession of any Inside information.
why_it_matters: The Authorised Officer must be given the size and timing of the trade, so the notional, tenor and settlement mechanics of the collar cannot be kept confidential from the Company.

clause: Closed Period ... (a) in respect of Board members and Executive Management ... from 9 June ... from 10 December ... four weeks prior to the conclusion of the annual general meeting; (b) in respect of all other Restricted Persons ... four weeks prior to the announcement ... two weeks prior to the conclusion of the annual general meeting.
why_it_matters: Directors and Executive Management face materially longer closed periods, roughly 9 June to the full year result and 10 December to the half year result plus an AGM window, so open windows for entering or unwinding a collar are narrow.

clause: If you trade in Megaport Securities you must notify the Company Secretary of the details of all completed transactions within 14 days after each transaction. This is necessary whether or not authorisation or Written Clearance was required prior to trading.
why_it_matters: Every leg, roll and settlement of the collar must be reported to the Company Secretary and recorded on the register, and directors must report within 2 days for Appendix 3Y purposes.

clause: This Policy applies to the securities of other companies if: the other company is a joint venture or collaborative partner of Megaport; ... or Megaport has a substantial interest (5% or more) in the other company.
why_it_matters: The clearance and closed period regime extends to securities of certain counterparties, so a basket hedge that includes those names would also be caught.

clause: A Restricted Person must not engage in transactions designed to hedge their exposure to Company Securities.
why_it_matters: This single sentence defeats a funded collar: the put and call legs are transactions designed to hedge exposure, the ban has no approval or waiver route and no vesting-state carve-out, and it applies to every Restricted Person and their Closely Connected Persons.

topic: financing is approvable but hedging is not
clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, unless the prior approval of the Chairman (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.
why_it_matters: The loan leg alone is available with Chairman approval, so an unhedged secured loan against BSP shares is possible even though the collar that would normally accompany it is not.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain, including on-market short-term buying and selling, forward contracts and short-selling. BSP considers "short-term" to be a period of 6 months or less.
why_it_matters: Forward contracts are prohibited by name, closing off prepaid forwards and forward-sale monetisations as an alternative to a collar, and any hedge unwound within 6 months would independently breach the short-term ban.

clause: A waiver will only be granted if ... the Restricted Person is selling not buying Company Securities.
why_it_matters: Even the exceptional circumstances route cannot authorise buying a put or entering a derivative position, so there is no discretionary path to a collar; the only sanctioned way to raise cash against a holding is an outright sale or an approved secured loan.

clause: All periods that are not Trading Windows are "closed periods" for the purposes of the Listing Rules, during which time Restricted Persons are prohibited from dealing in Company Securities. ... A Trading Window may be varied, suspended or withdrawn by the Board at any time.
why_it_matters: Dealing is prohibited by default and permitted only inside four announced windows totalling roughly 70 business days a year, and the Board can suspend a window at any moment, so any transaction timetable is fragile.

topic: no assumption of an open window
clause: Restricted Persons may not assume that a Trading Window is open, even after the relevant results announcement.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot infer an open window from the results calendar and must see the Company Secretary's written notification before any leg is executed.

topic: five day notice and five day execution
clause: made in writing to the respective persons specified in clause 3.11 at least 5 Business Days prior to the proposed dealing taking place ... If approved, the confirmation must specify a period of time of no more than 5 Business Days within which the dealing must be completed.
why_it_matters: Five business days' advance notice plus a maximum five business day execution window means pricing must be arranged in advance and cannot be left to the moment of approval.

clause: Prior notification, its receipt, any acknowledgement of or response to any such notification is not an endorsement, approval or recommendation of the proposed dealing. Restricted Persons remain responsible for their own investment decisions and compliance with applicable laws and this Policy.
why_it_matters: Chairman or Company Secretary sign-off gives the bank no comfort, so it must take its own representations on inside information and policy compliance.

clause: where a Restricted Person has been granted approval to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements (see clause 3.8.3), an involuntary disposal of securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement;
why_it_matters: The lender's enforcement sale is permitted outside a Trading Window only if the financing itself was approved in advance, so an unapproved facility leaves the client in breach on enforcement.

clause: Each Restricted Person must ensure that: any dealing by their Closely Connected Persons are undertaken in accordance with this Policy ... Closely Connected Entity: Any family company or family trust that the Restricted Person or their close family member(s) may control or have an interest in.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban and financing gate reach family trusts and companies in which the person merely has an interest, so no holding structure escapes them.

clause: Under the Papua New Guinea Capital Market Act 2015, Australian Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), PNGX Listing Rules, ASX Listing Rules, SPX Listing Rules ... Where this Policy is inconsistent with an applicable law, regulation or prudential standard within a relevant jurisdiction, the Policy applies only to the extent applicable.
why_it_matters: BSP is PNG-incorporated and triple listed, so any structure must clear PNG capital markets law and Bank of PNG prudential standards as well as Australian law, and disclosure runs to three exchanges.

clause: Restricted Persons must keep, and make available to the Company Secretary ... on request, a register of dealings by themselves and their Closely Connected Persons, in the form of a record of every dealing, together with supporting material such as contract notes or their equivalent.
why_it_matters: Every leg of any structure must be documented and producible to the Company on demand, so nothing about a financing arrangement can be kept private from BSP.

clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with Company Securities including Securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.
why_it_matters: The collar's put and call legs need prior written approval from the rule 7 approver even if written over unvested or holding-locked equity award shares, not only fully vested unrestricted stock.

clause: The policy contains no provision addressing margin lending, encumbrance, custodial transfer or any other secured financing arrangement over Company Securities.
why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not expressly prohibited or made subject to clearance or disclosure, but the bank should obtain the Company's written confirmation, since the broad 'vary economic risk' language in 6.9 could arguably be read by the Company to capture the financing structure as a whole.

clause: If granted, trading consent is only valid for a period of 5 trading days after notification of approval. Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.
why_it_matters: The collar must be priced and executed within 5 trading days of clearance, and clearance evaporates automatically if inside information arises beforehand, so timing risk sits with the executive and the bank.

clause: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn or refused by the Company in its discretion without giving any reasons... the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: The Company can refuse or withdraw clearance for the collar without explanation, and the executive cannot disclose a refusal to the bank, which is a practical execution risk for the transaction timeline.

clause: their associates (as defined in the Corporations Act) including, close family members and trusts and entities controlled by them
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled entity does not escape the clearance and hedging restrictions that apply to the Restricted Person.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested and locked securities
clause: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan (which includes Designated Persons) are prohibited from entering into a transaction that limits the economic risk of unvested Company Securities or vested Company Securities that are subject to a restriction on transfer, such as a holding lock.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban stops at vesting and release of the holding lock, so a collar over vested, unrestricted shares is not caught by it and remains available subject to clearance.

clause: Approval must be obtained prior to a Designated Person entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities. Such Dealings would cover: (a) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Company Securities; (b) transferring Company Securities into an existing margin loan account; and (c) selling Company Securities to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban all secured financing, AUB only requires Chair approval, so the loan leg of a funded collar is permissible if the Chair approves it.

clause: Designated Persons should consult with the Company's Chief Legal and Risk Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on collared shares should be put to the Chief Legal and Risk Officer up front, because if it is classified as margin lending the approval must come from the Chair rather than the ordinary clearance officer.

topic: margin call sale is a controlled dealing
clause: Such Dealings would cover ... selling Company Securities to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
why_it_matters: A forced sale or enforcement by the financier is treated as the executive's own Dealing needing prior Chair approval, so a collar loan must not permit the bank to sell shares during a Blackout Period without that approval.

clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term Dealing or short selling in Company Securities. In general, the purchase of Company Securities with a view to their resale within a 12 month period, or the sale of Company Securities with a view to their repurchase within a 12 month period, will be considered to be a Dealing of a 'short term' nature.
why_it_matters: A collar tenor of less than 12 months, or one with early unwind or roll features, risks being characterised as short term Dealing, so the structure should be written for at least 12 months.

clause: Any clearance granted: (d) will be valid for a period of 7 calendar days from the date of approval; and (e) may be withdrawn at any time prior to the Dealing occurring. Any Dealing must occur within the period of the approval.
why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar and the secured loan must all complete within 7 calendar days of clearance, and the clearance can be pulled at any point before signing.

clause: Following any Dealing, the Designated Person must notify the Company Secretary within one business day.
why_it_matters: Entry into the collar, and any later unwind, roll or settlement, must be reported to the Company Secretary within one business day, and for Directors it will also feed the Appendix 3Y notifiable interest disclosure.

clause: Securities includes shares, options, rights, debentures, or other securities or derivatives including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, or warrant.
why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so the OTC put and call written with a bank are themselves Company Securities and each leg is a Dealing subject to clearance and Blackout Periods.

clause: Associate means ... an entity (including without limitation trusts, companies and nominees) and/or person that the AUB Connected Person controls or may be expected to control or influence.
why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust, company or nominee does not avoid the policy; the AUB Connected Person must take reasonable steps to ensure the Associate complies.

clause: A Designated Person may be permitted to Deal in Company Securities during a Blackout Period where: (a) exceptional circumstances exist ... The Designated Person must demonstrate that the proposed Dealing is the only reasonable course of action available.
why_it_matters: There is a hardship and legal-obligation escape hatch approved by the Chair, but the 'only reasonable course of action' test means it will rarely support a discretionary collar entry or unwind inside a Blackout Period.

clause: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.1, all GQG Personnel must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike a typical open/closed trading window model, GQG Personnel need prior CCO approval for every dealing at any time of year, so a collar's entry, unwind or roll always needs fresh clearance rather than only during closed periods.

topic: no vesting carve-out for hedging or monetisation
clause: GQG Personnel are prohibited from engaging in hedging, monetization transactions or similar arrangements involving Company securities.
why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to unvested or restricted holdings, so even a collar entirely over long-held, unrestricted vested shares is expressly prohibited, with no clearance route at all.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where, in the judgment of the CCO, the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even the margin-lending leg, which is otherwise approvable, is subject to a discretionary reputational veto that a bank-structured, security-backed facility could well fail regardless of legal compliance.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 4.5(a) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: If a secured loan were ever approved, GQG can impose its own conditions on when the lender may sell on a margin call, constraining a bank's standard enforcement rights over collared shares.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
