why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the short-term dealing, blackout and preclearance rules, but this does not cure the separate, unconditional ban on entering the hedge itself.

clause: GQG Personnel must take appropriate steps to ensure that their "Connected Persons" only deal in securities in circumstances where the GQG Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a family member's account or a related entity does not escape the hedging and derivatives bans.

topic: hedging ban scoped to at-risk remuneration
clause: Personnel must not trade in PNI Securities as part of a hedging arrangement aimed at limiting exposure in relation to part of their "at risk" remuneration.
why_it_matters: Unlike a blanket hedging ban, this only reaches securities forming part of incentive remuneration; a collar over ordinary vested, unrestricted, non-incentive PNI shares is not caught by the hedging prohibition and only needs standard trade pre-clearance, making a funded collar structurally available.

clause: Where there is an existing holding and more PNI Securities are purchased, the holding period is 2 months for all new and existing PNI Securities.
why_it_matters: Any top-up purchase during the life of a collar (e.g. under a DRP variation, though DRP participation is itself blocked in Fixed Prohibited Periods) would restart the 2-month minimum hold across the whole collared position, delaying a permitted unwind.

clause: PNI discourages the use of leveraged margin lending arrangements and other secured financing arrangements by Personnel in relation to PNI Securities but has not prohibited their use.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is permitted in principle, but is subject to prior disclosure to the Company Secretary/Board, prior written approval, and PNI's discretion to impose its own conditions on the facility, including on forced-sale triggers.

clause: Disclosure of a Director's margin lending or secured financing arrangement will be required to be made to the ASX if there is a change in the Director's interest in Securities or if the Board determines that the existence of such arrangement would have a material effect on the price or value of Securities.
why_it_matters: A Director entering a funded collar may need to make a separate ASX disclosure of the financing arrangement itself, beyond the standard Appendix 3Y change-of-interest notice for the derivative legs.

clause: trading wholly initiated by a party independent to the Personnel member (e.g. a margin call related sale of stock initiated by the margin lender)
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default or margin call does not itself require fresh trading approval, giving the lender a clearer path to enforce security over the collared shares.

clause: Notwithstanding any other part of this policy, directors and employees of the Company must not at any time enter into transactions in associated products which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings in the Company.
why_it_matters: This is drafted to override every other provision of the policy, including the exceptional-circumstances relief available elsewhere, so there is no route by which a director or employee could obtain clearance for a collar under any circumstances.

clause: directors and employees of the Company must not at any time enter into transactions in associated products which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings in the Company (clause 10.1); any directors or employees ... (clause 11.1)
why_it_matters: Both the hedging ban and the margin lending/encumbrance disclosure obligation are drafted to apply only to directors and employees, not consultants, though this is not a realistic structuring option for a director or executive engaged in an employment or directorship capacity.

topic: narrow securities definition, broad deal definition
clause: securities includes shares in the Company, options over those shares and any other financial products of the Company traded on ASX; deal in securities includes ... trading in financial products issued or created over securities of the Company ... entering into transactions in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings
why_it_matters: Although "securities" itself is limited to products traded on ASX, the operative dealing and hedging limbs are not venue-limited, so an OTC put and call struck with a bank is still caught by the policy even though it would not itself qualify as a "security" under this policy's own definition.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: If any secured financing arrangement were ever entered into, a lender's enforcement sale would be excluded from the policy's dealing prohibitions and would not need fresh clearance, though this does not cure the separate, absolute ban on entering the hedge itself.

clause: Dated 20 December 2010
why_it_matters: This policy predates common ASX guidance-note updates on hedging and margin lending; NRW Holdings may have adopted a more recent version, which should be checked before relying on this analysis.

topic: absolute margin lending / secured financing ban
clause: You must not have margin lending arrangements in relation to EBOS Securities ... Restricted Persons must not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of EBOS Securities or in relation to which EBOS Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan. This restriction extends to Restricted Persons' Associates.
why_it_matters: This is an unconditional, no-clearance ban on using EBOS Securities as loan security, so the financing leg of a bank-funded collar cannot be implemented under this policy for any tier, vesting state, or associate structure.

topic: hedging ban scoped to unvested/locked entitlements
clause: Rule 8 No hedging on unvested entitlements: Restricted Persons must not enter into hedging arrangements ... to limit their exposure in relation to unvested entitlements or vested entitlements that remain subject to any holding lock or other trading restriction.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban does not reach ordinary vested, unrestricted EBOS shares, so the derivative legs of a collar (put and call) over such shares are not themselves prohibited and can proceed with CEO/Chair consent, unlike the financing leg.

clause: A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if you become aware of Material Information prior to trading and, in that event, you must not trade.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be executed within the 10-day consent validity and can become unexecutable if Material Information arises before completion, requiring a fresh Request for Consent.

clause: Rule 18 Chief Executive Officer trading ... Rule 19 Director trading ... Where the Chair proposes to make any Trade ... the prior written consent of the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee shall be required.
why_it_matters: For a collar involving the CEO, a Director or the Chair, the consent chain escalates to a different, more senior approver, which must be factored into execution timelines and confidentiality of the request.

clause: selling EBOS Securities to satisfy a call under a margin loan except where the holder of EBOS Securities has no control over the sale
why_it_matters: Even if a secured facility existed in breach of Rule 7, a forced sale the holder has no control over is treated as outside the banned activity, but the underlying margin lending or security arrangement is prohibited from inception regardless.

clause: Trading in EBOS Securities by a Director must be advised to NZX and ASX within 5 trading days ... All Trades in EBOS Securities by a Senior Manager must be disclosed to NZX (and will also be disclosed to ASX) within [5 trading days, or 20 working days for specified acquisitions].
why_it_matters: Entry into, and unwind of, the collar's derivative legs by a Director or Senior Manager each trigger separate NZX and ASX disclosure obligations with different timeframes depending on the trade type.

clause: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration is prohibited from entering into transactions (whether through the use of derivatives or otherwise) which limit the economic risk of participating in the equity based incentive remuneration.
why_it_matters: The only absolute prohibition in the Policy; it is drafted around the incentive remuneration itself rather than around a class of securities, so a collar over shares that are traceably incentive awards still at risk is banned outright with no consent route, while a collar over freely held or fully vested shares is not.

clause: so that the incentive remains at risk until achieved
why_it_matters: This purpose statement is the best argument that the clause 6 ban falls away once awards have vested and unrestricted title has transferred, which is the state in which the bank's collar would be written.

clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, charges, pledges, encumbrances or forced sales anywhere in its eight clauses or two Schedules.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is unregulated by this Policy, which is unusually permissive by ASX standards; only the derivative legs need clearance.

clause: To be transacted: On NZX/ASX/off-market trade/other (specify)
why_it_matters: The consent form expressly accommodates an off-market trade, confirming that an OTC collar can be described to and consented by the Company Secretary rather than being incapable of clearance.

clause: The Fletcher Building securities covered by this Policy include shares, capital notes, options and rights ... and any listed derivatives, including futures contracts or warrants listed on an authorised futures exchange, in respect of Fletcher Building securities.
why_it_matters: Paragraph 3.4 arguably confines 'securities' to listed derivatives while the definition of 'trade' in 1.1 has no venue limit; the conservative reading (consent required for an OTC collar) should be applied, and the ambiguity should be resolved with the Company Secretary in writing.

clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification.  A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to trading.
why_it_matters: The 10 trading day window is generous by ASX standards and allows time to price and document a collar, but the consent self-destructs if the executive learns material information before execution, so a bank should require a bring-down confirmation at signing.

clause: Although the approval to trade is at the discretion of the Fletcher Building Company Secretary, Schedule II to this Policy sets out some general guidelines on when approval will not be granted.  In declining any approval to trade, no reasons need be given.
why_it_matters: Consent can be refused without reasons for any reason, so neither the executive nor the bank can rely on a collar being renewable, rollable or unwindable at a future date.

clause: Any significant acquisition or divestment, having regard to the group as a whole: From day that there is a realistic prospect of a transaction arising until after full public disclosure is generally available to the market.
why_it_matters: Undisclosed corporate-activity and capital-raising blackouts can arise at any time and are not calendar-bound, so physical settlement, unwind or roll of the collar may be blocked without warning.

clause: Any such person is included with respect to all of their interests in any of the Company's securities, whether direct, indirect, contingent, beneficial or legal.  The nature of an interest should be interpreted widely.  This will extend to interests held through other entities or persons (eg trusts, associates, related parties, spouses, and closely-held companies, etc) where the person has the ability to influence or control that person or entity.
why_it_matters: A 'contingent' interest is expressly captured, so a collar or loan documented through a family trust or holding company is within the Policy and cannot be used to sidestep the consent requirement.

clause: The Policy contains no minimum holding period, speculative trading ban or intention test.
why_it_matters: There is no tenor constraint on a collar and no risk that a short-dated or early-terminating structure is characterised as prohibited short-term dealing.

clause: Employees are prohibited from entering into margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Spark New Zealand Restricted Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is expressly and unconditionally prohibited for all employees regardless of vesting state or tier, with no clearance or exemption route identified anywhere in the policy.

clause: Any permission to deal can be given or refused by Spark New Zealand in its discretion, without giving reasons. ... Permission to deal can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: Even the unfunded derivative legs of a collar are subject to unreasoned, revocable consent, so a cleared trade cannot be relied upon as final until executed within the 10 trading day validity window.

clause: There are no 'safe' periods for dealing in Spark New Zealand Restricted Securities. You may never deal in Spark New Zealand Restricted Securities if you have Inside Information.
why_it_matters: Collar entry, unwind, roll or settlement must always be individually checked against Inside Information status; there is no blanket open window that removes that check.

clause: A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be priced and executed within the 10 trading day validity and becomes unexecutable if Inside Information arises before signing.

clause: All dealing involving: 1. Spark New Zealand Directors; or 2. Greater than 100,000 shares/options, must be approved by the Chairman of the Spark New Zealand Board.
why_it_matters: A collar of institutional size (or entered by a director) escalates approval to the Chairman rather than the Company Secretary alone, adding a decision-maker to the bank's execution timetable.

clause: You cannot avoid the insider trading laws by dealing in Spark New Zealand Restricted Securities through companies or trusts you control.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the consent regime or the secured financing ban.

topic: third-party derivative ban has no exemption route
clause: Key Management Personnel and their Associates are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of NHF Securities, including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over NHF Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.
why_it_matters: This is an absolute, unconditional ban on buying options (including puts) or other derivatives from a bank counterparty over NHF shares; unlike the Part 3 closed-period regime it carries no exceptional-circumstances or Board-approval carve-out, so the option legs of a funded collar cannot be cleared under any provision of this policy.

clause: Examples of prohibited arrangements: a put option on incentive remuneration
why_it_matters: The policy names a put option specifically as an example of a prohibited hedging arrangement, directly capturing the purchased-put leg of a collar.

topic: secured financing permitted with Board approval
clause: Key Management Personnel and their Associates are permitted to enter into or maintain other secured financial arrangements over NHF Securities subject to Board approval being obtained.
why_it_matters: Unlike margin loans, a loan secured on the collared shares (not itself a margin loan) could in principle proceed with Board approval, but this is moot while the option legs remain absolutely prohibited by paragraph 4.1.

clause: (lender disposal) a disposal of NHF Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights;
why_it_matters: If a secured facility were ever put in place, the lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the closed-period/notification regime (though still subject to the insider trading ban), so enforcement is not itself a breach.

clause: Notification of any dealing in NHF Securities under this paragraph and the completion of Part B of the Notification Form to Deal in NHF Securities does not constitute approval of the dealing by or on behalf of the nib Group.
why_it_matters: Outside closed periods the KMP self-certifies via notification rather than obtaining company approval, so nib bears no responsibility for clearing the collar's timing even when the process is followed.

clause: Any such approval must be obtained in advance, cannot be given after the event and will be final and binding on the applicant. No reasons are required to be given for any decision regarding whether or not to provide an approval.
why_it_matters: Even if the derivative ban were waived, closed-period execution of the collar would require discretionary, unreasoned and unappealable approval obtained strictly in advance.

clause: The policy contains no provision addressing margin lending, other secured financing arrangements, or encumbrance of L1G Securities.
why_it_matters: The absence of any margin lending, secured financing or encumbrance restriction means a loan secured on the collared shares is not itself restricted by this policy, though the hedging ban still blocks the option overlay.

topic: hedging ban not limited to unvested securities
clause: in derivative instruments or other products associated with L1G Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their holding in L1G Securities
why_it_matters: The hedging ban applies to a Covered Person's holding generally, not just unvested or performance-conditioned securities, so a collar over fully vested, unrestricted shares is caught just as much as one over unvested rights.

topic: no closed-period relief for hedging or short selling
clause: A Covered Person wishing to: Trade in L1G Securities ... during a Closed Trading Period; or engage in short-term Trading in L1G Securities, may apply in writing to the Company Secretary for an exemption if special circumstances exist
why_it_matters: The Company Secretary's exemption mechanism is limited to Closed Trading Period and short-term trading breaches; it does not extend to the section C(d) hedging or short-selling prohibitions, so there is no route to clear a collar even in special circumstances.

clause: Platinum Covered Persons must obtain pre-authorisation ... Directors ... must obtain pre-authorisation ... by submitting a request to c&l@platinum.com.au ... All other Covered Persons ... must obtain pre-authorisation ... from the L1 Capital Head of Legal and Compliance
why_it_matters: Execution timing for any cleared dealing depends on which L1 Group entity a director or executive is affiliated with, and approvals are valid for only one Business Day regardless of route.

topic: broad reach to controlled and beneficial interests
clause: any account over which a Covered Person has an economic interest
why_it_matters: A collar or loan written through a family trust, SMSF or other controlled vehicle is still caught, because the policy reaches any account in which a Covered Person or immediate family member has an economic or beneficial interest, or direct or indirect control.

clause: Securities means all Metcash shares, options, notes, performance rights, debentures and other securities on issue or granted from time to time
why_it_matters: Because 'Securities' is limited to instruments Metcash itself issues or grants, a bank-written OTC put or call is not 'Securities' under this policy; over vested, unrestricted shares such a derivative falls outside the Closed Period, approval and short-term dealing rules entirely, since section 6.1's hedging/derivative ban is the only provision reaching derivatives and it is expressly confined to unvested or holding-locked incentive securities.

topic: hedging ban limited to incentive-plan securities
clause: Team Members must not enter into a hedging or other derivative transaction in connection with Securities: (a) acquired under any executive or employee incentive plan prior to vesting; or (b) whilst they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of any executive or employee incentive plan.
why_it_matters: The ban does not reach ordinary on-market vested shares, or plan shares once vesting and any holding lock have ended, so a collar over such shares is not prohibited by this clause.

topic: margin loan disclosure limited to acquisition financing, Directors/GLT only
clause: Directors and members of the GLT who finance acquisitions of Securities by margin call loans must advise the Company Secretary of these arrangements
why_it_matters: The disclosure/register obligation is worded around financing new acquisitions and applies only to Directors and GLT, not Specified Management or other Team Members; it is unclear whether a loan secured on already-held vested shares (rather than financing a purchase) triggers the same obligation, so the bank should seek voluntary disclosure or Board sign-off for certainty.

clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: If the bank ever enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that sale is excluded from the short-term dealing, Closed Period and outside-period rules, though it remains subject to the insider trading law generally.

clause: The Approver may request more information from the applicant, grant the request, refuse the request or impose conditions on the dealing. ... If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: Even where a dealing does require approval (e.g. a collar entered while shares remain locked, or during a prohibited period), the Approver can impose bespoke conditions on the collar's terms and can revoke a granted approval at any time without reason.

clause: Any other time as determined by the Board of Zip in its sole discretion. ... The Board or Company Secretary may not necessarily be in a position to explain why or for how long the prohibition will be in place.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed Board-imposed blackout can block collar entry, unwind or roll at any time with no explanation given to the executive or the bank.

topic: unvested hedging ban vs. holding-lock approval route
clause: 7.1 prohibits hedging 'unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme' outright, while 8.1 allows hedging of holdings 'unvested or subject to a holding lock or other escrow' with prior approval.
why_it_matters: A collar cannot be written over unvested scheme entitlements at all; it should be confined to shares that have already vested (whether still holding-locked or fully unrestricted), where 8.1's approval route applies.

topic: secured financing is approvable, not banned
clause: Zip Personnel must not enter into agreements with lenders with rights over their interests in Zip securities ... without first seeking and obtaining prior written approval from the Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: Unlike an outright ban, the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the shares is structurally available subject to case-by-case, unreviewable and confidential Approving Officer sign-off.

clause: The Approving Officer has absolute discretion in considering an application ... is not obliged to provide reasons ... and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: Both legs of the collar (hedge and loan) can be refused or revoked without reasons and without notice, so the bank should not assume durability of an initial approval.

clause: I understand that approval, if granted, will be valid for 7 business days, on the condition that I do not come into possession of price sensitive information before the transaction occurs.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar and loan must occur within 7 business days of clearance or fresh approval must be sought.

clause: Zip Personnel ... (c) immediate family members of all Directors ... Officers ... the Group Executive Team and other senior executives ... and (d) companies, trusts and entities over which such Directors, Officers, Group Executive Team members or their immediate family members have control, or otherwise are closely connected to.
why_it_matters: A family trust or holding vehicle used to warehouse the collared shares or take the loan is itself Zip Personnel and fully subject to the Policy; it is not a way to route around the approval requirements.

clause: As a guiding principle, Zip Personnel are discouraged from actively trading in Zip securities.
why_it_matters: While not a binding rule, this soft discouragement may inform the Approving Officer's discretion when asked to approve a collar with frequent rolls or adjustments.

clause: The Policy contains no provision restricting hedging, or transactions that limit the economic risk of a security holding.
why_it_matters: A collar's derivative legs are not caught by any hedging-specific prohibition; they are governed only by the general prior-written-approval process for 'trading' and, for the loan leg, the encumbrance approval process.

topic: encumbrance approvable even in a Closed Period
clause: Company Personnel who are not in possession of Inside Information may also apply for and be given written approval to encumber Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar can be secured on the shares even inside a Closed Period, subject to a case-by-case approval, which is unusually permissive compared with policies that ban secured financing outright.

topic: lender enforcement excluded from Closed Period ban
clause: A disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is Excluded Trading, completed] without seeking prior approval.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default or margin call is not itself a Policy breach and needs no fresh clearance, even during a Closed Period, reducing the bank's execution risk on default.

clause: Any prior written approval to trade in Securities ... is automatically deemed: (a) to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of any Inside Information ... (b) suspended upon the start of any Closed Period ... (c) to lapse upon expiration of any time limit for which the approval to trade applies.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade must be executed within its stated time limit and before any Closed Period or inside information arises, or fresh approval is required.

topic: Canadian SEDI reporting of related financial instruments
clause: a Reporting Insider is required to disclose any change in any interest in, or right or obligation associated with, a related financial instrument. Reporting Insiders must file an insider report electronically through ... 'SEDI', usually within five days after the trade occurs.
why_it_matters: As a Canadian-incorporated, dual-listed issuer, a collar entered by a Reporting Insider is likely a 'related financial instrument' requiring its own SEDI filing within about 5 days, additional to and separate from the ASX-side approval and reporting process.

clause: The Policy contains no reference to unvested entitlements, holding locks or equity incentive scheme vesting.
why_it_matters: There is no distinct restriction (or exemption) tailored to unvested shares; the collar analysis turns entirely on the general trading-approval and encumbrance-approval provisions regardless of how the shares were acquired.

clause: Company Securities... includes any shares in the Company, debentures (including convertible notes) issued by the Company, units of shares in the Company and options to acquire or subscribe for shares in the Company... to 'deal' in Company Securities includes subscribing for, purchasing or selling Company Securities or entering into an agreement to do any of those things.
why_it_matters: A third-party OTC put/call collar is arguably neither a 'Company Security' nor itself a 'deal', so its creation may fall outside this Policy's clearance and Blackout Period regime entirely, though this interpretation carries risk and should be confirmed with the Company Secretary before relying on it.

topic: Director ASX disclosure of option-like contracts
clause: a director of the Company must notify ASX within 5 business days after any change in ... interests in contracts to which the director is a party or under which the director is entitled to a benefit, and that confer a right to call for or deliver shares in or debentures of the Company
why_it_matters: Even if the internal clearance process does not reach the collar, a Director must still notify ASX (Appendix-3Y-style) within 5 business days of entering it, and must tell the Company Secretary promptly so that filing can be made.

topic: margin lending expressly excluded from broker-credit ban
clause: not utilise broker credit ... Such prohibition does not extend to normal documented margin lending or loan facilities offered to the general public by brokers, banks or other lending institutions.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not banned outright, though the 'offered to the general public' qualifier creates doubt as to whether a bespoke bilateral facility for one executive squarely fits the carve-out.

clause: the purchase of Company Securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of Company Securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature
why_it_matters: If the collar's settlement disposes of shares within 12 months of their acquisition and any repurchase intention is present, it risks being characterised as prohibited short-term trading; a straightforward one-way exit is less likely to be caught.

clause: A "Blackout Period" operates in respect of ... the close of business on 31 December and 30 June ... and ... the last Trading Day of each month up to the ... Monthly Net Tangible Asset per Share announcement.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies granting the Board a general discretion to declare extra confidential blackouts, MFF's Blackout Periods are limited to fixed, predictable reporting dates, making collar timing more certain.

clause: Under this Policy, hedging of the Company's securities is not permitted.
why_it_matters: A put-and-call collar is a textbook hedge of holding risk; it is banned outright for every tier with no exceptional-circumstances or Board-discretion route anywhere in the Policy, unlike blackout dealing and short-term dealing which do have hardship/court-order routes.

topic: absolute margin lending ban, broadly worded
clause: Employees, directors, and Connected Persons must not engage in any dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement. ... entering into a margin lending arrangement ... transferring securities ... into an existing margin loan account ... selling securities ... to satisfy a call.
why_it_matters: The funded loan leg, if it functions as a share-secured facility with margin-call-style triggers, is likely to be treated the same as a margin loan and banned outright with no approval route at any stage of the arrangement.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Labelling the loan something other than a 'margin loan' is unlikely to escape the 6.2 prohibition if it is secured against, and enforceable by reference to the value of, the shares.

topic: lender enforcement carve-out does not legitimise the loan
clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.4 and 6.1].
why_it_matters: Even though a genuine secured lender's own enforcement sale is excused from blackout/window/approval rules, this exclusion is about the disposal only - it does not cure the underlying prohibition on the executive entering into the arrangement in the first place.

clause: Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.4 and 6.1 of this Policy do not apply to ... participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.
why_it_matters: The equity-plan exclusion only lifts the blackout/window/approval and short-term dealing rules for plan participation itself - it does not touch the hedging ban (6.3) or the margin lending ban (6.2), both of which apply with full force to vested plan shares once collar structuring is contemplated.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested at-risk remuneration
clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into hedging arrangements to limit their exposure in relation to "at-risk" remuneration (meaning any unvested shares, options or rights issued or acquired under any future Chorus employee incentive schemes where performance hurdles have not yet been achieved or other conditions have not yet been met).
why_it_matters: A collar over already-vested, unrestricted shares is not caught by the only hedging-specific prohibition in the Policy; it is treated as an ordinary dealing requiring consent (for Restricted Persons) or nothing beyond the Inside Information rule (for other Chorus Personnel).

clause: "Chorus Restricted Securities" means any Chorus shares, options, derivatives and debt securities. ... any options, derivatives or other financial products issued or created over or in respect of any securities of Chorus.
why_it_matters: There is no interpretive gap: entering an OTC put/call collar is unambiguously a dealing in a Chorus Restricted Security, so the consent process (for Restricted Persons) applies directly rather than by analogy.

clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, or encumbering securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is neither banned nor expressly permitted; the Bank should confirm with the General Counsel and Company Secretary whether pledging or transferring the shares to a collateral agent needs consent as an 'otherwise deal[ing]' in Chorus shares, by analogy with the express 'transferring shares to a trust' example.

topic: double approval for Directors and large trades
clause: all dealings involving (i) Chorus Directors or (ii) greater than 100,000 shares/options must be approved by the Chairman of the Board.
why_it_matters: A Director's collar, or any Restricted Person's collar exceeding 100,000 shares/options, needs both General Counsel and Company Secretary consent and separate Chairman approval.

clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification ... A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the Restricted Person becomes aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar must occur within 10 trading days of consent, and any inside information arising before execution voids the consent.

clause: This policy applies whether the dealing is to be done in New Zealand or overseas and whether or not the dealing relates to Chorus' New Zealand or foreign securities
why_it_matters: An offshore-booked OTC collar with an international bank is still squarely within scope of the Policy and its consent/black-out requirements.

clause: The Company does not have employees and most activities are outsourced, including investment management.
why_it_matters: There is no unvested/vested distinction to navigate; any collar would be over ordinary shares held outright by a director or officer, so the analysis turns entirely on the hedging ban and margin loan consent regime rather than plan-security carve-outs.

clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).
why_it_matters: Unlike the margin loan regime, there is no consent or clearance mechanism for hedging at all; a collar's put and call legs are squarely 'transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk' of the shareholding and are banned outright with no route to permission.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this Clause 5.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: Even though the loan leg of a collar (a secured financing/margin-type arrangement) is not banned outright, the Company's consent is required up front and can be conditioned on when and how the lender may force a sale, which a bank counterparty would need to accommodate contractually.

topic: no closed-period carve-out for margin calls
clause: The Restricted Persons are to be subject to restrictions on trading in the Company's shares at certain times of the year.
why_it_matters: The policy does not state that a lender's forced sale to meet a margin call is excluded from the blackout periods, so enforcement of the loan or unwind of the collar during a closed period is not clearly protected and would likely need Board agreement or advance structuring around windows.

clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time.
why_it_matters: An unscheduled, discretionary trading embargo (confidentiality not addressed) can override any planned collar entry, unwind or hedge adjustment at short notice.

topic: PDMR absolute derivatives and secured-financing ban
clause: PDMRs are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities (including, but not limited to, hedge arrangements). ... PDMRs are prohibited at all times from entering into margin lending or similar arrangements in respect to Company Securities they hold or in which they have a Relevant Interest.
why_it_matters: Both legs of a funded collar with a bank (the OTC put/call and the secured loan) are banned outright for any PDMR at all times, with no clearance mechanism, no vesting distinction and no listed exception route in Schedule 1 or 2 (those only cover ordinary share sales in Exceptional Circumstances).

clause: For the avoidance of doubt this prohibition in relation to financial products does not apply to an option over unissued capital granted by the Company.
why_it_matters: Confirms the ban targets third-party/market derivatives like a bank collar, not the Company's own incentive option grants; it gives no comfort for a bank-written structure.

clause: Sections 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 14 also apply to PCAs of PDMRs ... Section 5 (the absolute hedging/margin-lending ban) is not among the sections listed as extending to PCAs.
why_it_matters: On a literal reading, a PDMR's family trust or spouse (a PCA) is not directly bound by the absolute section 5 ban, only by the general clearance/notification regime; however the PDMR's own overriding duty to 'ensure that their PCAs do not breach this Policy' makes routing a collar through a PCA a live legal risk rather than a clean workaround.

clause: Deal ... includes: ... using Company Securities as security for a loan or other obligation.
why_it_matters: For senior employees who are not PDMRs, both the derivative legs and the secured loan of a collar are only 'Dealings' requiring ordinary prior clearance and post-trade notification, not an absolute ban, making a funded collar structurally possible for that population subject to Closed Periods and Approving Officer discretion.

clause: from 1 January of each year until publication of the Company's annual financial report ... from 1 July of each year until publication of the Company's half-year financial report ... from first day of each Quarter until the publication of the Company's quarterly report
why_it_matters: Because RSG reports quarterly, half-yearly and annually, and each Closed Period runs from the start of the period to publication (with a 30-day minimum for annual/half-year), open trading windows for entering or unwinding a collar are narrow and must be checked quarter by quarter.

clause: The status of Trading Plans and Investment Programmes under the UK Market Abuse Regulation and, more particularly the ability of a member of Personnel to carry out transactions under a Trading Plan or an Investment Programme during Closed Periods, remains uncertain.
why_it_matters: Even for non-PDMR Personnel, the Company treats derivative or plan-based structures executing during a Closed Period as legally uncertain under UK MAR and takes a conservative approach, so a bank should expect execution to be confined to open windows.

clause: Mesoblast Personnel must not trade in the Company's derivatives.
why_it_matters: This one-line, undefined and unconditional prohibition applies to every director, officer, employee, contractor and consultant (and their Connected Persons) at all times, with no clearance mechanism and no vesting distinction, and on a natural reading blocks the purchased put and written call legs of a bank collar outright.

clause: No provision of the policy refers to margin lending, security, charges, pledges or any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Company securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar (secured on the collared shares) is not expressly prohibited or regulated by this policy at all, so absent the derivatives ban it would not itself be a policy obstacle; however, since the derivative legs are banned, the financing leg cannot be isolated into a compliant transaction.

topic: trust/company structuring does not avoid insider trading
clause: the definition of "procure" can include a director or employee who acquires Company securities through a trust or company while in possession of "inside information" may contravene these insider trading provisions and this Policy.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a personal trust or holding company does not avoid personal liability if the individual is in possession of inside information at the time, and Connected Persons (including such trusts and controlled companies) are independently bound by the clause 3 rules including the derivatives ban.

clause: This policy was adopted by the Mesoblast Board of Directors on 28 August 2013.
why_it_matters: The document provided is dated 2013 with no amendment history or next-review date recorded; a bank should confirm this remains Mesoblast's current, in-force Share Trading Policy before relying on its terms.

clause: OBM Persons must not ... enter into any type of "protection arrangements" ... (a) in respect of any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock – at any time; and (b) otherwise – without approval under section 5.1.
why_it_matters: The prohibition on hedging/protection arrangements (and the parallel prohibition on granting security/margin lending in 3.6) is tied to vesting status, not to tier: it is an absolute, clearance-free bar while shares are unvested or subject to a holding lock, but becomes merely approval-gated once the shares vest and any holding lock lifts. A funded collar is therefore only conceivable over shares that have fully vested and are no longer holding-locked.

clause: A disposal of OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement, subject to the grant of security having been granted with approval under section 5.1 [is not regulated by this Policy and may be undertaken ... at any time].
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, OBM expressly exempts a bank's enforcement sale on default from the Policy altogether, including during a Blackout Period, so long as the original grant of security over the shares was itself approved. This directly de-risks the lender's ability to enforce the collar loan's security without the borrower being put in breach.

clause: grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities ... to secure any obligation of that person or any third party.
why_it_matters: The security-granting prohibition/approval regime is not limited to bank margin loans; it expressly covers any charge, mortgage or pledge securing any obligation (even a third party's), so the collar loan's security interest is squarely within scope and needs 5.1 approval once shares are vested and unrestricted.

clause: Any written approval granted under this Policy will be valid for the period of 5 trading days ... Written approval ... may be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer in writing, in person or by email at any time during the approval period.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar (derivative legs and/or security grant) must be executed within 5 trading days, and the Authorising Officer can revoke the approval at any point before execution, so timing and re-clearance risk should be built into the transaction schedule.

clause: In exceptional circumstances an Authorising Officer has discretion to approve under section 5.1: (a) Dealings in OBM Shares during a Blackout Period; or (b) other Dealings, that would otherwise be prohibited by this Policy but are not prohibited by law.
why_it_matters: It is unclear whether this hardship/court-order override (framed around 'Dealings') can reach the separately-worded absolute bans on protection arrangements and security-granting over unvested/holding-locked shares, since those bans are not expressed as prohibitions on 'Dealing'; the bank should not assume this route can unlock a collar before full vesting.

clause: Directors and employees must not at any time enter into a transaction (e.g. a derivative) that operates or is intended to operate to limit the economic risk of holdings of unvested Company securities or vested Company securities which are subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar are absolutely banned, with no clearance route, only while the underlying shares are unvested or holding-locked. Once vested and unrestricted, the same transaction is merely an ordinary 'dealing' in a security (since the Securities definition expressly includes derivatives and CFDs) requiring prior written clearance for Directors and Restricted Employees.

clause: Key Management Personnel (KMP) must not at any time enter into a transaction that involves using Company securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including margin lending arrangements.
why_it_matters: For a KMP, the secured loan leg of a funded collar is banned permanently and unconditionally, regardless of vesting status, with no clearance route and no exclusion under Section 4 (which only carves out Sections 2.3, 2.5 and 3.1, not 3.2). This blocks a funded collar for KMP even over long-vested, unrestricted shares.

clause: Section 3.2(b) applies only to Key Management Personnel; no equivalent express provision restricts non-KMP Directors or employees from granting security over their Company securities.
why_it_matters: For a Director or employee who is not KMP, the secured loan leg of a collar is not expressly prohibited by this Policy, and pledging shares (without a change of beneficial ownership) may fall outside the 'deal' definition altogether, making a funded collar structurally more feasible for that population, subject to legal confirmation.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the operation of Sections 2.3, 2.5 and 3.1].
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the Closed Period ban, the clearance requirement and the 12-month short-term trading rule, which materially de-risks the bank's ability to enforce security over a non-KMP borrower's shares.

clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Closed Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed, Board-imposed blackout can arise at any time and cannot be revealed even to a transacting counterparty, adding execution-timing risk to entering, adjusting or unwinding a collar.

clause: Directors or Restricted Employees given clearance to trade must trade no more than two (2) business days from clearance being received, otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.
why_it_matters: Collar execution must occur within 2 business days of clearance, and the approver may revoke clearance at any time beforehand without giving reasons, so timing needs to be tightly coordinated with the bank counterparty.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights [is an Excluded Dealing not subject to sections 3.3, 4.1 and 4.2]
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from both the short-term dealing ban and the Trading Window/blackout restriction, so it is not blocked by a closed window.

clause: Designated Persons must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities or transfer securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.
why_it_matters: The ban is confined to margin lending and margin loan accounts; a bespoke pledge-secured loan not structured or documented as a margin loan is not expressly captured, though the Policy's substance-over-form approach could still be invoked against it.

clause: Short‐term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: A collar (paired forward-like derivative positions) risks being characterised as a prohibited 'other short term dealing' irrespective of the 3-month on-market test, so structuring and tenor should be cleared with the Company Secretary in advance.

clause: The Approval Officer is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar could be revoked without reasons before execution, so the bank cannot treat clearance as final until both legs are signed within the validity window.

clause: the approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of both collar legs must complete within 5 business days of approval or a fresh clearance application is required.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: A publicised leveraged hedge around an executive's shareholding could be refused on reputational grounds even where otherwise compliant.

clause: Designated Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Parties only deal in securities in circumstances where the Designated Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the Trading Window, margin-lending or hedging restrictions.

clause: Key Management Personnel or Other Employees must notify the Company Secretary if they enter into a margin lending facility or other secured financing arrangement affecting their MND Securities ... The Company will determine whether the arrangement requires disclosure to the market.
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, MND does not prohibit margin lending or other secured financing over its securities; a bank loan secured on the collared shares only triggers a notification duty, with the Company deciding whether market disclosure is needed.

clause: a disposal of Securities of MND that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example (where permitted), under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: An enforcement sale by the bank as secured lender falls outside the Policy entirely, so it is not blocked by a closed period or the need for Chairman approval.

clause: shares or other securities issued by MND or by third parties over MND’s securities (such as derivatives) (collectively, "Securities")
why_it_matters: OTC put/call derivatives referencing MND shares are expressly 'Securities', so the collar legs are subject to the same trading-window and notification regime as ordinary share dealings, rather than falling outside the Policy altogether.

clause: The notification must state that the proposed Dealing is not as a result of access to, or being in possession of Unpublished, Price-Sensitive Information.
why_it_matters: Within an open trading window there is no discretionary approval gate to negotiate -- only a pre-trade no-inside-information declaration -- so collar execution timing is largely within the executive's control once a window is open.

topic: hedging ban limited to Corporations Act scope
clause: Key Management Personnel and their closely related parties are prohibited from entering into hedging arrangements with respect of any part of their remuneration that has not vested, or that has vested but is subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: Once incentive securities vest and any holding lock lifts, hedging is no longer expressly banned, opening the door to a funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares.

clause: The Chairman reserves the right to approve or refuse a request without providing reasons and can withdraw approval if new information comes to light or there is a change of circumstances. Any decision of the Chairman is final.
why_it_matters: Collar entry during a closed period cannot be relied upon until executed; the Chairman can withdraw a granted approval before the 5-working-day completion deadline expires.

topic: Associated Product ban scoped to unvested entitlement
clause: Where Genesis Energy Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'. An Associated Product is any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Genesis Energy Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.
why_it_matters: This anti-hedging rule is framed around the unvested incentive entitlement, not shares already vested and held outright; on its literal wording a collar over vested, unrestricted shares is not caught, though this reading should be confirmed with the General Counsel and Company Secretary.

clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, charges, pledges or a secured lender's enforcement rights.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is neither prohibited nor subject to any notification or disclosure duty under this Policy, unlike most ASX peer policies; that silence, and any separate NZ financial markets law overlay, should be checked before relying on it.

topic: pre-approval required for every trade by Restricted Persons
clause: Restricted Persons must seek pre-approval for any Trading in Securities.
why_it_matters: Every leg of a collar (entry, roll, unwind) by a director or senior manager needs prior written consent valid for only 10 trading days (2 trading days if granted during a Blackout Period), and lapses automatically if Material Information arises before execution.

clause: You cannot avoid "Key Rule 1" by Trading in Securities through companies or trusts you control. If the companies or trusts that you control, Trade in Securities while you have Material Information, you will be deemed to have traded in the Securities.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or a related hedge through a controlled trust or company does not avoid the insider trading prohibition or the Restricted Person pre-approval requirement.

clause: Securities means Ordinary shares of Genesis Energy which are quoted on the NZX Main Board and Australian Stock Exchange, Genesis Energy capital bonds quoted on the NZDX market, and NZ electricity futures contracts that are traded on ASX.
why_it_matters: Both NZX and ASX disclosure regimes (and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013) can be triggered by a collar over Genesis Energy shares, in addition to this Policy's own approval and notification requirements.

clause: (security or margin interests) creating a security interest or other financial interest, or entering into a margin loan, in respect of Securities ... Board approval cannot be granted for proposed Dealings that are prohibited Dealings.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar -- any security interest over the shares, not just a margin loan -- is an absolute, Board-unwaivable prohibition for Designated Persons (the Chair, all directors including the MD/CEO, and their direct reports), so the structure cannot be cleared under any circumstances for this tier.

topic: remuneration hedging ban tied to disposal restriction, not vesting
clause: entering into a hedging or similar arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of a Designated Person to risk relating to an element of the Designated Person's remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal.
why_it_matters: This ban follows the disposal restriction rather than the vesting date -- shares that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock cannot be collared -- and it is also an unwaivable prohibited Dealing.

topic: hedge and security interest expressly named as Dealings
clause: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to the Securities
why_it_matters: Both legs of a collar (the hedge/derivative and the secured loan) are expressly named as Dealings, removing any argument that a bespoke OTC structure falls outside the Policy.

clause: [The excluded dealings in section 9 do not include a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights.]
why_it_matters: Because Designated Persons cannot create a security interest at all, the Policy provides no carve-out for a lender's enforcement sale; secured financing is simply unavailable for this tier rather than merely restricted.

topic: off-market authorisation lapses in 5 business days
clause: is taken to be withdrawn in respect of any off-market Dealing not completed within five business days, or in respect of any on-market Dealing where the relevant trade has not been entered into within ten business days.
why_it_matters: An OTC collar is an off-market Dealing, so any authorisation to enter it (for the non-prohibited, vested-unrestricted hedge leg) lapses after 5 business days and must be re-sought if not executed in time.

clause: Dealings that would not satisfy The Front Page Test should not occur, even where the Dealing may not strictly be prohibited under the Policy or otherwise at law.
why_it_matters: Even the permitted hedge-only leg for a Designated Person could be discouraged or refused on reputational grounds beyond the strict legal analysis.

clause: Employees and Designated Officers are not permitted to enter into transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements) in Company Securities (or any derivative thereof) which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company or any vested or unvested entitlements to securities in the Company under any equity based remuneration schemes offered by the Company (or any member of the Group).
why_it_matters: This single clause bans both legs of a funded collar outright -- the hedge (put and call) and any margin loan or other risk-limiting financing -- for all Employees and Designated Officers, across vested and unvested holdings, with no clearance or exemption route referenced anywhere in the Policy.

clause: transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements)
why_it_matters: The 'not limited to' wording means a bespoke secured loan or novel collar structure cannot be argued to fall outside the ban merely because it is not called a margin loan or hedge by name.

clause: which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company or any vested or unvested entitlements to securities in the Company under any equity based remuneration schemes offered by the Company
why_it_matters: The prohibition is not confined to incentive-plan securities -- it extends to 'any security in the Company', so open-market purchased shares held by a director or executive are equally covered.

clause: I acknowledge that this approval to trade is value for only fourteen (14) days from the date indicated below, unless otherwise revoked earlier by notice in writing.
why_it_matters: Even for the narrow set of dealings not caught by clause 14 (e.g. an outright sale of vested shares outside a window), a Designated Officer's clearance to trade lapses after 14 days.

clause: [The Policy does not state that a refusal of clearance must be kept confidential, nor that the Approving Officer may impose conditions on a clearance.]
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, there is no express confidentiality protection around a refused clearance request and no explicit power to attach conditions; clearance here is effectively binary.

clause: GYG Persons and other GYG employees may at any time: ... a disposal of GYG securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a lender's enforcement sale as a breach, GYG expressly permits it 'at any time', including in a Blackout Period, so the bank could enforce against the collared shares on default without putting the executive in breach (subject to post-event notification to the Authorising Officer).

clause: Section 6 states it 'applies to Directors and Senior Management only', yet its Authorising Officer table (6.1(c)) includes a row for 'Any other GYG Person or other GYG employee', and sections 9.2(b)/9.3(b) (which apply to all GYG Persons and employees) cross-refer to 'consent under paragraph 6.1'.
why_it_matters: For a non-Director/Senior-Management participant the availability of a clearance route for the collar's derivative and security legs is not free of doubt; the conservative reading (and the one supported by the 6.1(c) table) is that Company Secretary/General Counsel consent is still required.

clause: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which ... operate to limit the economic risk of any GYG Person's security holding ... or otherwise enable a GYG Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities
why_it_matters: The definition is not limited by venue or instrument type, so an OTC put and written call over vested shares squarely falls within 'protection arrangements' and needs consent even though derivatives, hedging and monetisation are not separately named.

clause: not addressed
why_it_matters: There is no floor on retained holdings, so a collar sized against the full vested position would not itself breach a shareholding guideline.

clause: Directors and senior executives must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 3.3 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar always needs prior written approval for this tier, never just the lighter open-window notification, and the secured-lender forced-sale exclusion is itself expressed as 'subject to paragraph 3.4', so enforcement sales are not an automatic safe harbour from approval.

clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg in its annual report or to ASX).
why_it_matters: The bank and executive should expect the collar to potentially be publicly disclosed by the Company.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with paragraph 3.4(b) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The Company can constrain the loan's margin-call/enforcement mechanics as a condition of approval, which the bank's standard facility terms would need to accommodate.

clause: Connected Person means, in relation to an Employee ... a company or any other entity which the Employee has an ability to control.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a controlled company or trust does not escape the policy's hedging and margin lending rules.

clause: A useful question to ask yourself is: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could my proposed transaction be perceived by the market as me ... taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way?
why_it_matters: Approvers may weigh reputational perception, not just legal compliance, when assessing a novel OTC collar and loan structure.

clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)
why_it_matters: The policy's own Derivatives definition expressly lists 'collars', so a bank equity collar is unambiguously within the section 6.2 regime: banned unvested or holding-locked, permitted with Chairperson/Board approval once vested and unrestricted.

topic: margin lending approval scope and recent amendment
clause: This update introduces a formal approval process for any margin lending arrangements involving Company Securities by Key Management Personnel (KMP) ... These changes provide flexibility that will enable the Founders to hold their Tasmea shares given their confidence in the unique business model ... and potentially deal with the consequences of the proposed taxation changes to Superannuation Laws.
why_it_matters: The August 2025 amendment was adopted specifically to let KMP/Founders borrow against their shares, evidencing Board willingness to approve secured financing (the loan leg of a funded collar) for KMP, subject to the tiered approval procedure.

clause: Where approval is given for entry into a margin lending arrangement, the Company may, where appropriate or required by law, disclose to the ASX the fact and nature of the margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The bank and executive should expect the secured loan (and by extension a funded collar) to potentially be publicly disclosed.

clause: Derivatives may, subject to the approval of the Chairperson ... be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions.
why_it_matters: Unlike sections 3-5, section 6.2 is not expressly limited to Designated Persons, while non-Designated employees/consultants/contractors are otherwise free to deal absent Inside Information (3.3); conservatively, Chairperson approval for the derivative leg should be sought regardless of tier.

clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period are subject to the following restrictions once the Black-out Period commences: the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: Relevant to timing the unwind, roll or physical settlement of a collar leg that straddles the start of a Black-out Period.

clause: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise
why_it_matters: A bank-written or purchased OTC put/call over Alkane shares is squarely within the policy's definition of Company Securities, so the hedging clearance requirement (section 10) applies directly rather than by analogy.

clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
why_it_matters: A collar can only be entered once the relevant equity has vested; there is no clearance route for unvested entitlements.

clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in section 5.
why_it_matters: Relevant if collar or loan proceeds are intended to fund the exercise price of options via a cashless exercise during a Prohibited Period.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights ... is excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 5. Please note section 11 ... Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements ... without first obtaining prior written clearance.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is not blocked by a Blackout Period, but only because the underlying secured loan was itself cleared in advance under section 11; an uncleared facility would not benefit from this carve-out.

clause: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: Timing certainty for collar execution, roll or close-out for Restricted Persons can be disrupted by an undisclosed Additional Period.

clause: The Company Secretary must report all notifications of trading in, and clearances given, in relation to trading in Company Securities to the next Board meeting of the Company.
why_it_matters: The Board will be made aware of any collar or secured-lending clearance granted to a Restricted Person.

clause: Restricted Persons must obtain the Board's approval to enter into a margin lending, hedging, derivative or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to the Company's securities (Funding Arrangements). Restricted Persons must provide the Board with the material terms of any proposed Funding Arrangements, including the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and any trigger events.
why_it_matters: A funded OTC collar (put, call and secured loan) is squarely a 'Funding Arrangement' requiring Board-level approval, not just the standard Clearance Officer sign-off, and the Board must be told upfront about the lender's unilateral sale rights and trigger events.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into Funding Arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk in relation to all or part of their remuneration that has not vested, or has vested but remains subject to a restriction arrangement (including by holding lock).
why_it_matters: The collar and its financing can only reference shares that are fully vested and free of any holding lock or other restriction arrangement.

clause: where a Funding Arrangement of a Restricted Person involves 5% or more of the Company's securities, the Board and Company Secretary shall make appropriate disclosure to the market of any key terms of the Funding Arrangements.
why_it_matters: A sufficiently large collar/loan over a Restricted Person's holding may trigger mandatory public disclosure of its key terms.

topic: lender enforcement carve-out conditional on prior approval
clause: (lender disposal) where the Dealing arises through the disposal of the Company's securities by a lender exercising their rights under an approved Funding Arrangement
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is only excluded from the Blackout Period restriction if the Funding Arrangement was properly Board-approved beforehand; an unapproved arrangement would not benefit from this carve-out.

topic: short-term sale clearance extends to all tiers
clause: Any proposed sale of the Company's securities less than 120 days after their acquisition must receive prior Clearance to Deal in accordance with the procedure set out in section 2.5.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or settling the collar by selling shares within 120 days of their vesting/acquisition requires Clearance to Deal even for personnel who are not otherwise Restricted Persons.

clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company’s securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult the Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Because only 'margin lending arrangements' are banned, a bank loan secured on vested shares that does not itself compel a forced sale during a closed period appears permitted in principle, though it must be cleared with the Company Secretary as not being a margin loan in substance.

clause: Deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company’s securities, except for a type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy.
why_it_matters: This is a standalone, unconditional prohibition, not a clearance gate, on entering OTC derivatives such as a purchased put or written call; none of the section 7 permitted-dealing carve-outs covers a bank collar, so the derivative legs cannot proceed under any clearance route.

clause: a disposal of Company’s securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under any margin lending agreements, where such agreements are prohibited by this policy.
why_it_matters: If the loan leg were structured as a non-margin secured facility, the lender's enforcement sale on default would be a Permitted Dealing available at any time, including in a closed period, without prior notification or clearance, subject only to the general insider trading prohibition.

clause: Financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company’s securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: The definition is venue-neutral and covers third-party-issued instruments, so an OTC put/call written by a bank falls squarely within the banned category regardless of being off-exchange.

clause: Designated Persons may enter into or acquire such other types of loan arrangements or instruments, but only after first notifying the Chairman of their intention to do so and disclosing the terms of such loan arrangements or instruments.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on vested REIT Units for a funded collar is not banned outright (only 'margin lending arrangements' are), but the Designated Person must pre-notify the Chairman and disclose the loan's terms, and should confirm with the Company Secretary that the facility is not in substance a margin loan.

clause: Additionally, the REIT may publicly disclose any Derivative positions over REIT Units taken out by a director of the REIT.
why_it_matters: A director's collar position may be publicly disclosed by the REIT at its discretion, a confidentiality consideration for the executive and the bank when structuring the trade.

topic: margin lender forced sale not excluded from blackout
clause: a disposal of REIT Units that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A secured (non-margin) lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the blackout restriction, but this carve-out is unavailable if the facility is characterised as margin lending, so the loan should be structured and documented as a non-margin secured facility to preserve the bank's ability to enforce during a closed period.

clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)
why_it_matters: The Policy expressly names 'collars' as a type of Derivative, so an equity collar is squarely subject to the section 3.5 vesting-state restrictions and, for Designated Persons, the notification and approval procedure.

topic: blanket security/margin ban with no carve-out
clause: must not grant security or enter into margin lending arrangements against Company securities held
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, there is no carve-out for non-margin secured financing; granting any security interest over the shares (the loan leg of a funded collar) is banned outright for Directors, staff and their associates, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route available for this restriction.

topic: no general preclearance outside closed periods
clause: Directors (other than the Chairman) and staff may seek prior written permission to deal in the Company’s securities during the Closed Periods from the Chairman, but only in exceptional circumstances
why_it_matters: Outside Closed Periods there is no general preclearance or notification-before-trading requirement (only the post-trade disclosure duty in section F), so dealing in the derivative legs of a collar outside a Closed Period, absent material non-public information, is not gated by a formal approval process under this policy.

clause: Directors and staff must not deal in the Company’s securities in the following circumstances: ... For short term trading or speculative purposes and must not grant security or enter into margin lending arrangements against Company securities held.
why_it_matters: The policy never mentions derivatives, options, swaps, CFDs or hedging, so whether entering an OTC put/call is a 'dealing' subject to the Closed Period and inside-information prohibitions is untested; this should be confirmed with the Company Secretary before relying on the policy's silence.

clause: If their trading activity materially conflicts with the Company’s trading activity.
why_it_matters: As a listed investment company, AUI's own trading book could create a distinct conflict-of-interest constraint if the collar counterparty bank trades the same securities AUI holds.
