clause: the Access Person or Director is required to make a quarterly certification to confirm that in the event of a margin call during a Blackout Period, sufficient available cash or other acceptable collateral is available to meet any margin calls to provide reasonable assurance that a sale of MFG Securities would be prevented.
why_it_matters: If the collar's financing were treated as a margin loan, the executive would need to certify quarterly that a margin call during a blackout period would not force liquidation, effectively requiring a cash or collateral buffer beyond the collared shares.

clause: 'MFG Securities' means any shares, options and any other securities issued by MFG, as well as any other financial products issued or created over MFG Securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call written by a bank is itself an 'MFG Security' by this definition, so entering it is a Trade requiring pre-clearance and blackout compliance in its own right, quite apart from the section 3.3 ban on using it to limit economic risk of the shareholding.

clause: with an employee, individual or agent of a broker/dealer with whom the Group conducts business
why_it_matters: If the bank writing the collar is a broker/dealer with which the Magellan Group conducts business, transacting with its personnel may itself be a separately prohibited counterparty under 3.3.

topic: MFG Board approval gates margin loans
clause: Margin lending of MFG Securities by Access Persons or Directors is prohibited except in exceptional circumstances that are acceptable to and have been approved by the MFG Board.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if treated as margin lending, requires the MFG Board itself (not just the CCO) to approve it as an exceptional circumstance before the CCO can consent to the associated Trade.

clause: DBI will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A funded collar structured to avoid the words 'hedging' or 'margin lending' will still be assessed on its economic substance, so documentation choices are unlikely to avoid the express restrictions.

clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: The bank should build in execution risk: approval to deal can be revoked without reasons at any time before the trade completes, and the executive cannot disclose that a refusal or revocation occurred.

topic: margin lending ban with no carve-out
clause: Employees are prohibited from entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of DBI securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, there is no Board approval process or exceptional-circumstances carve-out for margin lending, and non-margin secured financing is not separately addressed, so the loan leg sits in an unaddressed grey zone that the Company Secretary should confirm is not caught by this ban before proceeding.

clause: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding DBI securities.
why_it_matters: This definition is broad enough to catch a collar's combined put/call position regardless of how it is documented, so the vesting-state restrictions in 3.6 govern the derivative legs directly.

topic: derivatives ban has no clearance route
clause: Designated Persons must not trade in the Company's derivatives.
why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary share dealing (which can be cleared by the Chairperson), this clause is a standalone, unqualified prohibition with no approval mechanism, so an OTC put and call collar cannot be cleared under this policy at all.

clause: Before any Designated Person deals in securities of the Company (at any time), they must first obtain approval from the Chairperson. ... This obligation operates at all times.
why_it_matters: Even outside the annual closed period, any purchase, sale, unwind or physical settlement of a collar's share leg needs fresh Chairperson approval and a written no-inside-information statement each time.

clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance or minimum shareholding requirements.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not expressly banned, but granting security over the shares to the bank is not addressed either, leaving real uncertainty over whether it would be treated as a 'dealing' requiring Chairperson approval and, if effected during the annual closed period, a breach.

clause: If approval is given, the Designated Person may ordinarily trade within five business days after receiving the approval. ... A further application will need to be made if no dealing takes place within the five business days.
why_it_matters: Any cleared step of a collar (e.g. entry or unwind, to the extent not itself blocked by the derivatives ban) must be executed within a short window or re-cleared, complicating multi-leg execution with a bank counterparty.

topic: margin lending consent applies even inside a window
clause: This procedure applies even if the request for consent is made during a trading window.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if it looks like a margin loan capable of triggering a forced sale, cannot simply be timed into an open trading window; it needs the separate exceptional-circumstances consent that is rarely granted.

topic: risk limiting products sweep unvested and locked shares
clause: designated personnel must not engage in transactions or arrangements in risk limiting products which operate to limit the economic risk of unvested entitlements to EVENT securities ... or vested EVENT securities that are subject to a holding lock or other disposal restriction.
why_it_matters: A collar can only be considered over vested, unrestricted EVT shares; performance rights, unvested options and plan shares still subject to a holding lock cannot be collared at all, with no consent override.

clause: Designated personnel must not conduct any dealings or enter into transactions during a trading window until acknowledgement has been received for the notification.
why_it_matters: Even within an open window, the derivative legs of a collar cannot be executed until written acknowledgement of the notification is received, adding a timing dependency to any bank execution schedule.

topic: no defined secured financing concept beyond margin loans
clause: The policy prohibits margin loan arrangements which could result in a forced sale of EVENT securities.
why_it_matters: Because only margin lending (not secured financing generally) is named, a loan structured to avoid the specific features of a 'margin loan' resulting in forced sale may arguably sit outside this restriction, though it would likely still be treated as such in substance by the Company Secretary.

clause: Margin Loan means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.
why_it_matters: Combined with the outright ban on using Company Securities as security for 'a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement' (6.3(b)), this generic definition extends beyond broker margin loans to catch any bank loan secured against the collared shares, so the funded leg of a collar is banned outright with no clearance path.

clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)
why_it_matters: The policy expressly contemplates 'collars' as a derivative instrument, confirming a purchased put/written call structure is squarely within scope of the derivatives/hedging restrictions rather than an interpretive stretch.

clause: an Employee may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).
why_it_matters: Even the hardship/court-order exception route only ever permits a sale or transfer during a Black-out Period, not entry into a new derivative or financing arrangement, so a collar cannot be established, and its loan cannot be secured, under this exception.

clause: A consultant or contractor (who is not an Employee) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.
why_it_matters: This narrow, unlikely-to-apply tier escapes the Black-out Period, approval and margin loan restrictions altogether, but a director or senior executive holding vested equity would not typically qualify.

clause: where the Flight Centre Securities subject to such arrangements represent 5% or more of Flight Centre's issued capital.
why_it_matters: A funded collar over less than 5% of Flight Centre's issued capital escapes even the notification duty for margin lending, encumbrance and hedging; above that threshold it triggers mandatory immediate notification to the Company Secretary, who informs the Board, but this is disclosure only, not a veto.

topic: vesting-based ban targets directors and executives specifically
clause: Directors, Senior Executives and Closely Connected Persons are prohibited from entering into margin loans, hedging or any other arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk in relation to an element of their remuneration that: i. has not vested ... or ii. has vested ... but remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: The very population a bank would target for a funded collar faces an absolute, non-waivable ban on both the loan and hedge legs until the shares are both vested and free of any holding lock.

topic: no general pre-clearance once vested and unrestricted
clause: Restricted Persons may only Deal in Flight Centre Securities during Trading Windows
why_it_matters: Once vested and unrestricted, a Director or Senior Executive can enter derivative or financing arrangements within an open Trading Window without needing case-by-case prior approval, only the 5% notification duty if applicable - comparatively permissive relative to policies requiring approval for every dealing.

topic: outside-window approval covers any dealing, not just disposals
clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from trading in Flight Centre Securities at times outside the Trading Windows, unless otherwise approved by the Company Secretary in exceptional circumstances.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that limit out-of-window relief to sales, this approval (7-day validity) could in principle extend to entering a collar or its financing outside a window, provided exceptional circumstances and no inside information.

topic: forced-sale exception conditioned on prior consent
clause: an involuntary disposal of HMC Capital Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale under a properly consented loan is excused from the Blackout Period ban; but if the loan itself was never cleared under section 8.1, the forced-sale exception is unavailable and the enforcement sale would breach the policy - so obtaining upfront consent for the loan is essential to preserve the bank's enforcement rights.

topic: consent can be conditioned on margin-call sale terms
clause: A Group Entity may, at its discretion, make any consent granted under section 8.1 conditional upon such terms and conditions that the relevant Group Entity sees fit (for example, specifying the circumstances in which HMC Capital Group Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement mechanics for a funded collar could be pre-negotiated and built into the consent itself, giving more structuring flexibility than a blanket-ban policy would allow.

clause: Any Employee who holds HMC Capital Group Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to Trade in the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities during that time.
why_it_matters: Units under ASX escrow or a voluntary lock-up cannot be collared or pledged at all, regardless of vesting state, until the escrow period ends.

topic: pre-approval required at all times, not just in closed periods
clause: When permitted to Trade in accordance with this Policy, or where Trading is proposed during a Blackout Period, all Directors and Employees must give a prior written request for pre-approval to the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary of any proposed Trading
why_it_matters: Unlike open-window-only policies, every leg of a collar (entry, unwind, or roll) needs individual case-by-case pre-approval regardless of the Blackout Period calendar, adding execution friction and a 5-trading-day validity window to each step.

clause: Directors and Employees are only permitted to buy a derivative position ... however not a contract to sell a put or a call option.
why_it_matters: The written-call leg of any collar cannot be granted by the executive under this Policy, which permits only long derivative positions; only the purchased-put leg is capable of being structured.

clause: The intention of this Policy is that it only permits hedging arrangements which are within the control of the Director or Employee rather than conferring control of any purchase or sale decision to a third party.
why_it_matters: Even a compliant long put must leave exercise/pricing decisions with the executive, not the bank counterparty, which may constrain how the bank structures settlement mechanics.

topic: no equity plan or vesting provisions
clause: The Policy contains no reference to unvested securities, performance hurdles, employee equity incentive schemes or a minimum shareholding requirement.
why_it_matters: There is no vesting-based restriction on the shares to be collared, so the analysis turns entirely on the general dealing, hedging and short-term trading rules rather than any plan-specific lock-up.

clause: The Board of Directors will decide whether disclosure is required in relation to margin loans taken by Director/s. ... in certain circumstances the existence of 'margin loans' or similar arrangements financing securities holdings may constitute material price sensitive information.
why_it_matters: A Director-level loan secured on the collared shares may trigger a Board assessment of whether the financing itself must be announced to the ASX.

clause: If such a sale occurs during a Trading Blackout period, the Chairman will consider whether a breach of this policy has been made after considering all circumstances.
why_it_matters: Enforcement of the bank's security over the collared shares during a blackout is not automatically excused; it is reviewed case by case for breach, creating execution uncertainty for the lender.

clause: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement ... a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is an express, automatic exception, available at any time including in a Closed Period, without needing separate clearance.

clause: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the company's securities unless Board approval is obtained, such approval not to be withheld unreasonably.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of the collar, secured over the collared shares, needs upfront Board approval, but the Board cannot unreasonably refuse it, giving a workable (if not guaranteed) path.

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: If the collared shares (or the call exercise/put exercise settlement) exceed these thresholds, the unwind must be pre-discussed with the Board and legal advisers and documented before execution, adding a process step beyond ordinary approval.

clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
why_it_matters: If the shares to be collared are being funded via a cashless option exercise, that funding sale must occur outside Closed Periods, which can constrain timing of when the collared parcel becomes available.

clause: Directors, KMP and Employees must not trade in Perpetual Securities in a Personal Capacity ... as part of a hedging arrangement aimed at limiting the economic risk of holding Perpetual Securities or at limiting exposure in relation to "at risk" remuneration.
why_it_matters: A purchased put and written call is precisely a hedging arrangement limiting economic risk, so both legs of the collar's option structure are prohibited outright with no clearance, Board or hardship override.

clause: Directors, KMP and Employees must not enter into or otherwise facilitate margin loans over Perpetual Securities in a Personal Capacity.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares cannot be structured as, or to facilitate, a margin loan; unlike some peer policies there is no Board-approval carve-out for this prohibition.

clause: They must not structure arrangements or procure third parties to trade to circumvent the operation of this policy.
why_it_matters: Restructuring the collar or loan through a bank counterparty or wrapper to avoid the literal terms 'hedge' or 'margin loan' would still breach the policy's anti-avoidance clause.

clause: For the avoidance of doubt, this policy applies globally. ... Employees of some Controlled Entities outside of Australia must ensure compliance with any additional clearance requirements or restrictions that apply to owning or trading in Perpetual Securities under the entity's Pre-trade Compliance Systems.
why_it_matters: Offshore-based executives may face additional local restrictions layered on top of the absolute hedging and margin-loan bans.

topic: substantive terms sit in an unattached Group Policy
clause: RE Services staff are included in the definition of Employees for the purposes of the Group Policy – Personal Trading in non-Perpetual Securities ... (a) Prohibition of Insider Trading (b) Prohibition on procuring or encouraging third parties to trade (c) Conflicts of interest (d) High volume personal trading. Under the Group Policy, RE Services staff are not included in the definition of Restricted Employees.
why_it_matters: This document does not itself contain any derivatives, hedging, margin lending or secured financing rules; those (if any) would be in the referenced Group Policy or the separate Group Policy – Personal Trading in Perpetual Securities, neither of which is in evidence, so a collar verdict cannot be given with confidence from this document alone.

clause: Approval granted pursuant to this Policy is valid for that business day only. Where the RE Services staff member has failed to act on that approval, a new approval must be sought to trade on another business day.
why_it_matters: Any dealing approved under this Policy (e.g. entering a put/call leg) must execute the same business day it is approved, which is a tight window for coordinating a bank-structured collar and loan drawdown.

clause: Redemptions: Position must be held for at least three months.
why_it_matters: As MXT is a unit trust, exit is via redemption rather than on-market sale; this minimum hold constrains the earliest point at which a collared position could be unwound by redemption.

clause: Securities ... includes ... derivatives (including forward contracts, swaps, warrants, futures, caps and collars and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the securities)
why_it_matters: The policy's own Securities definition expressly names 'collars' as a derivative that limits economic risk, so the exact structure the bank would offer is captured by name and squarely triggers the section 8.2 hedging prohibition.

topic: encumbrance ban vs conditional margin loan approval
clause: Granting any form of security over any Company Securities. ... Entering into margin lending arrangements involving Company Securities (for Designated Persons) without prior approval.
why_it_matters: There is an internal tension: margin lending may be approved for Designated Persons, but granting security over the shares - which a margin loan or the bank's loan would typically require - is separately and absolutely banned with no stated exception, so it is unclear how any approved loan could actually be secured on the shares.

clause: Arrangements that enable a person to profit from a decrease in the market price of Company Securities.
why_it_matters: Independently of the hedging and short-selling bans, this separately catches the purchased-put leg of a collar even if it were not characterised as 'hedging'.

clause: If Virgin Australia makes a material change to this trading policy, the amended trading policy will be provided to the ASX for release to the market within five business days of the material changes taking effect.
why_it_matters: Any bespoke carve-out negotiated to permit a collar program would require a material policy amendment that must be publicly released to the ASX within five business days, so it cannot be arranged confidentially.

clause: Any hedging of unvested equity will result in immediate forfeiture.
why_it_matters: A collar written over unvested entitlements does not merely breach policy, it triggers automatic loss of the underlying award, so the collar can only be structured over already-vested shares.

clause: If a member of KMP enters into a margin lending arrangement involving Company shares or otherwise encumbers Company shares (“Security Arrangement”), then the member of KMP must provide details of the Security Arrangement to the Chairman, or the Company Secretary immediately.
why_it_matters: The bank loan secured on the collared shares is not prohibited and does not require prior clearance, only immediate notification after entry (and possible ASX notification if material), making the financing leg comparatively straightforward versus policies that ban secured financing outright.

clause: If shares are to be bought or sold then they should wherever possible be traded on one trading order and not over an extended period of time. This is intended to indicate the trade is an investment decision and not a speculative one.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar and any unwind as discrete, single-order transactions helps avoid characterisation as short-term or speculative dealing.

clause: Any permission to deal in Macmahon shares should specify how long that clearance will last.
why_it_matters: The executive should ensure the clearance granted for collar execution states a validity window wide enough to complete pricing and documentation with the bank.

topic: margin lending vs other secured funding
clause: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company’s Securities... This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company’s Securities may be included as security.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is not a 'margin lending arrangement' and is expressly carved out of the only financing prohibition in the policy, but the executive should have the Company Secretary confirm the classification before entering the facility.

topic: financial products dealing restricted to permitted types
clause: deal at any time in Financial Products associated with the Company’s Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs of the collar are Financial Products, so they can only be entered as a dealing that fits the standard notification/confirmation process or a Part 5 exception, not as an unrestricted OTC trade even outside a Prohibited Period.

topic: hedging ban extends to holding-locked vested shares
clause: has vested but remains subject to a holding lock
why_it_matters: Shares that have technically vested but remain under a holding lock are treated the same as unvested shares for hedging purposes, narrowing the pool of shares eligible for the collar to fully unrestricted vested holdings.

topic: lender enforcement carve-out excludes margin loans
clause: a disposal of the Company’s Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement where such agreements are prohibited by this policy
why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security and force-sells the collared shares, that disposal is an excluded dealing outside the confirmation process only because the facility is not classified as margin lending; correct structuring of the loan is therefore load-bearing for exit mechanics.

clause: A confirmation ... expires five days from its date, unless it specifies a different expiry date.
why_it_matters: Collar execution and documentation with the bank must be completed within the five business day clearance window (or a longer window if the Notification Officer specifies one), or fresh clearance must be sought.

topic: dealing definition sweeps in derivatives, hedging, security interests and lending
clause: granting or receiving interests in securities may include but is not limited to directly or indirectly granting, allowing the grant of or becoming entitled to a security interest in or over securities. Lending securities is a form of dealing in securities.
why_it_matters: Both the OTC put/call legs and the grant of security over the collared shares are 'dealing' requiring notice and Company Secretary confirmation like an ordinary share trade, but none of these instruments is separately banned outside the unvested-hedging rule.

clause: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter transactions with securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes offered by the Company.
why_it_matters: A collar over already-vested shares falls outside the express anti-hedging ban, so vested holdings are eligible subject only to the general clearance and Trading Window regime.

topic: forced sale carve-out names margin lending
clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: Enforcement of the bank's security by force-selling the collared shares is expressly excluded from the Trading Window and approval restrictions, giving the bank a clean enforcement path even during a Closed Period.

clause: you are authorised to deal in Company Securities for the 5 business days following the approval date of the Managing Director and/or CEO
why_it_matters: Collar documentation and execution with the bank must be completed within the 5-business-day clearance window unless a longer period is specified.

clause: Restricted Persons should ensure that any securities trading which is prohibited by this Policy is not undertaken by their ... a company or trust over which the Restricted Person has influence or control (regardless of who is the beneficiary)
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the clearance obligation or the anti-hedging ban on unvested entitlements.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a collar structure that literally complies with every rule can still be refused clearance if the Approving Officer judges it would look bad publicly, adding a discretionary reputational filter on top of the mechanical requirements.

clause: Perenti may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with Section 6.2(a) conditional upon such terms and conditions as Perenti sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which Perenti securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: Perenti can constrain when and how the bank may force-sell the collared shares on a margin call or collar trigger, so the loan facility's default/enforcement terms may need Perenti's sign-off, not just the initial financing approval.

topic: hedging of vested unrestricted shares expressly permitted
clause: Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Perenti securities provided that the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Perenti securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications required under Section 5 are made on that basis.
why_it_matters: This is an unusually explicit endorsement of hedging (including, by extension, a collar) once shares are vested and unrestricted, provided it goes through the ordinary approval and notification process like any other trade.

clause: a disposal of Perenti securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement (where that arrangement has been entered into in accordance with this Policy)
why_it_matters: For the bank's enforcement sale to be excluded from blackout-period restrictions, the underlying loan facility must itself have been approved under Section 6.2/Section 5 when it was entered into; an unapproved financing arrangement would not benefit from this carve-out.

clause: if clearance to deal is refused, the Restricted Persons seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone (other than its Connected Persons where relevant, and the Restricted Persons must ensure that the information is kept confidential).
why_it_matters: If the collar clearance is refused, the executive cannot tell the bank or advisers why, which may complicate renegotiating deal timing or terms.

topic: outright margin loan ban for Directors/Designated Executives
clause: No Director or Designated Executive may enter into a margin loan arrangement in respect of Lend Lease securities.
why_it_matters: If a bank loan secured on the collared shares is characterised as a margin loan arrangement, it is banned outright for this tier with no exemption route stated; the policy's silence on non-margin-loan secured financing leaves the classification of a bespoke collar loan untested.

topic: hedging of vested entitlements confined to prescribed trading periods
clause: Transactions or arrangements must only be entered into during the prescribed trading periods.
why_it_matters: Even where hedging of vested entitlements is permitted with notification, execution is confined to the narrow 6-week windows following results announcements and the AGM (for Directors/Designated Executives) or the Employee closed-period window, materially constraining when the collar can be struck.

clause: The following circumstances are not subject to the trading restrictions in this policy: [superannuation transfers, diversified fund investment, takeover acceptance, pro-rata offers, employee benefit scheme receipt] (no exception for a secured lender exercising enforcement rights is listed).
why_it_matters: Unlike more modern policies, there is no stated exception allowing a lender to force-sell pledged shares outside a trading window, so enforcement of the collar's security outside a window is not clearly protected from breaching the policy.

topic: notification, not formal approval, for ordinary dealing
clause: Directors and Designated Executives should notify the General Counsel or Company Secretary prior to any dealing.
why_it_matters: There is no formal pre-clearance/approval system (with refusal rights, conditions or validity periods) for ordinary trades in this 2010-era policy, only an advisory notification, which may not satisfy a bank's diligence expectations for a company-sanctioned clearance process.

clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not, and must ensure their associates do not, enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Tabcorp securities, or grant lenders any rights over their Tabcorp securities.
why_it_matters: The unqualified ban on granting a lender any rights over Tabcorp securities is not limited to acquisition financing, so it appears to catch a bank's security interest over already-vested, collared shares and blocks the loan leg outright for Directors and Restricted Employees.

clause: Any trading that is the subject of approval must be executed within five business days of the receipt of the written approval (unless the approval is withdrawn).
why_it_matters: Both derivative legs of a cleared collar must be priced and executed within five business days of approval, a tight window for negotiating bank documentation.

clause: If approval is withdrawn or refused, the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: A bank structuring the collar may never be told why clearance was refused, complicating any attempt to restructure around a refusal.

clause: An application for approval to deal in Tabcorp securities may be refused where the applicant is not, or as a result of the proposed dealing will not be, in compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy.
why_it_matters: If exercise of the written call could cause a disposal that breaches the director's or executive's Minimum Shareholding Policy, approval for the collar could be refused up front.

clause: The policy contains no exception permitting a lender's forced sale of securities during a Blackout Period.
why_it_matters: Absent an express carve-out, enforcement or physical settlement by the bank during a Blackout Period is not clearly excused, so unwind mechanics would need to be timed to open windows.

clause: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: A purchased put, and the collar as a whole, squarely fits this definition, so the absolute hedging ban applies to Restricted Persons with no consent or clearance mechanism at all, unlike the margin loan provision.

clause: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured against Company shares is only conditionally restricted and can proceed with the Company's prior consent, potentially subject to conditions on forced-sale triggers, but this cannot cure the outright hedging prohibition on the derivative legs.

clause: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
why_it_matters: Even in hardship, only a sale can be cleared during a prohibited period; delivering or physically settling shares under a collar during a prohibited period would need to fit within this narrow sale-only exception.

clause: The Chairperson must determine, and specify in the written clearance, the maximum duration of the clearance.
why_it_matters: There is no default execution window; the collar's execution timetable (if it were otherwise permitted) would be entirely at the Chairperson's discretion.

clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her 'associated parties' (being immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust) complies with the same respective restrictions as apply to Restricted Persons.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or family company does not escape the hedging ban or margin loan consent requirement.

topic: hedging ban has no waiver route
clause: the Restricted Person must apply to the person specified in section 7 for a waiver from compliance with the provisions in sections 6.5(b) or 6.6(a).
why_it_matters: The exceptional-circumstances waiver mechanism covers only the blackout-period and short-term dealing rules, not the absolute hedging ban in section 6.11, so there is no waiver route at all for a collar structured as a hedge.

clause: where a Restricted Person has been granted approval to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangement (refer section 6.11), an involuntary disposal of securities that result from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement.
why_it_matters: If the Chairman (or Board, for the Chairman) approves the loan under 6.11, a subsequent forced sale by the bank on default is expressly excepted from the blackout-period restriction, giving the bank a clean enforcement path once the initial approval is obtained.

topic: Chairman's approval routed to the Board
clause: Chairman of the Board | The Board
why_it_matters: If the Chairman personally wants a funded collar, approval authority for the loan shifts from the Chairman/delegate to the full Board, a materially higher bar than for other Restricted Persons.

clause: Each Restricted Person must ensure that any trading by their Closely Connected Persons are undertaken in accordance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: A collar or secured loan cannot be routed through a spouse, minor child, or family trust/company to avoid the hedging ban or the secured-financing approval requirement.

clause: The policy contains no reference anywhere to margin lending, security interests, charges, liens or other secured financing arrangements.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured against Beach shares is not addressed at all by this Share Trading Policy, so it is neither prohibited nor conditioned by it, though general law and any separate corporate policy could still apply.

topic: hedging ban covers holding-locked vested entitlements
clause: Entering into transactions which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements, such as unvested options or vested entitlements that remain subject to a holding lock, under a Beach equity based executive or employee incentive plan.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban extends beyond unvested awards to vested shares still subject to a holding lock, so a collar can only be written once shares are both vested and released from any holding lock.

clause: Where the dealing would be regarded as 'short term dealing';
why_it_matters: No holding period or months threshold is defined, creating uncertainty over how soon after vesting a multi-month collar (or its unwind) could be entered without being characterised as short-term dealing.

clause: The prohibition may not be generally advised to Beach People to protect confidentiality so a Beach Person wanting to deal in Beach securities may not be told why or for how long the prohibition will last.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed CEO-imposed blackout could block entry, unwind or settlement of a collar at any time without warning or explanation.

clause: Any dealing in Beach securities must occur within five business days after notification (or permission being granted for a Designated Person) and must be consistent with the notification.
why_it_matters: Both collar legs must be priced and executed within five business days of notification or approval, a tight window for arranging bank documentation.

clause: Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders shall not in respect of Company Securities engage in transactions in derivatives in respect of Company Securities (such as put and call options), or any other hedging or equity monetization transaction in which the individual's economic interest and risk exposure in Company Securities is changed (such as collars or forward sales contracts).
why_it_matters: This is an outright, unconditional ban on the exact structure proposed — a collar is named verbatim — with no exceptional-circumstances or approval route available anywhere in the policy, unlike blackout-period trading, margin lending or short-term dealing, each of which can be approved.

clause: Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders must not engage in any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities without prior approval of the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Executive Chairman.
why_it_matters: The loan secured on the collared shares could in principle be approved, but this approval cannot cure the absolute ban on the derivative legs, so the funded collar as a package cannot proceed even though its financing component is only conditionally restricted.

clause: the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Executive Chairman may provide written clearance to a Reporting Insider or Designated Insider to trade in Company Securities during a regular blackout period
why_it_matters: This waiver mechanism is expressly limited to trading during a blackout period; it has no application to the Anti-Hedging Restrictions, confirming there is no back door for a collar even in hardship or court-ordered circumstances.

clause: any other instrument, agreement or understanding that affects, directly or indirectly, a person's economic interest in a security of the Company
why_it_matters: The definition is broad enough to capture almost any synthetic or economic-exposure structure, reinforcing that a funded collar cannot be engineered around the express derivatives/hedging ban by re-labelling it.

clause: If the Executive Chairman wishes to engage in any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, he must first submit a pre-clearing request to the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Lead Director.
why_it_matters: If the collar's loan leg were sought by the Executive Chairman specifically, approval routes to the Lead Director instead of the Executive Chairman approving himself.

clause: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Tamboran securities (or Tamboran products in the derivatives markets) ... includes ... operate to limit the economic risk of any Tamboran Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) ... or otherwise enable a Tamboran Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call over vested, unrestricted shares squarely falls within 'protection arrangements' and is permitted only with prior consent under 1.6; over unvested or holding-locked shares it is banned outright.

clause: a disposal of Tamboran securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of collared shares under the loan security is an exempted dealing that Tamboran Persons may make at any time, including during a Blackout Period, subject only to advising the Authorising Officer per 1.12(b) — a clean lender remedy.

topic: granting security ban on unvested/locked shares
clause: Tamboran Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Tamboran Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities.
why_it_matters: The bank's loan cannot be secured on shares before vesting or while subject to a holding lock, so the funded collar can only be structured over vested, unrestricted shares.

topic: consent for security/margin over vested shares
clause: Unless paragraph (a) applies, Tamboran Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities, with consent under paragraph 1.6.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of the collar, secured on vested unrestricted shares, is permitted but needs prior written consent from the relevant Authorising Officer, the same as the derivative legs.

clause: The policy uses 'buy or sell', 'trade' and 'deal in' without one omnibus defined term for 'Dealing' (contrast a typical Attachment-style definition).
why_it_matters: Activities are expressly and separately named (protection arrangements at 1.10, security/margin lending at 1.11) rather than swept in by a broad dealing definition, which reduces ambiguity about whether a bespoke OTC collar or its financing leg is caught — both are caught expressly.

clause: for the purposes of section (d) only, a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child ... a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to in sub-paragraph (i)
why_it_matters: The associate extension is literally limited to 'section (d)' (the Directors and Senior Management definition); a bank should not rely on this apparent gap to route a collar or loan through an associate's account, as the Company would likely treat it as caught regardless.

clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officer, has discretion to approve dealings in Tamboran securities during a Blackout Period, or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
why_it_matters: Entry into or unwind of a collar during a Blackout Period is not a right but could be approved case-by-case for hardship or court order, via email, at the Board's absolute discretion.

clause: Secured Lending Arrangement means any arrangement involving the use of Company Securities as collateral or security for any indebtedness or other obligation, including without limitation a margin lending or other secured arrangement.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is squarely a Secured Lending Arrangement, triggering clause 7 approval for a GLT/Finance Team member and clause 6.2/6.3 approval for anyone else.

clause: Global Leadership Team and Finance Team members are expected to have sufficient resources to meet a margin call by any means other than the sale of Company Securities ... they must take immediate steps to rearrange their affairs to prevent this from occurring.
why_it_matters: The Company expects the loan (and by extension the collar's financing leg) to be structured with enough headroom that a margin call never forces a sale of the collared shares, which should inform the LVR/put strike chosen.

clause: The Company may publicly disclose the terms and nature of any margin loan or Secured Lending Arrangement to which a Company director is a party, and the terms and circumstances of any call made or likely to be made under those arrangements.
why_it_matters: A director's funded collar could be publicly disclosed by the Company at its own discretion, including its loan-to-value ratio and any margin call, independent of the director's own ASX notification obligations.

clause: Persons to whom this policy applies must not sell more than 2% of the total issued share capital worth of securities in any 6 month period without obtaining approval from the Chairman ... as to the form and timing of the sale and the management of its public disclosure.
why_it_matters: Unwind or settlement of a large collar involving delivery/sale of more than 2% of issued capital in a 6-month window needs separate Chairman/Board sign-off on timing and disclosure, on top of ordinary Trading Window and Secured Lending clearance.

clause: Any approval given may be revoked in writing, prior to the Dealing taking place, if ... new information comes to light in relation to the Secured Lending Arrangement ... or any other relevant event or circumstance, as determined by the Board.
why_it_matters: Approval to enter the collar's loan leg is not final until the dealing occurs and can be pulled by the Board on a broad discretionary trigger.

clause: If a person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving an approval to Deal, they must not Deal despite having received the approval.
why_it_matters: Execution of a cleared collar (or its unwind) must be re-checked against Inside Information at the moment of trade, not just at the time approval was granted.

clause: Approval will only be given under exceptional circumstances where the Dealing would occur in the period between 30 June and the announcement to ASX of final results for the year and between 31 December and the announcement to ASX of the interim results for the half-year.
why_it_matters: Collar entry, unwind or roll timed in the weeks immediately before annual or half-year results faces a materially harder approval bar than an ordinary Closed Period dealing.

clause: Derivatives include: (a) derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and (b) any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: The policy's own definition of Derivatives expressly names 'collars', so a funded equity collar's put and call legs are squarely and expressly caught, not merely swept in by inference.

clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: There is no clearance route, vesting-state carve-out, or exemption for this ban - the loan leg of a bank-funded collar cannot be implemented for any Designated Person, regardless of whether the shares are vested and unrestricted.

clause: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments ... Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.
why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar could in principle be executed over vested, unrestricted shares with standard clearance, even though the financing leg cannot be implemented at all - the two legs face fundamentally different treatment.

clause: In exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).
why_it_matters: Even the Black-out Period override is limited to disposals/transfers for hardship or court order, so it could permit unwinding an existing collar position during a black-out but not entering into new derivative legs or a financing arrangement.

clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period ... the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: Execution of a collar's derivative legs straddling the start of a Black-out Period is time-limited and cannot be adjusted once the black-out commences.

clause: An employee, consultant or contractor (who is not a Designated Person) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.
why_it_matters: Black-out Periods, the clause 5 approval regime, and the clause 6.3 margin loan ban are all expressed to apply only to Designated Persons; the policy is silent on secured financing by a non-Designated employee, though this is an unlikely profile for a bank collar counterparty.

clause: Securities include securities of any kind including ordinary shares, preference shares, debentures, convertible notes, options and hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call sold by a bank are expressly 'Securities' under this definition, so the collar's derivative legs are directly and expressly regulated by the Policy, not merely inferred.

clause: Directors must obtain the Board's approval before entering into a margin loan or similar arrangements concerning Securities.
why_it_matters: A director may enter the collar's loan leg (secured on the collared shares) with prior Board approval - there is no outright prohibition, unlike some peer policies, but the process is Board-level, not a single officer's sign-off.

clause: for more than $50,000 worth of Securities to any party if written approval from the Chairman is not obtained, covering the form of and timing of the sale, and the management of its public disclosure, before entering into discussions for the potential sale of those Securities.
why_it_matters: Any collar-sized position (almost certainly over $50,000) triggers a separate Chairman approval covering timing, form and public disclosure management, before even entering into sale discussions - relevant to structuring the written call and any unwind.

topic: Management Team can never trade freely
clause: A member of the Management Team may not Trade at any time, including during a Trading Window, unless they obtain prior written approval from ... the Chairman
why_it_matters: A likely collar counterparty (director, CEO or CFO) needs the Chairman's prior written approval for every trade, including inside a Trading Window, so entry, adjustment and unwind of both collar legs each require individual sign-off.

topic: public disclosure of margin loan terms
clause: Where a Director has entered into margin loan or similar funding arrangements for a material number of Securities, the Company may need to disclose the key terms of the arrangements, including the number of Securities involved, the trigger points, the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and any other material details.
why_it_matters: If the collar's financing leg is material, the Company may be required to publicly disclose its size, trigger points and the bank's unilateral sale rights.

clause: disposals by a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under an approved margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is an Excluded Trade, so it is not blocked by a Prohibited Period and needs no fresh Chairman/Board approval - a clean lender remedy, provided the original margin loan was itself approved.

clause: The policy makes no reference anywhere to 'unvested', 'vesting' or a 'holding lock'.
why_it_matters: Unlike several peer policies, MGH does not separately restrict hedging, derivatives or margin loans over unvested equity incentives; the general Trade/Trading Window/Management Team approval regime is the only gate, aside from the Excluded Trading carve-out (f) that blocks selling securities obtained on exercise until the relevant exercise date has passed.

clause: Relevant Persons may not deal in the Company's securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is banned if characterised as a 'margin lending arrangement'; the term is undefined, so whether a bespoke bilateral loan secured on the collared shares escapes the ban is untested and should be cleared with the Chair/CEO before proceeding.

clause: subject to paragraph 3.4, a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: This exclusion removes a lender's enforcement sale from the blackout and approval requirements in 3.2 and 3.3, but only 'subject to paragraph 3.4', so it does not rescue a financing arrangement that is itself a prohibited margin loan.

clause: Hedging includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities.
why_it_matters: A purchased put and written call collar squarely fits this definition; it is permitted with clearance only over vested and unrestricted shares, and never over unvested or holding-locked vested shares.

clause: If a waiver is granted... the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 2 business days.
why_it_matters: A collar entered under an exceptional-circumstances waiver during a blackout period must be fully executed within 2 business days, a tight window for documenting a bank collar and loan.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could my proposed transaction be perceived by the market as me (or my Connected Persons) taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way?
why_it_matters: Even a formally compliant collar must be self-assessed for negative market perception, and any concerns must be flagged in the approval request, giving the approver discretion to refuse or condition clearance.

clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg in its annual report or to ASX).
why_it_matters: The bank and executive should expect the collar's existence and terms could be publicly disclosed by the Company in its annual report or to ASX.

clause: a company or any other entity which the Employee has an ability to control.
why_it_matters: Routing the loan or collar through a controlled entity or trust does not avoid the Policy's approval requirements or the margin lending ban, since Connected Persons' dealings are treated as the Employee's own.

clause: The trading restrictions set out in this policy are additional to any provisions governing or restricting the trading of securities set out in any agreement between Bega Cheese and a Designated Person or a Securityholder or any provisions in Bega Cheese's employee share plans... the most restrictive provisions will prevail.
why_it_matters: Even where this Policy permits or is silent on a collar or loan structure, the executive's individual equity plan rules or other agreements may impose stricter hedging or encumbrance restrictions that override this Policy and must be separately checked.

clause: A Designated Person is prohibited from entering into margin lending and other secured financing arrangements when purchasing or selling Bega Cheese securities.
why_it_matters: The ban is framed around financing 'when purchasing or selling'; a loan secured on already-vested shares with no contemporaneous purchase or sale of Bega Cheese securities arguably falls outside the literal wording, but this gap should be confirmed with the Relevant Officer rather than assumed.

clause: Any clearance to trade can be given or refused by Bega Cheese at its discretion, without giving reasons... the refusal must be kept confidential and not disclosed to anyone.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on any right to clearance; approval is wholly discretionary, reasons for refusal will not be given, and a granted clearance can be withdrawn before execution if circumstances change.

clause: A clearance to trade can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar could lose its clearance before execution within the 14-day window, so the collar should be documented and executed promptly after approval.

clause: Bega Cheese may blacklist certain securities in relation to particular Designated Personnel... that Designated Person must not deal in the Blacklisted Securities for the time period specified in the notice.
why_it_matters: If the collar references, or the executive also holds, securities of another entity connected to Bega Cheese's dealings, a blacklist notice could independently block that leg of the structure.

clause: dealing by Designated Personnel in Bega Cheese's securities may take place only during the following periods... (collectively the Trading Windows).
why_it_matters: Absent an exceptional-circumstances clearance, the collar's entry, unwind or roll may only occur within the three 30-day Trading Windows each year (post half-year results, post full-year results, post AGM).

clause: This Policy contains no clause prohibiting hedging of Company securities, margin lending, or secured financing arrangements generally.
why_it_matters: There is no express bar on granting security over vested Premier shares to fund a collar loan; the only relevant control is that a secured lender's forced sale during a Closed Period requires the Board to exercise its discretion to lift the restriction (clause 4.1(f)).

clause: Where the provisions of an agreement between Premier and a Shareholder conflict with the provisions of this policy, the most restrictive provisions will prevail.
why_it_matters: Any separate restriction in the executive's employee share plan or personal agreement with Premier overrides this Policy if stricter, so those documents must be checked before relying on the absence of an express hedging or margin-lending ban here.

clause: If I am purchasing securities, I do not intend to sell the securities within 6 months of the date of purchase.
why_it_matters: This representation on the standard dealing forms is a de facto 6-month restriction on new purchases (longer than the usual 3-month rule), but it does not restrict hedging, encumbering or selling already-held vested shares.

clause: they may notify the Company Secretary of their intention to deal in the Company's securities
why_it_matters: Routine dealing outside Prohibited Periods proceeds by notice, not a refusable approval, so a KMP without inside information has a comparatively low-friction path to executing a collar within a window period.

clause: a disposal of Premier's securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan agreement
why_it_matters: This clause tacitly acknowledges that a KMP may grant security over Premier shares under a loan agreement; a bank's enforcement sale on default is contemplated by the Policy, subject to the Board exercising discretion to permit that sale if it falls within a Closed Period.

clause: Without limiting any other provision of this policy, a Restricted Person must not enter into any Dealing or arrangement that provides lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities without first obtaining the prior written consent of the Designated Officer.
why_it_matters: This is the operative gate for the funded collar's loan leg: granting the bank security over the collared shares is expressly permitted, but only with the Designated Officer's (the Chairman's, or the Company Secretary's if the executive is the Chairman) prior written consent -- there is no blanket ban on secured financing as seen in many peer policies.

topic: hedging and scrip lending are express Dealings
clause: Deal or Dealing means buying or selling a Security holding in the Company or entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement which involves a Security holding in the Company.
why_it_matters: A collar (a hedging arrangement) and a margin loan are both expressly named as Dealings, so the put/call legs and the loan leg both sit within the ordinary clearance and Closed Period framework rather than a separate prohibition.

clause: a Restricted Person must not Deal in the Company's Securities: (a) where the Dealing is of a short-term nature
why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a fixed 3- or 6-month rule, 'short-term nature' is undefined, leaving the Chairman/Designated Officer discretion to treat an early unwind or short-dated collar as prohibited; a longer-dated structure reduces this risk.

clause: a disposal of the Company's Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement (note the rules applicable to Restricted Persons entering into arrangements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities in paragraph 9 of this policy)
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default can proceed during a Closed Period as an Excluded Dealing, but only after a 7-business-day Excluded Dealing Notice to the Designated Officer, who can block it without giving reasons.

clause: Restricted Persons are: (a) All Directors and their spouses and any Related Party; (b) The Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Officers, the Chief Financial Officers of Group Companies; and (c) All Key Management Personnel ... not otherwise mentioned.
why_it_matters: The Policy has no unvested/vested-locked distinction and no equity-plan hedging carve-out, so the same clearance and Closed Period rules apply uniformly to any vested shareholding used to fund a collar.

clause: Designated Persons must not engage in margin lending or other secured financing arrangements over Orora Securities.
why_it_matters: This is a blanket, unconditional ban on the loan leg of a funded collar for Designated Persons (Directors, Senior Executives, all KMP and their Associates), with no clearance route and no carve-out for vested shares.

clause: A disposal of Orora Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights
why_it_matters: This exclusion contemplates a secured lender existing, yet Designated Persons are separately and absolutely banned from entering into any secured financing arrangement in the first place; it may only be relevant to non-Designated Orora Persons or legacy arrangements, and should not be read as reviving the loan leg for Designated Persons.

clause: 'Derivatives' ... includes the following if they relate to or derive value from Orora Securities: ... contracts for difference, spread bets and caps and collars.
why_it_matters: The Policy expressly anticipates a collar structure and treats it as a Derivative/Security, so the put/call legs are squarely Trading requiring notification (Designated Persons) and compliance with Blackout Periods, quite separate from the outright ban on the financing leg.

clause: any hedging over vested Orora Securities must comply with this Policy and, if applicable to that Orora Person, Orora's Minimum Shareholding Policy
why_it_matters: A collar over vested shares subject to an MSR may be restricted or reduced in permitted size by the separate Minimum Shareholding Policy, which is not in this document and must be independently reviewed.

clause: This prohibition against insider trading applies to all Orora Persons at all times, including outside of Blackout Periods and other ad hoc restriction periods, and overrides all other provisions of this Policy, including any consent or approval to trade which may be granted under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Even a Company Secretary/Chairman-approved collar trade cannot proceed, and any purported approval is void, if the executive possesses inside information at the time of execution.

clause: it is unlikely that details of the ad hoc restriction will be communicated to all Orora Persons ... Any such communication is to be treated as confidential.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad hoc restriction can silently block execution or unwind of a collar even outside the scheduled Blackout Periods.

clause: Following the end of each financial year, all Directors and Senior Executives must certify to the Company Secretary that they and their Associates are in compliance with this Policy (or advise of any breaches of this Policy).
why_it_matters: A collar or loan arrangement inconsistent with the Policy would need to be disclosed (or falsely certified) at each annual compliance certification, so any secured financing question should be resolved with the Company Secretary well before that certification falls due.

clause: Centuria Securities: securities of any class, notes, options bonds or any related derivatives issued by the Group.
why_it_matters: Because only Group-issued derivatives are 'Centuria Securities', an OTC put/call written by a bank over an executive's existing vested shares is not itself within the defined dealing universe, so entry into the collar is not expressly regulated.

clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, other secured financing, encumbrance, hedging, short selling, stock lending or CFDs.
why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not prohibited by this policy, but the complete silence also means there is no bank-facing disclosure or consent carve-out to rely on if a dispute arises; general insider-trading and blackout principles would still govern any resulting sale or transfer of the shares.

clause: Procedures for Directors reporting on trading in Centuria Securities ... Directors must immediately report any trades ... The consent requirement in paragraph 12 is addressed only to 'Employees'.
why_it_matters: A Director entering or unwinding a collar outside a blackout period may not need prior Company Secretary/CEO consent at all under this policy, only post-trade notification, easing execution timing (subject to the separate blackout and inside-information bans).

clause: Directors and Employees are not permitted to buy, sell or otherwise trade in Centuria Securities during a "blackout period".
why_it_matters: Entering a cash-settled OTC derivative that does not itself involve buying or selling the underlying shares may fall outside the blackout ban, though delivery, exercise or a forced sale of the physical shares would not.

clause: the sale or disposal of the Centuria Securities is the most reasonable method available to alleviate the exceptional circumstances
why_it_matters: The only blackout carve-out is framed around a sale/disposal for hardship reasons, so it would not obviously extend to establishing a collar or granting security for a loan during a blackout period.

clause: The rules covers shares in the Company, derivatives related to the Company's shares, whether issued by the company or not and to any traded company options.
why_it_matters: This is an express, venue-agnostic sweep that catches an OTC put and call written by a bank ('whether issued by the company or not'), so the collar's derivative legs are within-policy and only need ordinary Chairman clearance and black-out compliance, not a separate carve-out.

topic: unvested hedging ban with vested carve-out
clause: Directors may enter into hedging transactions in respect of the Company securities held by them outside any equity based performance plan or once the securities have been vested.
why_it_matters: The prohibition is confined to unvested plan entitlements; once shares vest, a funded collar over them is expressly not caught by the hedging ban, only by the general approval/black-out regime.

clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance or stock lending.
why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not addressed at all, so it is not prohibited, but the bank also gets no policy-based comfort (e.g. forced-sale carve-out or financing disclosure duty) if the executive defaults during a black-out period.

clause: Directors, employees and contractors must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.
why_it_matters: With no stated holding period, a short-dated or early-unwound collar risks being characterised as short-term trading; tenor and structuring should avoid any appearance of short-term speculation.

clause: The prohibition extends to dealings by anyone, including Directors' and employees' nominees, agents or other associates, such as family members, family trusts and family companies.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a related trust or entity does not avoid the approval process or black-out timing restrictions.

clause: Directors and executives are also excluded from dealing in securities within the period from receipt of the Board Pack and the Directors' Meeting.
why_it_matters: This recurring short blackout window (in addition to the 14-day results and AGM windows) further narrows the calendar available to enter, unwind or roll the collar.

clause: not use derivatives such as caps, collars, warrants or similar products into in relation to any Company securities held by employees.
why_it_matters: The policy names 'collars' specifically as a banned derivative product over Company securities, so a bank-written funded collar (purchased put and written call) is expressly and unconditionally prohibited for Employees and, via the 'additional restrictions' overlay, for Key Management Personnel, with no clearance route available.

clause: not enter into arrangements ... where the lender is granted a right to sell or compel the sale of the securities at a time that this policy prohibits the employee dealing in the securities [Employees item 4] versus a disposal of securities ... that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights ... is specifically excluded from the application of this policy [Scope of the Policy].
why_it_matters: The policy discourages granting a lender forced-sale rights exercisable during a prohibited dealing period, yet separately excludes the lender's actual exercise of such rights from the policy altogether; a bank relying on enforcement should seek company comfort given this internal tension, though it is moot for a collar structure because the hedge leg is independently and absolutely banned.

clause: Will the transaction take place on the ASX (circle): YES/NO. If the transaction is not to take place on the ASX, advise details of the transaction.
why_it_matters: The Key Management Personnel clearance application contemplates off-market/OTC transactions generally, showing the policy anticipates non-exchange dealings, but this administrative accommodation does not override the standalone, unconditional ban on derivative products.

clause: take all reasonable steps to prevent the trading by their spouse, partner, child or other immediate family member, or trust or other entity controlled by them or an investment adviser on behalf of them intends dealing in Imdex securities.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or related entity does not avoid the derivatives ban, since employees must take reasonable steps to prevent associated persons from dealing on their behalf.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: The Company can look through a bank-structured collar's legal form to its economic effect, so labelling a collar as something other than a hedge is unlikely to avoid the hedging ban on unvested or holding-locked securities.

clause: Sections 3.3, 4.1 and 4.3 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the short-term dealing ban, blackout periods and the pre-approval requirement altogether, giving the lender a clean enforcement path even during a closed period.

clause: Selling securities received following the vesting of entitlements under an employee, executive or director equity plan within 3 months of the vesting date is not a short-term dealing.
why_it_matters: Physical settlement or unwind shortly after vesting is not penalised as short-term trading, giving some flexibility on timing for establishing or closing out a collar around a vesting event.

topic: Front Page Test as approval gate
clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Beyond the formal rules, a bank-funded collar could still be refused clearance if it would be perceived as the executive exploiting their position, an additional discretionary hurdle beyond the express criteria.

clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family member or a controlled entity does not avoid the Policy; the Restricted Person remains responsible for ensuring the same clearance and timing rules are met.

company: PM CAPITAL GLOBAL OPPORTUNITIES FUND LIMITED
clause: Derivatives ... includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Company Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
why_it_matters: The definition of 'Derivatives' expressly names 'caps and collars' among the instruments caught by the ban on transactions that limit the direct economic risk of a holding, so a bank-written funded collar is squarely and specifically targeted, not merely swept in generically.

company: PM CAPITAL GLOBAL OPPORTUNITIES FUND LIMITED
clause: The Company Secretary (or their delegate) will generally withhold prior written consent unless special circumstances exist (such as financial hardship or a court order requiring the sale of securities) and the Chair has agreed to the granting of consent.
why_it_matters: The only route to clearance for a collar or margin loan uses the same high bar as hardship sales; an ordinary wealth-management-motivated collar is unlikely to be approved even though the Policy formally permits an application.

company: PM CAPITAL GLOBAL OPPORTUNITIES FUND LIMITED
topic: forced-sale exclusion conditioned on prior consent
clause: A disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement which has been conducted with the prior written consent of the Company Secretary (or their delegate), after consultation with the Chair.
why_it_matters: The forced-sale carve-out only protects a margin lending arrangement that itself had prior written consent; an unconsented loan gets no such protection, so the bank should confirm consent was obtained for the financing leg before relying on an unencumbered enforcement path.

company: PM CAPITAL GLOBAL OPPORTUNITIES FUND LIMITED
clause: Associate means someone that a Restricted Person (the Principal) can be regarded as having investment control or influence over. Such person might include: a family member ...; a nominee ... (including an investment manager managing funds on the Principal's behalf); a trust ...; a person in partnership ...; and a company that the Principal controls.
