why_it_matters: Investment control/influence tests catch nominees, investment managers acting for the Principal, and controlled trusts/companies, so routing the collar or loan through a related vehicle does not escape the Policy.

company: PM CAPITAL GLOBAL OPPORTUNITIES FUND LIMITED
clause: Each trading window opens one hour after the Company announces to the ASX its estimated Net Tangible Assets and closes at the end of the last Trading Day before the day on which the Company announces its next estimated Net Tangible Asset value.
why_it_matters: Because NTA is announced weekly and monthly, the default 'open' trading window is narrow and recurring; even if consent for a collar were obtained, execution timing would still need to fit within these short windows and outside the separate results/DRP/buy-back Blackout Periods.

clause: No person shall purchase or sell or otherwise monetize securities of the Company while in possession of Undisclosed Material Information.
why_it_matters: This is the only clause that plainly reaches an OTC collar (naming 'monetize'), but it only bars entry while the individual holds undisclosed material information; the separate quarterly blackout provision is worded narrower ('purchasing or selling') and does not on its face use the word 'monetize', creating a textual gap for collar entry during the blackout window if no MNPI is held.

clause: The Policy imposes no requirement to seek clearance or give notice before dealing, other than the Chief Executive Officer's written consent needed to deal during a blackout period.
why_it_matters: Outside the quarterly blackout and while free of undisclosed material information, a director or executive can enter, unwind or roll a collar without company approval, which simplifies timing but leaves the bank with no company sign-off trail confirming the trade is compliant.

clause: This Policy covers all written or oral communications and applies to any director, officer or employee of the Company. It also applies to any consultant or contractor (a 'Representative').
why_it_matters: Spouses, trusts and controlled entities are not mentioned, so routing the collar or its security through a related vehicle is not addressed or restricted by the document.

clause: the Company complies with its timely disclosure obligations as required under applicable Canadian securities laws, including the Securities Act (British Columbia)
why_it_matters: The Policy is drafted for a TSX-listed, BCSC-regulated issuer with no reference to ASX Listing Rules or the Australian insider trading regime, so an Australian bank should confirm which regime actually governs the executive's holding before relying on this document alone.

topic: silence on secured financing and derivatives
clause: (No provision addresses margin loans, pledges, encumbrances, derivatives, hedging, short selling, stock lending or CFDs.)
why_it_matters: None of the structural elements of a funded collar (the put, the call, or the loan secured on the shares) is expressly prohibited, permitted or made subject to clearance, so the transaction is not blocked by the Policy but also receives no express safe harbour.

topic: outright hedging ban on held securities
clause: Directors, key management personnel and any other designated Restricted Persons covered under this policy are also prohibited from entering into any transaction to hedge securities held in the Company.
why_it_matters: This is an absolute, non-waivable ban with no clearance route; a purchased put and written call are squarely a hedge of securities held, so a funded collar cannot be structured for directors, KMP or any other designated Restricted Person even with company consent.

clause: Directors, officers and employees of the Company are prohibited from entering into arrangements for the hedging, or otherwise limiting their exposure to risk in relation to unvested shares, options or rights issued or acquired under the Company's employee equity scheme.
why_it_matters: Closes off a collar over unvested equity incentives for the entire workforce, not just Restricted Persons, so vesting must complete before any collar discussion.

clause: a disposal of securities that is a result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example, under a margin loan arrangement [is excluded from the operation of the share trading policy].
why_it_matters: Suggests the loan/security leg of a structure is not itself barred by the trading policy (only the derivative hedge legs are), though enforcement remains subject to general insider trading law and could occur while the executive holds inside information.

clause: clearance may be given for a Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities when they would otherwise be prohibited from doing so
why_it_matters: Even where a closed-period exception is granted for hardship or court order, it only ever permits a sale, so collar legs (a purchased put and a written call) could not be entered under this route during a Closed Period.

clause: the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their respective associated parties trading in Company securities at any time.
why_it_matters: An unscheduled, discretionary embargo could freeze collar entry, unwind or roll at any time, with no stated notice period or confidentiality treatment.

clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that their 'associated parties' ... complies with the same respective restrictions as apply to Restricted Persons
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its security through a spouse, family company or trust does not avoid the hedging ban or Closed Period restrictions.

clause: A clearance to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused without a reason being given. The decision is final and binding. Any clearance refusal or withdrawal must be kept confidential by the person who sought clearance, and may not be disclosed to anyone.
why_it_matters: Even though both collar legs and the loan are only subject to clearance (not an outright ban), the Company Secretary's decision cannot be reasoned, appealed, or discussed once refused, so a bank should plan for the possibility of an unexplained rejection with no recourse.

topic: both collar legs and the loan are separately gated
clause: may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance ... may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved
why_it_matters: The derivative hedge and the secured loan are each independently subject to the same five-business-day clearance, so both must be documented, cleared and executed within that narrow window for the structure to close.

topic: Connected Persons must clear through sponsor
clause: a Connected Person must seek clearance through their EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure prior to trading in Units.
why_it_matters: A family trust or related entity cannot independently apply for clearance to enter the collar or grant security; the application must run through the individual's own EQT/LIT Person channel.

topic: broad insider trading scope across vehicles
clause: For the avoidance of doubt, all forms of insider trading in relation to the Units of any entity or vehicle are prohibited.
why_it_matters: Suggests the Responsible Entity treats economic exposure obtained via any vehicle -- potentially including a bank's OTC derivative book -- as within the insider trading prohibition, reinforcing that clearance and inside-information checks apply regardless of how the collar is structured.

clause: LIT Partners and LIT Persons may trade in a LIT's Units provided ... the trade has been executed in accordance with the LIT Partner's trading policy, procedures and/or controls which have been agreed with the Responsible Entity [yet section 6 separately names LIT Partners as needing the Responsible Entity's own Trading Request Procedure clearance for hedging, margin lending and short-term trading].
why_it_matters: It is unclear whether an external LIT Partner seeking a funded collar over its own LIT Unit holding applies to its own internal compliance function or to the Responsible Entity's Company Secretary; written confirmation of the applicable regime should be obtained before relying on either clearance.

clause: EQT Persons who have knowledge of the buy-back and are involved in the day to day management of the buy-back, are subject to a further Black-out Period commencing from the date the Responsible Entity makes the decision to buy-back the units in a LIT, to the next full business day after the buy-back has been completed.
why_it_matters: An unscheduled buy-back-related blackout for informed EQT Persons could freeze collar entry, unwind or roll for a period whose length tracks the buy-back timetable rather than the standard quarterly/annual calendar.

topic: derivatives named in Closed Period ban
clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in DTL securities (nor trade in financial products issued or created over, or in respect of, DTL securities) during the following Closed Periods
why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar are expressly caught by the Closed Period ban but are otherwise unrestricted outside the two Closed Periods (absent Inside Information), so timing -- not an outright ban -- is the primary constraint on a funded collar.

clause: If a Restricted Person enters into a margin lending arrangement involving DTL shares or otherwise encumbers DTL shares (a "Security Arrangement"), then the Restricted Person must provide details of the Security Arrangement to the Chairman ... immediately.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is not prohibited but triggers an immediate written disclosure obligation, and DTL may separately need to notify the ASX if the number of shares involved is material.

topic: forced sale permitted at any time
clause: A Restricted Person may sell securities at any time where the disposal is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights under a margin lending or similar arrangement.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is expressly permitted even during a Closed or Prohibited Period, giving the lender a clear, policy-sanctioned right to liquidate the collateral regardless of the executive's own trading restrictions at the time.

clause: (the terms 'hedge' and 'hedging' do not appear anywhere in the Policy)
why_it_matters: A collar is analysed purely as 'dealing'/'trading' in DTL securities or financial products over them; the Closed Period and 12-month short-term rules are the operative constraints, not a separate hedging prohibition.

clause: A Restricted Person must immediately notify the Chairman or the Company Secretary in writing if he or she receives a margin call that can only be satisfied by the sale of DTL's securities.
why_it_matters: If the bank's facility has margin-call mechanics rather than being fully secured to a fixed level, any call forcing a sale must be reported immediately even though clearance for the sale itself is not required.

clause: GPG Persons may at any time ... dispose of GPG securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a lender's enforcement sale as a breach, this exemption lets a bank liquidate collateral shares at any time, including during a Blackout Period, provided the underlying secured financing was itself validly entered into (i.e. over vested, unlocked shares with consent).

clause: for the purposes of clause 3 only, a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child ... a close relative, a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to in clause 1(b)(i)
why_it_matters: Natural-person associates (spouse, children, dependants) are only brought within clause 3 (Blackout Periods/notification); the express clause 4 bans on protection arrangements and secured financing/margin lending apply only to the GPG Person and entities they control, so a collar or loan booked in a spouse's own name arguably sits outside clause 4's literal wording, though general insider trading law and the acting-in-concert language would still need to be checked case by case.

clause: a company or trust controlled by any of the persons referred to in clause 1(b)(i) above
why_it_matters: Unlike natural-person associates, a company or trust the executive controls is included in the GPG Person definition without limitation, so routing the collar/loan through a family trust or investment vehicle does not escape clause 4's bans.

clause: GPG may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading ... even where the proposed trade would otherwise take place outside a Blackout Period ... must be kept strictly confidential.
why_it_matters: A scheduled collar entry, roll or unwind date can be blocked by an undisclosed ad hoc restriction with no advance warning and no stated end date.

clause: If an GPG Person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving a clearance to trade, they must not trade despite having received the clearance.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar or financing transaction can become unexecutable if inside information arises between clearance and signing, with no stated re-clearance mechanism.

clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officer has discretion to approve dealings in GPG securities during a Blackout Period ... may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship, or a requirement to comply with a court order.
why_it_matters: Offers a narrow, wholly discretionary and unreviewable route to execute, unwind or settle a collar during a closed period, but cannot be relied upon as a matter of right.

clause: If an GPG Person undertakes any of the actions described in paragraph 5(a), that GPG Person must advise the relevant Authorising Officer.
why_it_matters: Even exempt dealings (e.g. a secured lender's enforcement sale) must still be reported to the Authorising Officer after the event, creating an ongoing disclosure trail for any financing arrangement.

clause: (not addressed anywhere in the policy)
why_it_matters: There is no minimum shareholding requirement to preserve, simplifying sizing of the collar and loan against the full vested, unlocked holding.

topic: margin lending ban is KMP-only and margin-loan-specific
clause: directors, officers and other “Key Management Personnel” ... of the Group are prohibited from using his or her holding in any of the Group's securities as collateral for any margin lending.
why_it_matters: The express prohibition is confined to KMP and to 'margin lending'; other employees and contractors face no express bar on pledging shares, and even for KMP whether a bank's collar-secured loan counts as 'margin lending' (rather than another form of secured financing) is undefined and would need to be tested.

clause: A Key Management Person with security over his or her holding ... in connection with margin lending which is in existence prior to 1 March 2016 will not be in breach ... provided that the Key Management Person notifies the Chairman ... within five business days of becoming aware that his or her margin loan facility ... is subject to a margin call, in material breach, or reaches 90% or above of any applicable loan-to-value ratio.
why_it_matters: Any new collar-secured loan post-dates 1 March 2016 and so cannot rely on this grandfathering; it confirms the general rule is a forward-looking ban on new KMP margin/secured lending against Group shares.

topic: hedging ban tied to vesting/restriction status only
clause: must not enter into a transaction if the transaction effectively operates to hedge or limit the economic risk of securities allocated under the Group's employee incentive plans during the period those securities remain unvested or subject to restrictions under the terms of the plan.
why_it_matters: Once plan securities vest and restrictions lapse, hedging is no longer expressly banned and only ordinary Dealing clearance and Closed Period rules apply, so the collar's put/call legs over vested unrestricted shares are structurally available subject to clearance.

clause: Dealing in securities is a broad concept and covers more than simply buying or selling securities. It extends to exercising options over securities and entering agreements to buy or sell securities.
why_it_matters: Granting a charge or lien is not listed as a form of Dealing, so outside the KMP margin lending clause, pledging shares to secure a loan is not independently regulated by this policy.

clause: A Relevant Person must notify the Company Secretary: before, or immediately after, any buying or selling by them ... of Group securities at any time.
why_it_matters: Entry into, unwind of, or settlement under a collar (to the extent treated as buying or selling) must be notified to the Company Secretary regardless of Closed Period status, creating an ongoing disclosure trail for the bank's structure.
